jobs.title: Brand Strategy Lead, Brand Architecture & Naming
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As a Brand Strategy Lead at Anthropic, you will own brand architecture and naming strategy across the Anthropic and Claude brands. Claude is becoming part of how people work, build, and discover, and how we organize and name what we make shapes how a broad, global audience of enterprise buyers, developers, researchers, policymakers, and the general public understands it and whether they trust it. This is a foundational role: you'll solidify this function at Anthropic, making the routine calls yourself and bringing the biggest decisions to senior leaders with a clear recommendation.

In this role, you'll own all brand architecture and naming strategy work globally, from how the portfolio fits together as it grows to the names we ship, and you'll build the systems, structure, and processes other teams follow. In a single week, you might map part of the portfolio, generate names, and take multiple recommendations to senior leaders. This is a senior individual contributor role, so you'll scope the work yourself and set a roadmap a year out with minimal direction. You'll partner closely with Brand Design, Product and Brand Marketing, Product teams, IP Legal, and Comms to position new offerings and introduce them to the world.

Key responsibilities

• Own all brand architecture strategy across Anthropic and Claude, including how brands, products, models, features, plans, and programs relate to one another

• Lead decisions on where new products, models, features, and programs sit in the portfolio, including when an offering extends an existing brand and when it needs its own, and when something earns a name versus a plain description

• Own the company's global naming strategy and all naming work from brief to launch, across products, features, events, and programs

• Develop names yourself, in volume, from descriptive to coined, and help teams and leaders pressure test them, running research when a decision needs it

• Build coherent brand architecture, naming, and terminology systems, including conventions, usage rules, and a source of truth, along with tools and training so teams can make routine calls on their own

• Manage intake and review, and get teams to come to us early, while there's still space to think, connect dots, and simplify

• Present brand architecture and naming decision docs to senior leaders, and advise them on the hard calls

• Track the portfolio over time, auditing and simplifying where it has grown complex

• Partner with IP Legal to evaluate options, plan around clearance risk, and take names through clearance

• Partner with Product and Brand Marketing to shape how new offerings are positioned, and ensure names work across global markets, including linguistic and cultural checks

• Lead alignment across Product, IP Legal, Brand Marketing, and Comms on where a new offering sits, what its name means, how to use it, and how to introduce it to the world

• Use Claude throughout the naming process, from generation to testing to governance

Minimum qualifications

• Have deep expertise in brand architecture, including deciding where new products and programs sit in a complex and growing portfolio

• Have built or rebuilt the brand architecture of a multi-brand portfolio, including how a company brand and its product brands work together

• Can weigh branded house, endorsed, and house of brands models, and make a clear recommendation

• Are genuinely passionate about brand architecture and naming as a craft, and appreciate how it builds stronger, more coherent brands and audience understanding

• Know the range of naming strategies, from descriptive to coined, and have personally generated and shipped names across products, features, events, and programs

• Have created systems and processes that codify brand architecture or names, such as nomenclature frameworks, conventions, databases, and governance, that teams at a company or client adopted

• Have worked with trademark counsel and can plan around clearance risk

• Write clear docs that get decisions made, and have scoped and led cross-company work with minimal direction

• Can teach senior leaders why brand strategies and systems should matter to them, defend a system with conviction, and know when an exception is worth making

• Are excited about Anthropic's mission to develop AI that is safe and beneficial

Preferred qualifications

• Led brand architecture or naming in-house, at a specialty branding agency, or at a consultancy

• Restructured a brand portfolio through rapid growth or major change

• Experience with AI products, models, or programs, or with technology companies more broadly

• Led naming across global markets, including linguistic and cultural checks

• Worked across both consumer and enterprise brands

• Designed qualitative or quantitative brand architecture or naming research, or managed naming, verbal identity, or research partners

• A background in linguistics, copywriting, or verbal identity, and experience using AI tools in creative work

• The ability to learn new, often technical, domains well enough to position, name, and brand them

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:

$255,000—$320,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

Who We Are

Atwell, LLC is a bold leader in the consulting, engineering, and construction services industry, delivering a broad range of creative solutions to clients in the real estate & land development, and energy markets. We have a strong national presence and a diverse, award-winning project portfolio. Atwell is a privately owned company, with 2,000+ passionate team members across 75+ locations and growing!

Atwell, LLC is a proud recipient of the following 2025 awards:

• Ten consecutive years in a row as a “Best Place to Work” by Zweig Group (#11)

• Recognized in Crain's “Fast 50” as one of the fastest-growing companies (#14)

About the Position

As a Senior Physical Engineer in Renewable Physical, you will provide technical leadership for the development and execution of renewable energy, energy storage, and substation projects. This role leads engineering efforts for complex project scopes, manages technical quality, and serves as a technical lead for project teams. In this role, an employee will be expected to demonstrate proficiency in regard to the essential functions of the job below.

• Lead engineering activities associated with renewable energy, energy storage, and substation projects.

• Lead technical execution for assigned project scopes and engineering work efforts.

• Perform and review complex engineering analyses, calculations, technical evaluations, and design activities.

• Manage technical quality and QA/QC activities within assigned scopes of work.

• Prepare and review engineering reports, technical studies, specifications, design criteria, and project documentation.

• Lead the development and review of site plans, general arrangements, elevations, bill of materials, trench and conduit plans, grounding plans, illumination design, lightning protection, and construction documents.

• Coordinate engineering activities across multidisciplinary project teams.

• Evaluate engineering alternatives, identify technical risks, and provide recommendations supporting project objectives and execution strategy.

• Lead project planning, technical coordination, and execution activities within assigned scopes of work.

• Serve as a technical lead and engineering resource for project teams.

Must-Have Qualifications

• Ability to lead technical execution and manage technical quality for assigned project scopes.

You will lead Central Office equipment, cabling, -48V DC infrastructure, testing, and integration work under approved MOPs and customer standards, including TP76300 where assigned. Strong hands-on Central Office experience and proven crew leadership are required. General telecommunications, outside-plant, commercial cabling, or data-center-only work does not replace that experience. Every project is subject to customer audit. Attention to detail, timely field completion, and a clean, passing customer audit are core expectations of this Level 4 role.

Core Responsibilities:

jobs.title: Physical Design and CAD Engineer
jobs.description:
Astera Labs (NASDAQ: ALAB) provides rack-scale AI infrastructure through purpose-built connectivity solutions. By collaborating with hyperscalers and ecosystem partners, Astera Labs enables organizations to unlock the full potential of modern AI. Astera Labs’ Intelligent Connectivity Platform integrates CXL®, Ethernet, NVLink, PCIe®, and UALink™ semiconductor-based technologies with the company’s COSMOS software suite to unify diverse components into cohesive, flexible systems that deliver end-to-end scale-up, and scale-out connectivity. The company’s custom connectivity solutions business complements its standards-based portfolio, enabling customers to deploy tailored architectures to meet their unique infrastructure requirements. Discover more at www.asteralabs.com.

About the Role

As a Physical Design & CAD Engineer, you will serve as a Technical Lead developing Astera Labs’ next-generation connectivity ASICs for cloud and AI infrastructure.

This role combines Physical Design CAD methodology development with hands-on place-and-route (PNR) implementation. You will develop and optimize automated design flows for advanced process nodes while contributing to block-level physical design, timing closure, and GDSII signoff.

You will collaborate with cross-functional engineering teams to improve design efficiency, automation, and silicon implementation.

What You'll Do

• Develop and maintain Physical Design CAD flows and methodologies for advanced process nodes.

• Build automation frameworks using Python and Tcl to support synthesis through signoff.

• Perform hands-on Physical Design and PNR, including floorplanning, placement, CTS, routing, and timing closure.

• Develop and optimize EDA tool flows for timing analysis, extraction, EM/IR, and physical verification.

• Support block-level implementation from synthesis through GDSII signoff.

• Improve design quality, automation, and flow efficiency.

• Collaborate with design, verification, and engineering teams to support ASIC development and tapeout.

Basic Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field; Master's degree preferred.

• 5+ years of experience in ASIC Physical Design, CAD methodology, or design automation.

• Strong understanding of physical design implementation and RTL-to-GDSII methodologies.

• Experience developing or maintaining Physical Design CAD flows.

• Hands-on experience with PNR, timing closure, and physical design signoff.

• Proficiency in Python and/or Tcl scripting.

• Experience with Cadence and/or Synopsys physical design tools.

• Experience with advanced semiconductor process nodes (7nm or below).

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with 3nm or more advanced process technologies.

• Experience building automated CAD flows from synthesis through signoff.

• Familiarity with Cadence Innovus, Tempus, Genus, Synopsys ICC2, Fusion Compiler, and PrimeTime.

• Experience with EM/IR analysis, DRC/LVS, ECO, and timing signoff methodologies.

• Experience with block-level ownership through tapeout.

• Experience developing scalable CAD methodologies and automation frameworks.

Compensation

The base salary range for this role is $160,000–$200,000 USD. Your salary will be determined based on your experience and the pay of employees in similar positions.

We know that creativity and innovation happen more often when teams include diverse ideas, backgrounds, and experiences, and we actively encourage everyone with relevant experience to apply, including people of color, LGBTQ+ and non-binary people, veterans, parents, and individuals with disabilities.

jobs.title: Member of Deployed Staff
jobs.description:
ABOUT FACTORY



Our mission is to create a world where software builds and improves itself.

We build the platform for self-improving software development, helping the world's largest enterprise engineering teams turn their organizations into autonomous software factories. Customers including Nvidia, Blackstone, Royal Bank of Canada (RBC), Palo Alto Networks, Adobe, and T-Mobile run Factory to ship code, review PRs, run tests, and deploy continuously - getting smarter with every cycle.

In 2026, we raised $200M at a $5B valuation, bringing our total funding to over $400M. We are backed by world-class investors and operators including Khosla Ventures, Sequoia, Blackstone, Ali Ghodsi (CEO of Databricks), and Frank Slootman (Former CEO of Snowflake).




ABOUT THE ROLE 

Factory is hiring Members of Deployed Staff to solve engineering problems alongside our customers. You’ll use Factory to deliver projects such as migrations, large-scale refactors, federated systems, agent harness engineering, and security remediation.

You’ll own scoped technical projects from discovery through implementation, validation, and handoff. That means understanding the customer’s systems, agreeing on what success looks like, writing and debugging code, and working through deployment constraints.

This is a hands-on engineering role with direct customer responsibility. We default to candidates with a technical engineering background who combine development skills with product judgment and exceptional technical communication.




WHAT YOU WILL DO AND ACHIEVE

 - Work with customer engineers and leaders to identify a concrete problem, define scope, and agree on success criteria.

 - Build and deliver solutions in customer codebases and environments, using Factory to accelerate the work.

 - Design integrations with customers’ development tools, infrastructure, and agent harnesses.

 - Diagnose failures across unfamiliar codebases, build systems, and production environments.

 - Validate changes through tests, evaluations, and rollout plans appropriate to the project.

 - Own delivery milestones, communicate risks, and leave customers with working software and a clear operational handoff.

 - Turn successful implementations into reusable tools, reference integrations, and guides.

 - Bring reproducible issues and field-tested recommendations back to Factory’s Product and Engineering teams.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - A technical engineering background, typically in software, infrastructure, platform, mobile, or security engineering.

 - Hands-on ability to read unfamiliar code, make changes, debug failures, and validate the result.

 - Strong understanding of software development, systems design, testing, and production operations.

 - Experience taking an ambiguous technical problem through to a delivered outcome.

 - Clear communication with engineers and non-technical stakeholders, including explaining trade-offs and setting realistic expectations.

 - A deep passion for working with customers and delivering exceptional outcomes.

 - Additional experience in tech lead or product management roles is a plus.





NICE TO HAVE

 - Migrations: Moving applications, databases, cloud infrastructure, ERP systems, or legacy platforms, including validation and cutover.

 - Refactors: Making substantial changes to complex codebases, architecture, frameworks, or APIs while preserving required behavior.

 - Federated systems and on-premises deployments: Helping customers build federated systems within complex enterprise architectures, working across infrastructure, identity, networking, and security boundaries.

 - iOS / Android: Shipping mobile applications, with experience in platform-specific development, build systems, testing, and release workflows.

 - Federal / public sector: Delivering technical systems in government environments and working through their security, authorization, and operational requirements.

 - Agent harness engineering: Building agent runtimes or integrating agents into existing systems, including tools, orchestration, execution environments, and evaluations.

 - Security: Application or infrastructure security, vulnerability remediation, secure development workflows, or validating security fixes.

We’re interested in what you personally built, the constraints you worked through, and how you verified that it worked.




LOCATION AND TRAVEL

This is a hybrid role. Based in San Francisco, New York, London, Washington, DC, Australia, or Singapore. Customer travel is typically about once a month, mostly within your region.

jobs.title: Principal Software Engineer (Remote)
jobs.description:
Who We Are

At 8th Light, we bring life to the best ideas.

Founded in 2006 and headquartered in Chicago, we are a technology solutions consultancy that partners with organizations from early-stage startups to the world's largest companies. We take on hard software challenges and turn them into durable results. We build agentic products, the platforms they run on, and the engineering and design at every layer.

Our commitment to quality means we deliver solutions we’re truly proud of, while our curiosity sparks innovation and breakthrough thinking. 8th Lights thrive in an environment that champions continuous education, fueling our growth through mentorship and hands-on work. We foster an open, collaborative culture grounded in honesty that builds trust, and believe true success is measured by the outcomes we create for our clients.

If this kind of work and our kind of people energizes you, you’ve found the right place.

Who You Are

You’ve shown long-term repeated success on a variety of projects, typically over the course of 10+ years. You are a trusted expert and leader, often called upon to guide ambiguous initiatives and architect scalable solutions. You bring a blend of deep consulting acumen, technical expertise, and product thinking that drives measurable and impactful outcomes. In your previous experience, you have:

• Built and shipped production-grade platforms: the reusable foundations, tools, infrastructure, and workflows that help other teams shift faster and more reliably

• Taken AI and agentic systems from prototype to production, with a strong understanding of infrastructure, authentication, and observability

• Delivered on high-stakes consulting engagements across multiple language paradigms, stacks, ecosystems, and client industries

• Built high-quality, maintainable software collaboratively, incrementally, and through an approach tailored towards the unique needs of the clients you’ve served

• Led the development and delivery of production-grade software using a variety of languages and frameworks, including but not limited to: Java, C#/.NET, Python, TypeScript, JavaScript, React, Go, Ruby, Scala, R, Rust, and SQL

• Actively experimented with AI development tools and translated that experimentation into faster, higher-quality delivery for your teams

• A track record of understanding, assessing, and embracing new tooling and trends within the software industry

• Built or integrated AI/ML features into products and systems, including recommendation engines, NLP, computer vision, predictive analytics, RAG pipelines, and agents

• Successfully led modernization and replatforming efforts to align legacy systems with short and long-term business needs

• Led and delivered solutions to architecture-level problems including scalability, security, reliability, performance, maintainability, and observability

• Facilitated alignment across technical and non-technical stakeholders to move initiatives forward through ambiguity and complexity

• Provided mentorship and team support at scale, while sharing knowledge and improving team practices

• Collaboratively led stakeholders to balance technical considerations with product and user needs

• Actively sought out and effectively given feedback

What You’ll Do At 8th Light

As a go-to technologist and strategist within 8th Light, you’ll work with a variety of clients, typically one to two in a year, while continuing to deepen your and our collective domain expertise over the course of your career with us. You’ll be responsible for:

• Rapidly building trust with clients, demonstrating technical expertise and understanding of their domain and objectives

• Driving platform engineering work at the client level, connecting long-term technical vision to what ships

• Leading platform strategy and delivery across diverse platform types, connecting long-term vision to what ships

• Working pragmatically to balance technology choices while delivering high-quality work within deadlines

• Advising clients on architecture, scalability and platform evolution, connecting technical decisions to product and business outcomes

• Collaborating on systems that involve the full ML lifecycle from data ingestion and preprocessing, to model deployment, integration, and performance monitoring

• Driving innovation by proactively surfacing new technical approaches and product solutions

• Leading or initiating formal feedback conversations with teams and clients via retrospectives

• Clearly articulating and documenting outcomes and driving forward action items

• Contributing to the health of your team and 8th Light’s culture by modeling our Values

• Designing and managing high-level technical roadmaps for large engagements

• Building your network and maintaining relationships with clients and other industry leaders within your domain

• Coaching client engineering teams, transferring knowledge and leveling up practices

• Influencing client CTOs and executive decisions. Planning and execute technical work that involves stakeholders outside of project boundaries such as across a client's technical organization

• Partner with account teams on planning, opportunity identification, stakeholder relationships, and pre-sales scope shaping

• Facilitating retrospectives, strategy sessions, and technical deep-dives to improve team and project outcomes

• Identifying, mitigating, and resolving blockers to team progress

• Contributing to 8th Light by serving as a mentor, leading or designing workshops internally or for clients, representing 8th Light in the tech community, or supporting our hiring processes

• Demonstrating leadership in scalable system design, modular architecture, and platform- or product-oriented development

• Bringing depth in testing strategies, observability, fault tolerance, and secure engineering practices

• Applying architectural patterns to evaluate tradeoffs and drive clear, documented design rationale

Strongly Preferred Skills

We work across many areas, and encourage anyone with the experience listed above to apply. We would particularly like to encourage applicants with experience in the following areas:

• Platform engineering: building reusable software foundations, internal developer platforms, and infrastructure that other teams build on

• Data Engineering: including platforms like Databricks for data processing and analytics

• Delivering production agentic systems, including RAG pipelines, vector search, and agentic frameworks such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, AutoGen, and n8n

• DevSecOps & DevOps

• MLOps

• Infrastructure as Code

Building a truly diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace is an ongoing journey, and we’re excited to keep learning and growing together. We have a proud tradition of hiring talented colleagues with real-world career experiences.

How You’ll be Supported

At 8th Light, we believe our people are our greatest asset. Their growth, well-being, and success shape our future.

Our wellness package is designed with the Whole YOU in mind and includes:

• A robust L&D program featuring unlimited access to thousands of books, courses, and expert-led training on the O'Reilly learning platform.

• Annual financial stipend and time allotment for learning & development

• Coworking support for our global team

• Flexible PTO

• 12 weeks of new parent leave available for eligible employees

See our full list of Benefits.

A Note on Compensation

At 8th Light, we are committed to a compensation philosophy that is transparent, fair, and helps us attract and retain top talent in alignment with our company’s strategic growth goals and clients’ needs.

We benchmark our salaries using Geographic Structures to establish competitive pay ranges within the regions where 8th Lights live. Our pay ranges for our Principal Engineer position within our four US structures are as follows:

• Structure 1 (Denver, Tampa Metro, Philadelphia Metro, Ohio, Wisconsin)

• RANGE: $151,535-$189,418 USD

• Structure 2 (Chicago Metro, Miami Metro, Philadelphia Metro, Raleigh Metro )

• RANGE: $159,240-$199,050 USD

• Structure 3 (Austin Metro, Boston Metro , DC Metro)

• RANGE: $169,513-$211,892 USD

• Structure 4 (Los Angeles, Seattle, New York City)

• RANGE: $176,705- $220,881 USD

Reach out to recruiting@8thlight.com for more relevant information pertaining to your local market.

8th Light Hubs and Geographies

As a remote-first company, 8th Light's culture is rooted in strong connections that extend across our teams, regions, and beyond client work. We are a distributed team across the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom, with hubs in Chicago, London, Los Angeles, New York, and Seattle.

If you are hired into a hub, you will be a part of a team with regular rituals around co-working and community building. For team members outside of those cities, we offer access to coworking spaces to foster continued collaboration and connection across our global team.

In most cases, our consulting engagements do not require travel.

We hope to see you apply!

A Note on Your Privacy

At 8th Light, one of our core values is Honesty that builds trust — and that shapes how we approach hiring. We want you to have a clear picture of who we are, what we're looking for, and how we handle your information throughout the process.

Before submitting your application, please take a moment to review our Global Candidate Privacy Notice. By applying, you acknowledge that you've read it.

jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SR. AUTOMATION AND CONTROLS ENGINEER, INSOURCE MANUFACTURING (STARLINK)

SpaceX is developing a low latency, broadband internet system to meet the needs of consumers across the globe. Enabled by a constellation of low Earth orbit satellites, Starlink will provide fast, reliable internet to populations with little or no connectivity, including those in rural communities and places where existing services are too expensive or unreliable.

As a member of the Materials Engineering group, you will develop and implement technologies to support high-volume production, rapid product iteration, and new capabilities at SpaceX. You will work with multiple manufacturing disciplines, including injection molding, high pressure die casting, stamping, and mold manufacturing. A strong focus on safety is required, ensuring that all technologies and processes meet the highest safety standards. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams, including design engineering, manufacturing, and operations. Having an open mindset, challenging requirements, and using engineering fundamentals are essential in this role.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Design, develop, and manage automation projects

• Manage specifications, cost, lead-time, installation, and commissioning of new equipment

• Own safety strategy and planning. Implement ANSI/RIA15.06/OSHA compliant systems

• Collaborate with and challenge mechanical designers and manufacturing engineers to create system requirements and architecture

• Create and maintain equipment documentation and drawings to enable hand-off to operational teams

• Debug, root-cause, and make continuous improvements of equipment in a high-rate production environment

• Architect, write, and debug PLC code with an emphasis on generating code that is organized, structured, documented, maintainable, and reusable for high-volume manufacturing applications

• Generate aesthetically simple HMI screens to make complex machines easy to understand, operate, and troubleshoot

• Design electrical systems compliant to NEC, NFPA, & UL508A regulations

• Manage electrical cabinet builds, field wiring, pneumatic and fluid plumbing

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline

• 5+ years of experience in the design and commissioning of controls systems for industrial applications

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Process integration and electromechanical/mechatronic systems experience

• Robot programming experience, preferably ABB

• C#, .NET, python and/or SQL experience

• PLC programming experience, preferably Beckhoff TwinCAT or Siemens TIA Portal

• HMI and SCADA programming experience, preferably Ignition or Beckhoff TwinCAT HMI

• Field bus networks, serial communication and Ethernet communication

• Knowledge of NEC, UL508A codes

• Experience with 3D CAD, preferably Siemens NX

• Exposure to a wide variety of industrial machinery

• Experience in fast-paced iterative design and test environments

• Experience automating the aggregation of metrics into dashboards and alerting systems

• Experience with developing and deploying tools used for data analysis

• Industrial software application to mechanical assemblies, electrical systems, sensors, pneumatics/hydraulics, including how to safely checkout these interdisciplinary systems prior to production implementation

• Electrical schematic CAD experience using EPlan

• Electrical sizing of motors, cables, circuit protection, VFDs, motor starters, and other motion systems

• Hands-on experience building and commissioning high quality electrical control panels and electro-mechanical systems

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Must be willing to travel up to 10%

• Standing/walking for long periods of time

jobs.description:
At Qualtrics, we create software the world’s best brands use to deliver exceptional frontline experiences, build high-performing teams, and design products people love. But we are more than a platform—we are the creators and stewards of the Experience Management category serving over 18K clients globally. Building a category takes grit, determination, and a disdain for convention—but most of all it requires close-knit, high-functioning teams with an unwavering dedication to serving our customers.

When you join one of our teams, you’ll be part of a nimble group that’s empowered to set aggressive goals and move fast to achieve them. Strategic risks are encouraged and complex problems are solved together, by passing the mic and iterating until the best solution comes to light. You won’t have to look to find growth opportunities—ready or not, they’ll find you. From retail to government to healthcare, we’re on a mission to bring humanity, connection, and empathy back to business. Join over 5,000 people across the globe who think that’s work worth doing.

Enterprise Account Executive - K-12

Why We Have This Role

At Qualtrics, our Enterprise sales teams tackle high-stakes institutional challenges, driving digital and cultural transformation across the nation’s largest school districts and state agencies. In this role, you will lead transformative Experience Management (XM) initiatives across Tier-1 public school systems, regional educational agencies, and state DOEs to solve critical challenges—from school climate and educator retention to community engagement. You will serve as an executive strategic advisor to Superintendents, Cabinets, and elected School Boards, orchestrating complex multi-stakeholder sales campaigns. Working closely with internal deal teams—including Solutions Engineers, Education Strategists, Professional Services, and RFP Specialists—you will champion solutions that elevate student voice and reshape public education.

How You’ll Find Success

• Consultative Executive Advising: You thrive on establishing trusted partnerships with Superintendents, CAOs, CTOs, and School Board members, aligning software solutions directly with district strategic plans.

• Complex Deal Orchestration: You love navigating long, multi-stakeholder enterprise cycles (6–18 months) and mobilizing cross-functional experts to deliver compelling proposals.

• Public Sector Acumen: You are energized by mastering the nuances of public procurement, including state purchasing cooperatives (e.g., Omnia, TIPS), formal RFP/bids, and federal funding streams (Title I, II-A, IV).

• Strategic Territory Ownership: You take pride in building targeted account plans, executing disciplined land-and-expand strategies, and maintaining rigorous pipeline hygiene using MEDDPICC and Command of the Message.

• Autonomous Drive: You excel with the operational freedom to run your territory remotely while traveling on-site (25%–40%) to lead high-impact board and cabinet presentations.

How You’ll Grow

• Executive Leadership Pathways: Access structured leadership tracks, executive coaching, and continuous product enablement to accelerate your career.

• Category-Defining Influence: Deepen your domain mastery by expanding the Experience Management (XM) category across the public sector and statewide education systems.

• High-Complexity Deal Mastery: Hone your enterprise acumen by closing seven-figure, multi-year public sector agreements at scale.

Things You’ll Do

• Drive Strategic District Penetration: Formulate and execute account-level business plans for Tier-1 districts to successfully navigate budget seasons, long sales cycles, and school board approvals.

• Achieve ARR Impact: Meet and exceed annual seven-figure ARR targets through new logo acquisition, large-scale enterprise expansions, and multi-year contracts ($150K–$1M+ ACV).

• Deliver Value-Based Executive Advisory: Partner with district c-suites and board members to identify critical climate, staffing, and community gaps, mapping them to Qualtrics XM outcomes.

• Mobilize Cross-Functional Deal Teams: Lead Solutions Engineers, Education Strategists, RFP Specialists, and Executive Sponsors to craft winning, compliant public sector bids and presentations.

• Master Procurement & Public Funding: Align enterprise deals with cooperative contracts and federal/state funding allocations (Title I, Title II-A, Title IV, state legislative grants) to accelerate contract execution.

• Maintain Operational Rigor: Deliver reliable quarterly forecasts, disciplined pipeline tracking, and MEDDPICC qualification within Salesforce.com, Gong, and Clari.

What We’re Looking For On Your Resume

• Enterprise Quota Attainment: A documented track record of carrying enterprise SaaS quota and consistently hitting or exceeding seven-figure annual ARR targets.

• Complex Multi-Stakeholder Deals: Proven experience running 6- to 18-month consultative sales cycles with high ACVs ($150K–$1M+) and formal buying committees.

• Public Sector & Education Sales Background: Direct experience selling software, data, or analytics platforms into K-12 school districts, state/local government, or public sector agencies (with established relationships across Superintendents and state agencies preferred).

• Procurement & Bidding Competence: Demonstrated success navigating formal RFPs/RFIs, state purchasing cooperatives, and public funding mechanisms.

• Modern Sales Stack Mastery: Hands-on experience executing with MEDDPICC or Command of the Message, alongside CRM and sales intelligence platforms (Salesforce, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Gong, Clari).

• Education & Mobility: Bachelor’s degree and ability to travel 25%–40% for client meetings and national conferences.

What You Should Know About This Team

• Qualtrics’ K-12 Account Executive team is dedicated to changing the way our customers focus on Experience data. Forrester reports that companies generate a 674% return on investment when using Qualtrics. Now that’s a solution you can get behind!

• As an Enterprise Account Executive, you will focus on growing new revenue through strategic, relationship-based selling, a hunter mentality, and educating prospective and current customers on the value of Qualtrics XM. Our most successful Account Executives have a track record of exceeding quota, acting as trusted advisors to clients, and being passionate teammates.

• The challenge? Qualtrics XM is a very versatile platform, adding value to a limitless array of decision makers. If you love a strategic, analytical sales process and working with a variety of stakeholders, selling Qualtrics XM will always keep you learning and growing.

Our Team’s Favorite Perks and Benefits

• Salary + Uncapped Commissions and Accelerators

• 100% Performance based promotions -- not politics or tenure

• Catered lunch

• Culture - Incredible work environment - you can wear jeans and bring your dog to the office, anytime

• Quarterly team activities, winter and summer parties, and lots of Qualtrics swag

The Qualtrics Hybrid Work Model: Our hybrid work model is elegantly simple: we all gather in the office three days a week; Mondays and Thursdays, plus one day selected by your organizational leader. These purposeful in-person days in thoughtfully designed offices help us do our best work and harness the power of collaboration and innovation. For the rest of the week, work where you want, owning the integration of work and life. #Remote

Qualtrics is an equal opportunity employer meaning that all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other protected characteristic.

​​​​​​​Applicants in the United States of America have rights under Federal Employment Laws:Family & Medical Leave Act, Equal Opportunity Employment, Employee Polygraph Protection Act

Qualtrics is committed to the inclusion of all qualified individuals. As part of this commitment, Qualtrics will ensure that persons with disabilities are provided with reasonable accommodations. jobs.title: Sr. Mechanical Engineer, Insource Manufacturing (Starlink)
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SR. MECHANICAL ENGINEER, INSOURCE MANUFACTURING (STARLINK)

The Insource Manufacturing team is responsible for designing, building, and qualifying custom equipment and automation systems to enable high-volume production of Starlink products. As a Mechanical Engineer in this group, you will take end-to-end ownership of critical manufacturing equipment and material handling systems. This role requires a detail-oriented engineer who is passionate about designing robust mechanical and automation systems, optimizing existing equipment, and developing novel solutions that push the boundaries of high-volume manufacturing while minimizing risk and maximizing efficiency in our state-of-the-art Starlink factory.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Own manufacturing subsystems and equipment from conceptual design through fabrication, commissioning, and high-volume production ramp

• Develop design criteria, collaborate on requirements with cross-functional teams, and drive system-level optimization

• Perform failure modes and effects analysis (FMEA), reliability modeling, and stress testing to predict and mitigate potential failures and improve overall equipment effectiveness (OEE)

• Design and develop production equipment including structures, mechanisms, robot end effectors, automation systems, and material handling solutions

• Uptime Optimization: Monitor and track equipment performance metrics using data analytics; identify bottlenecks and downtime causes, then implement preventive and predictive maintenance strategies to maximize operational availability

• Evaluate and select equipment suppliers and vendors based on reliability, performance, and business needs; oversee installation, commissioning, and ongoing performance of both internally designed and vendor-supplied equipment

• Demonstrate extreme ownership of projects through their entire lifecycle while balancing multiple initiatives in a fast-paced environment

• Collaborate closely with design, manufacturing, and test teams to develop products and production processes in parallel

• Solve complex, open-ended problems with an emphasis on speed of execution, efficiency, and scalability

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, manufacturing, materials, or other engineering discipline

• 5+ years of professional experience with mechanical design, analysis, testing, or manufacturing (internship experience is applicable)

• 3+ years of experience with CAD and FEA software packages

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Master’s degree or PhD in an engineering discipline

• 3+ years of experience in a leadership position in a manufacturing environment

• Experience with custom machine design including electromechanical systems, end-of-arm tooling, motors, actuators, linear rails, bearings, and lifting/rigging

• Proficient in 3D CAD (Siemens NX preferred) and Teamcenter

• Solid understanding and application of GD&T, mechanical engineering fundamentals, structural analysis, and failure modes of complex mechanical systems

• Prior ownership of a complex component or assembly from initial design through production ramp

• Experience applying common manufacturing processes (welding, machining, assembly, inspection) and designing for manufacturability

• Hands-on experience with mills, lathes, manual and CNC machines

• Experience with FEA, structural hand calculations, and sizing of mechanical components

• Self-motivated with strong organizational, written, and oral communication skills

jobs.title: Senior Flight Test Engineer - Advanced Effects (Roadrunner)
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE ROLE

This position is looking for a highly motivated flight test engineer with emphasis in developmental test of new aircraft weapon and missile systems. You will work closely with the program test leadership, and a wide spectrum of cross-departments team members, solving hard problems and changing the industry forever. The role will be responsible for planning, coordination, execution and reporting on all facets of the test program.

The Test and Evaluation team at Anduril works across the entire spectrum of products and business lines, as well as all flight operations and test range management. Our team conducts full system level development testing, new production acceptance testing, sub-component qualification testing and much more. In short, if it involves test, we support it. If you are interested in working in an extremely innovative and fast paced environment, where your work directly makes an impact and difference in the products that are fielded, this a fantastic opportunity.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Plan and execute system level T&E of hardware and software with emphasis placed on resource planning, conducting ground and flight test, initial issue investigation, and process improvement/development.

• Act as lead or supporting test engineer for missile or weapon systems to include development, certification and integration test of subsystems to the AUR configuration.

• Collect test data and perform initial data analysis for the system under test.

• Work closely with program management and other engineering departments to develop requirements, and discuss test results to include collected data and observations.

• Assist in the creation of developmental test plans, test cards, technical updates and test reports.

• Conduct ground and flight testing at private and government-owned test ranges.

• Work in a safe manner in accordance with established operating procedures and standard practices.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• A bachelor's degree in engineering or a related technical discipline from an accredited institution. May substitute equivalent engineering experience in lieu of education.

• 8+ years of experience as test conductor/director for developmental aircraft, weapons, or missile systems.

• Must have a good understanding of engineering concepts, principles, codes, and theory; experience demonstrating a broad application of those concepts; and expanding knowledge of principles, concepts, theory, and practices in related technical specialties.

• Test engineering experience working with developmental weapon or missile systems on manned and/or unmanned aircraft to include requirements development, planning, execution, and reporting.

• Previous experience with and/or current working knowledge of MIL-STD-8591, MIL-STD-2088, MIL-STD-1553, MIL-STD-1760, AS8775, AS5653, etc.

• Experience integrating and conducting test with suspension, arming, and release equipment.

• Previous expertise and working knowledge of the National Airspace System and UAS operating rules and regulations thereof.

• Must possess the ability to understand new concepts quickly; apply them accurately; organize, schedule, and coordinate work phases; and, determine the appropriate approach at the task level or, with assistance, at the project level to provide solutions to a range of complex problems.

• Strong computer and documentation experience.

• Must have strong communication (written and verbal) and interpersonal skills.

• Ability to work independently and as part of a team; able to perform complex tasks in one or more engineering areas.

• Able to work extended hours as required.

• Ability to travel as required for test planning and execution.

• Bias for action – if you see a problem, you want to solve and fix it.

• Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Top Secret-Level security clearance.

• In this role, you will be subject to pre-employment and randomized substance screening, as required by the Company.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Experience working with the Department of Defense (DoD).

• Prior experience with software code/script building using programming languages such as Go, Java, C++, Python, JavaScript, etc.

• Prior experience with Linux based systems and command line.

• Working Knowledge with COTs Small UAS autopilot and mission planning software.

• Experience working with manned aircraft personnel and familiar with aviation terminology.

• Experience with weapon or tactical datalinks.

• Experience with multiple different propulsion systems to include air and non-air breathing.

US Salary Range

$147,000—$196,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

• No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

• Please always verify communications: Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address. Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

• Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

• What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineering, Thermal Control
jobs.description:
Vast is developing next-generation space stations and space infrastructure using an incremental, hardware-rich, and low-cost approach. Vast is rapidly developing its multi-module Haven Station to ensure a continuous human presence in space for America and its allies, enabling advanced microgravity research and manufacturing, and unlocking a new space economy for government, corporate, and private customers. Haven Demo’s 2025 success made Vast the only operational commercial space station company to fly and operate its own spacecraft. Next, Haven-1 is expected to become the world’s first commercial space station when it launches in 2027, followed by additional Haven modules. Additionally, the company recently announced Vast Satellite, a high-power satellite product line leveraging its space station components and the heritage of Haven Demo.

Headquartered in Long Beach, California, and with more than 1,000 employees and over a billion dollars in private capital, Vast has built the facilities required to manufacture and operate America’s next space station. The company plans to develop future habitats and systems for the Moon and Mars, dedicated space stations for government partners, and other crewed systems that will unlock the expanding long-term space economy.

Vast is looking for a Manufacturing Engineer, Thermal Control Systems, to help develop the systems behind our human-rated space stations. You'll use your engineering knowledge and creativity to design, build, and test novel solutions at the cutting edge of space technology.

This will be a full-time, exempt position located in our Long Beach, CA location.

Responsibilities:

• Develop and optimize manufacturing processes for environmental and thermal control systems, balancing efficiency, quality, and cost-effectiveness

• Design, fabricate, and activate ground support equipment and test articles in partnership with technicians, with an emphasis on pressurized ground systems

• Operate, troubleshoot, repair, maintain, and modify manufacturing and test equipment spanning vacuum to 20,000 psig, including pneumatic, hydraulic, oxygen, refrigerant, and data/control systems

• Author and maintain detailed manufacturing plans, assembly procedures, and work instructions for consistent and accurate production of TCS hardware

• Perform hands-on assembly, integration, and testing of components to ensure compliance with engineering specifications and industry standards

• Identify and resolve manufacturing challenges through root cause analysis and corrective action

• Collaborate with design teams to provide design-for-manufacturability, assembly, and test feedback on thermal and environmental hardware (e.g., tubing, heat exchangers, cold plates, pumps, fans, valves, heaters, filters, MLI)

• Partner with suppliers to ensure on-time delivery of high-quality components, including reviewing and approving supplier manufacturing processes

• Collaborate with quality assurance teams to establish and uphold rigorous quality control processes

• Drive continuous improvement initiatives to enhance efficiency, reduce waste, and elevate product quality

• Understanding of fluid systems, tube manufacturing processes, and assembly techniques

Minimum Qualifications:

• B.S. in mechanical, aerospace, manufacturing or electrical engineering, physics, mathematics, or a related technical field

• 2 + years of manufacturing experience managing a product/product line across multiple work centers and/or departments, fluid, pressurized, propulsion, or environmental control hardware in design, manufacturing, or test

• 2-4+ years of experience for Manufacturing Engineer II

• 4-6+ years of experience for Senior Manufacturing Engineer

• Hands-on fabrication, assembly, and/or integration experience; CAD proficiency (NX preferred)

• Experience with CAD tools (e.g., Siemens NX) and the ability to review designs, generate manufacturing documentation, and design assembly or test tooling

Preferred Skills & Experience:

• Hands-on experience building or testing hardware, in industry or through student teams such as Formula SAE, rocketry, CubeSat, or robotics

• Experience with aerospace, spacecraft, propulsion, or other safety-critical or high-reliability hardware

• Experience taking designs or processes from concept through build or test, and from R&D to production

• Familiarity with CAD tools, ideally Siemens NX, and PLM tools such as Teamcenter

• Exposure to thermal or structural analysis using Ansys, or similar tools

• Awareness of aerospace workmanship, design, and environmental test standards such as IPC, SMC-S-016, NASA-STD-5001, or MIL-STD-810

• Proficiency applying GD&T

• Strong problem-solving skills, including troubleshooting and structured root cause analysis

• Strong attention to detail, clear communication, and the ability to work well in cross-functional teams

• Senior Level: experience mentoring engineers or technicians and managing multiple projects at once

Additional Requirements:

• Willingness to work evenings and/or weekends to support critical mission milestones

Pay Ranges:

• Engineer/ Level I: $86,100.00 - $122,220.00

• Engineer/ Level II: $112,340.00 - $159,468.00

Full-time employees also receive company equity, as well as access to a full suite of compelling benefits and perks, including: medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and dependents, generous paid time off; up to 20+ days of vacation for exempt staff and up to 10+ days of vacation for non-exempt staff with the ability to cash-out unused vacation annually, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, ClassPass credits, personalized mental healthcare through Spring Health, and other discounts and perks. jobs.title: Director, Sales Compensation & Planning
jobs.description:
Who is Trace3?

Trace3 is a leading Transformative IT Authority, providing unique technology solutions and consulting services to our clients. Equipped with elite engineering and dynamic innovation, we empower IT executives and their organizations to achieve competitive advantage through a process of Integrate, Automate, Innovate.

Our culture at Trace3 embodies the spirit of a startup with the advantage of a scalable business. Employees can grow their career and have fun while doing it!

Trace3 is headquartered in Irvine, California. We employ more than 1,200 people all over the United States. Our major field office locations include Denver, Indianapolis, Grand Rapids, Lexington, Los Angeles, Louisville, Texas, San Francisco.

Ready to discover the possibilities that live in technology?

Come Join Us!

Street-Smart - Thriving in Dynamic Times

We are flexible and resilient in a fast-changing environment. We continuously innovate and drive constructive change while keeping a focus on the “big picture.” We exercise sound business judgment in making high-quality decisions in a timely and cost-effective manner. We are highly creative and can dig deep within ourselves to find positive solutions to different problems.

Juice - The “Stuff” it takes to be a Needle Mover

We get things done and drive results. We lead without a title, empowering others through a can-do attitude. We look forward to the goal, mentally mapping out every checkpoint on the pathway to success, and visualizing what the final destination looks and feels like.

Teamwork - Humble, Hungry and Smart

We are humble individuals who understand how our job impacts the company's mission. We treat others with respect, admit mistakes, give credit where it’s due and demonstrate transparency. We “bring the weather” by exhibiting positive leadership and solution-focused thinking. We hug people in their trials, struggles, and failures – not just their success. We appreciate the individuality of the people around us.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

The Director, Sales Compensation & Planning is responsible for the design, governance, and continuous improvement of Trace3's sales incentive compensation programs. This includes commissions, SPIFFs, overrides, accelerators, and other variable pay programs across the sales organization. The role leads annual incentive plan design, quota and target-setting support, territory planning alignment, and the development of analytics that measure plan effectiveness against Trace3's growth, profitability, and value-capture objectives.

This leader partners closely with GTM Strategy & Operations, Revenue Operations, Finance, and Sales Leadership to ensure compensation programs support business priorities and drive pay-for-performance outcomes across all go-to-market segments. The Director also leads and develops a team of compensation analysts, providing strategic direction, governance, and operational oversight of sales compensation programs.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

• Design, document, and maintain annual and in-year sales incentive plans, including commissions, SPIFFs, overrides, accelerators, and MBO components, across all sales segments and roles.

• Lead the incentive plan governance process, including plan approval workflows, exception handling, plan change control, and maintenance of a complete audit trail for plan decisions.

• Define and document sales compensation policies, crediting rules, and plan terms. Maintain the sales incentive plan document library and participant plan agreements.

• Partner with Sales, Finance, and GTM leadership on quota and target-setting methodologies, territory and account coverage planning, and segment-level capacity models.

• Model plan costs, payout curves, and pay-for-performance outcomes. Conduct scenario analysis to evaluate potential plan changes and business impacts prior to implementation.

• Build and maintain incentive compensation analytics and reporting that measure attainment distribution, plan effectiveness, participant behavior, and return on incentive spend.

• Lead the annual sales compensation planning cycle, ensuring incentive designs align with segmentation strategy, value-capture priorities, and revenue growth objectives.

• Serve as the subject matter expert for sales incentive compensation programs and provide guidance to Sales leadership on plan interpretation, governance, and crediting-rule matters.

• Partner with compensation administration, payroll, finance, and systems teams to ensure incentive plans are accurately configured and operationalized in downstream systems. This role is accountable for plan design and governance and does not calculate, process, approve, or disburse individual payments.

• Establish plan effectiveness metrics and lead recurring business reviews with GTM and Finance leadership to evaluate program performance and recommend enhancements.

• Lead, coach, and develop a team of compensation analysts, setting priorities, reviewing work product, and building analytical and business partnership capabilities.

• Maintain documentation, controls, and governance practices to support internal and external audits of sales incentive compensation programs.

QUALIFICATIONS & INTERESTS:

• Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Accounting, Human Resources, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• 8+ years of experience in sales compensation, sales operations, revenue operations, finance, compensation, or related analytical disciplines.

• 3+ years of experience leading and developing professional-level employees and/or teams.

• Deep knowledge of sales incentive plan design, including commissions, SPIFFs, overrides, accelerators, quotas, and crediting rules.

• Strong financial modeling and analytical skills with the ability to evaluate plan cost, payout scenarios, and business impacts and translate findings into actionable recommendations.

• Experience with CRM, ERP, and Sales Performance Management (SPM) platforms; advanced Microsoft Excel skills required.

• Working knowledge of quota setting, territory planning, account coverage models, and go-to-market segmentation.

• Strong governance and controls mindset with exceptional attention to detail, documentation, and process discipline.

• Proven ability to build effective partnerships across Sales, Finance, Revenue Operations, and executive leadership while balancing competing business priorities.

• Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate complex compensation concepts to senior leaders and stakeholders.

• Experience within a technology, value-added reseller (VAR), distribution, or similar sales-driven environment preferred.

Actual salary will be based on a variety of factors, including location, experience, skill set, performance, licensure and certification, and business needs. The range for this position in other geographic locations may differ. Certain positions may also be eligible for variable incentive compensation, such as bonuses or commissions, that is not included in the base salary.

Estimated Pay Range

$150,000—$200,000 USD

The Perks

• Comprehensive medical, dental and vision plans for you and your dependents

• 401(k) Retirement Plan with Employer Match, 529 College Savings Plan, Health Savings Account, Life Insurance, and Long-Term Disability

• Competitive Compensation

• Training and development programs

• Major offices stocked with snacks and beverages

• Collaborative and cool culture

• Work-life balance and generous paid time off

Our Commitment

At the core of Trace3's DNA is our people. We are a diverse group of talented individuals who understand the importance of teamwork and demonstrating leadership, character, and passion in all that we do.

We’re committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where everyone feels respected, valued, and empowered to grow. We recognize that embracing diversity drives innovation, improves outcomes, fosters collaboration, boosts teammate satisfaction, and builds a more inclusive culture.

As an equal opportunity employer, Trace3 bases all employment decisions based on individual qualifications, merit, and business requirements. We do not engage in discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including gender identity, sexual orientation, and pregnancy), national origin, age (40 or older), disability, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law.

Any demographic information provided is strictly voluntary, kept confidential in accordance with Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) regulations, and will not be used in employment decisions, including hiring, promotions, or mentorship programs. We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities for all.

If you require a reasonable accommodation to complete the application process or participate in an interview, please email recruiting@trace3.com.

As part of GTM Strategy & Operations, this role partners closely with Finance, Revenue Operations, Sales Leadership, business units, and data teams to align commercial and financial insights, establish performance metrics, and identify opportunities to improve growth, profitability, and operational efficiency.

This role analyzes customer profitability, cost-to-serve, customer lifetime value (LTV), customer acquisition cost (CAC), and related commercial economics. Through financial modeling, reporting, and scenario analysis, the GTM Economics & Profitability Manager provides insights and recommendations that support planning, forecasting, investment decisions, coverage strategies, and go-to-market initiatives.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

• Develop and maintain customer profitability and cost-to-serve models across customers, segments, regions, offerings, and routes to market.

• Support the development and ongoing refinement of commercial cost frameworks, including sales compensation, sales management, presales, customer success, renewals, delivery support, and other revenue-supporting resources.

• Partner with Finance, Revenue Operations, and business leaders to define, measure, and report key commercial performance metrics, including customer lifetime value (LTV), customer acquisition cost (CAC), LTV:CAC, payback, contribution margin, and return on investment.

• Create and maintain recurring dashboards, reports, and analyses that measure profitability, cost-to-serve, margin performance, and commercial efficiency across customer segments, regions, and business units.

• Analyze financial and operational performance data to identify trends, risks, opportunities, cost inefficiencies, and margin improvement opportunities.

• Evaluate the profitability impact of sales motions, account segmentation strategies, coverage models, pricing approaches, service offerings, and customer complexity.

• Develop financial models and scenario analyses to assess the impact of changes in productivity, headcount, support ratios, commission structures, retention, share of wallet, and growth investments.

• Support annual planning, forecasting, budgeting, and investment decisions through data-driven analysis and business case development.

• Identify and investigate anomalies in GTM and financial data, determine root causes, and recommend corrective actions where appropriate.

• Partner with business leaders to translate analytical findings into actionable recommendations that improve revenue growth, profitability, and operational effectiveness.

• Provide analytical support and decision-making insights to GTM Strategy & Operations leadership, Finance, and executive stakeholders on strategic initiatives and business performance.

• Maintain documentation of models, assumptions, methodologies, data sources, and reporting standards to ensure consistency, transparency, and auditability.

• Collaborate with BI, CRM, ERP, Finance, and data teams to improve data quality, automate reporting processes, and enhance analytical capabilities.

• Communicate complex financial and operational insights through clear, concise, and business-focused presentations, reports, and recommendations.

QUALIFICATIONS & INTERESTS:

• Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Business, Accounting, Analytics, Data Science, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• 5+ years of experience in finance, FP&A, commercial analytics, revenue operations, sales operations, pricing strategy, customer profitability, management consulting, or related analytical disciplines.

• Demonstrated experience developing and managing profitability, cost-to-serve, customer lifetime value (LTV), customer acquisition cost (CAC), contribution margin, or return-on-investment models within a complex business environment.

• Strong understanding of commercial and financial performance metrics, including LTV, CAC, LTV:CAC, payback, retention, gross profit, contribution margin, sales productivity, operating leverage, and return on investment.

• Advanced financial modeling, forecasting, and scenario analysis skills, with the ability to connect operational drivers to revenue, profitability, expense management, and business performance outcomes.

• Advanced Microsoft Excel and Power BI skills required. Experience with CRM, ERP, data warehouse, and planning platforms such as Microsoft Dynamics 365, Salesforce, NetSuite, or Workday Adaptive Planning preferred.

• Experience integrating, reconciling, and analyzing commercial and financial data from multiple systems while establishing governed metrics, controls, and scalable analytical processes.

• Proven ability to identify trends, anomalies, risks, and opportunities within complex datasets and translate findings into actionable business recommendations.

• Ability to challenge assumptions constructively through fact-based analysis and provide objective recommendations that influence planning, forecasting, investment, and go-to-market decisions.

• Strong business acumen and executive presence, with the ability to build effective partnerships across Sales, Finance, Revenue Operations, business units, and senior leadership.

• Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, including the ability to communicate complex financial and analytical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.

• Experience within a technology, value-added reseller (VAR), distribution, managed services, professional services, or other multi-solution commercial environment preferred.

Actual salary will be based on a variety of factors, including location, experience, skill set, performance, licensure and certification, and business needs. The range for this position in other geographic locations may differ. Certain positions may also be eligible for variable incentive compensation, such as bonuses or commissions, that is not included in the base salary.

Our Commitment

We’re committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where everyone feels respected, valued, and empowered to grow. We recognize that embracing diversity drives innovation, improves outcomes, fosters collaboration, boosts teammate satisfaction, and builds a more inclusive culture.
