• Support month-end close activities and other operational accounting initiatives as the company grows

How You’ll Know You’re Succeeding

• Financial records stay organized, current, and reliable because you take pride in getting the details right the first time.

• Reconciliations don't pile up. You catch discrepancies early, investigate them thoroughly, and resolve them before they become larger issues.

• Month-end is smoother because you've kept the day-to-day accounting work organized instead of letting it accumulate.

• Your teammates know they can count on you to keep accounting operations moving. When someone needs documentation, answers, or support, you're responsive, organized, and dependable.

• As Goodwin grows, you help create better processes that make the finance team more efficient and scalable.

What We’re Looking For

jobs.title: Seasonal Chef Instructor, Pastry (Sur La Table)
jobs.description:
With over 58 stores and the largest avocational cooking program in the US, Sur La Table offers an unsurpassed selection of exclusive and premium-quality goods for the kitchen and table – and the culinary expertise and inspiration to go along with it. Whether the job entails interacting with our customers, driving digital growth, or providing vital behind-the-scenes support, we’re all here for the same reason – to roll up our sleeves and create happiness through cooking and sharing good food. 


Position Overview
As a Seasonal Chef Instructor, Pastry at Sur La Table, you are the in-store expert and advocate for all things baking and pastry arts.  You deliver #bestincenter service, a company-wide standard for excellence in service, by sharing specialized knowledge in pastry techniques, baking fundamentals, and personalized instruction that supports all company initiatives. The Seasonal Chef Instructor, Pastry plays a key role in inspiring a love for baking while driving sales of bakeware, mixers, and decorating tools through hands-on pastry classes and engaging culinary instruction.
 
Key Responsibilities
Customer Experience & Brand Representation
·        Represent Sur La Table’s brand and culture by creating memorable, educational experiences that inspire repeat visits and customer loyalty. 
·        Deliver an exceptional in-store culinary experience focused on pastry and baking classes that reflects Sur La Table’s passion for food, teaching, and high standards, while following the provided recipes and game plans to ensure consistency and quality.
·        Communicate technical concepts and advanced pastry skills in a clear, encouraging, and approachable manner.
·        Maintains expertise by staying current on products, actively engaging in available training, and independently seeking out additional resources.
Sales & Business Performance
·        Drive sales by upholding kitchen standards, encouraging second class sign-ups through strong customer engagement, and promoting retail items used or featured in class.
·        Deliver class revenue goals by ensuring high enrollment, positive reviews, and guest return rates.
·        Consistently meet or exceed culinary program goals by delivering exceptional classes that drive customer engagement and sales. Performance is measured by key KPIs such as second-class sign-ups, retail culinary product sales, and guest feedback through Google reviews.
Team Engagement & Store Support
·        Assist in setting up and breakdown of classes including organizing mise en place, prepping ingredients, and cleaning workstations.
·        Clean and sanitize dishes and equipment promptly to ensure smooth kitchen operations.
·        Assist with restocking, organizing, and maintaining kitchen supplies and tools to support overall store readiness.
 
Operations & Compliance
·        Ensure compliance with food safety standards, local health codes, and sanitation regulations.
·        Properly handle all tools, ingredients, and kitchen equipment to maintain a safe and efficient work environment.
·        Maintain accurate inventory levels, minimize shrink, and control supply and culinary expenses.
·        May handle liquor, wine, and beer in compliance with state and location alcohol regulations, company policies, including enforcing age restrictions.
·        Ensure store safety and cleanliness, addressing any maintenance needs promptly.
·        Adhere to applicable wage and hour laws.  Accurately records time worked according to SLT Policy.
·        Model and ensure consistent adherence to all Sur La Table policies and standard operating procedures (SOPs).
 
Physical Requirements
·        Ability to communicate verbally and work cooperatively with associates and customers.
·        Ability to remain standing for up to 4 hours at a time.
·        Ability to move about the store directing class participants while selling to customers and retrieving merchandise from stockroom or sales floor.
·        The capability to accurately perceive and differentiate variations in intensity or quality of flavors or odors, or to identify specific tastes or scents using the tongue or nose.
·        Ability to grab, reach, push, pull, bend, stoop, kneel and crouch to demonstrate, retrieve and/or replenish merchandise and/or cooking equipment.
·        Ability to use hands to seize, hold, grasp, turn, or otherwise to chop, whisk, slice, stir, juice and/or demonstrate other techniques.
·        Ability to lift and/or move merchandise weighing up to 50 lbs.

Qualifications & Experience
·        Must be 21 years of age or older at the time of employment.
·        A degree in culinary arts is preferred; however, candidates with extensive culinary experience and demonstrated technical proficiency will be considered in lieu of formal education.
·        1-2 years of kitchen operations experience.
·        Valid Food Manager Certification.
·        Excellent communication, problem-solving, and decision-making abilities.
·        Passion for community engagement and providing exceptional customer experiences.

jobs.title: Staff/Senior Staff Technical Program Manager, Federal
jobs.location: Seattle, WA or McLean, VA (Preferred) or Remote (USA)
jobs.description:
About Us

Trase is the operating system for high-stakes environments, providing end-to-end solutions for deploying, managing, and optimizing AI within industries where security, governance, and data sovereignty are non-negotiable.

Our HIPAA- and SOC 2-compliant platform bridges the “last mile” of AI adoption, empowering sectors like healthcare and national security to run trustworthy, predictable AI agents across any model or environment—whether in the cloud, on-prem, or at the edge—with unified policy enforcement, continuous monitoring, and fully immutable audit trails.

Trase’s suite of products includes Origin, its agentic operating system; Leagues, its marketplace for specialized, configurable, ready-to-deploy agents; and Arena, where developers build, evaluate, and package the agents that run on Origin. The company has repeatedly topped Hugging Face’s GAIA Leaderboard for Generalized AI Assistants, placing it firmly at the forefront of AI-agent innovation.

About the Role

As a Staff/Senior Staff Technical Program Manager at Trase, you will own technical program execution dedicated to Red Cell Federal (RCF) and Red Cell Partners (RCP) incubations and portfolio companies. You will join Trase's dedicated RCF/RCP support team, with a strong focus on federal, government, and national security programs.

Red Cell Partners is an investment and incubation firm that builds and supports technology companies, including Trase. Red Cell Federal is our federal-focused partner within that ecosystem. This role helps RCF and other RCP partner companies adopt and operate Trase OS in their own environments. You will turn partner requirements into secure, reliable deployments and sustained operational support, with a strong focus on federal, government, and national security programs.

You will work with a dedicated team of full-stack software engineers and DevOps/SRE engineers, partnering closely with Trase Platform Engineering, Product, GRC, and RCF/RCP technical leaders. Your scope spans partner onboarding, integrations, environment readiness, releases, and ongoing support for RCF and RCP portfolio companies.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will drive decisions, resolve dependencies, and hold delivery commitments accountable from initial request through validated customer acceptance.

Scope of Responsibilities

• Own RCF/RCP program delivery: translate ambiguous requests into scoped user stories, acceptance criteria, owners, dependencies, and small, testable milestones. Confirm feasibility with engineers before committing dates.

• Establish a single intake and prioritized backlog with Product and RCF/RCP counterparts. Distinguish production blockers, security obligations, and committed customer needs from exploratory requests; keep partner-facing plans aligned with engineering execution.

• Drive secure deployment readiness across customer-managed cloud, private-network, and on-premises environments. Track infrastructure prerequisites, access, networking, secrets, model-provider integrations, and end-to-end workflow validation.

• Partner with GRC and security owners to incorporate applicable RMF/ATO, STIG, and impact-level requirements into delivery plans. Drive engineering remediation, evidence readiness, and approval dependencies while maintaining clear Trase/RCF/RCP responsibility boundaries.

• Coordinate release and image handoffs, including versioning, compatibility, vulnerability scan results, software bills of materials, release manifests, deployment guides, and rollback readiness. Verify readiness before partner delivery.

• Drive ongoing support for federal deployments, including Second Front where applicable: track patching, hardening, upgrades, security findings, and sustainment commitments with named engineering and GRC owners.

• Coordinate partner issue triage and technical escalations across the dedicated team and shared platform teams. Drive closure of integration, performance, reliability, and observability gaps against agreed acceptance criteria.

• Build repeatable onboarding and operational handoffs through runbooks, architecture and data-flow documentation, training, and knowledge transfer so partner teams can operate and repeat deployments.

• Run planning, grooming, delivery reviews, and risk escalation. Give technical and executive stakeholders clear visibility into commitments, capacity, dependencies, tradeoffs, and decisions; surface reusable partner needs for the core platform roadmap.

Staff / Sr. Staff Expectations

• Staff: independently lead complex RCF/RCP programs across engineering, security, operations, and partner teams; resolve ambiguity and drive measurable delivery and operational outcomes.

• Senior Staff: lead a portfolio of interdependent RCF/RCP programs; shape the engagement and delivery model, influence roadmap and investment tradeoffs with senior leaders, and establish practices that scale across partner deployments.

Required Qualifications

• U.S. citizenship is required. Ability and willingness to obtain and maintain a U.S. government security clearance, as required by assigned programs.

• 8–10+ years of experience in technical program management, engineering, or related technical delivery roles, with demonstrated Staff-level scope; broader multi-program leadership and organizational influence for Sr. Staff.

• Track record of delivering complex software, infrastructure, or platform programs to external customers, including secure or regulated environments.

• Strong technical judgment and experience leading cross-team execution, prioritization, risk management, and customer-facing escalations under ambiguity.

• Clear written and verbal communication with engineers, security specialists, partner teams, and executives, including the ability to challenge unclear requirements and negotiate realistic commitments.

Technical Depth

• Understand distributed systems, APIs, agent workflows, and integration boundaries well enough to inspect technical plans, challenge assumptions, and lead tradeoff discussions.

• Experience with cloud and/or on-premises deployments, containers, Kubernetes, CI/CD, networking, identity/access, and secrets management.

• Working familiarity with secure software delivery, vulnerability remediation, audit logging, observability, and operational readiness.

• Ability to translate security and compliance requirements into engineering deliverables and validation evidence in partnership with GRC.

Strongly Preferred

• Prior TPM experience supporting national security, defense, federal agencies, or other government programs, including work with government customers and delivery partners.

• An active U.S. government security clearance.

• Experience navigating RMF/ATO processes, STIG hardening, POA&M remediation tracking, or DoD IL4/IL5/IL6 environments.

• Experience with Second Front or comparable federal deployment platforms, government cloud environments, and ongoing support of authorized systems.

• Experience supporting AI/ML platforms, agent integrations, or developer tools across multiple partner organizations.

Working Style

• High ownership, sound judgment, and proactive follow-through.

• Comfortable moving between technical detail and executive decisions.

• Practical, collaborative, and focused on customer outcomes and repeatable delivery.

If you want to be on the cutting edge of technology, building AI solutions for the future, and are up for a challenge, let’s talk!

Salary Range: $220,000-260,000. This represents the typical salary range for this position based on experience, skills, and other factors.

#LI-RCP

Our Trase Benefits:

For full-time roles only

• Career track opportunity with potential for rapid advancement with strong performance as the firm grows

• 100% employer paid, comprehensive health care including medical, dental, and vision for you and your family.

• Paid maternity and paternity for 14 weeks at employees' normal pay.

• Unlimited PTO, with management approval.

• Opportunities for professional development and continued learning.

• Optional 401K, FSA, and equity incentives available.

• Mental health benefits are available through Tara Mind.

We’re an Equal Opportunity Employer: You’ll receive consideration for employment without regard to race, sex, color, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, or on the basis of disability.

Applicant Data Disclosure

By submitting an application, you acknowledge that Red Cell Partners, LLC ("Red Cell") uses third-party service providers to facilitate its recruitment and hiring processes. These providers include applicant tracking systems, candidate verification platforms, and fraud detection tools (collectively, "Hiring Platforms"). Your application materials, including your résumé, cover letter, work samples, responses to application questions, and any other information you submit, may be transmitted to and processed by these Hiring Platforms for the following purposes:

• Identifying indicators of potentially fraudulent, fabricated, or materially misleading application content, including but not limited to discrepancies between submitted materials and publicly available professional profiles, geographic anomalies, and fabricated work histories.

Applications that are flagged through this process as containing indicators of fraud or material misrepresentation may be declined from further consideration. If you have questions about the status of your application or the evaluation process, please contact talent@redcellpartners.com.

Red Cell requires its Hiring Platform providers to process your information solely for the purposes described above and in accordance with applicable law. Your information will be retained only for as long as necessary to fulfill these purposes and any applicable legal obligations, after which it will be deleted in accordance with Red Cell's data retention policies.

For more information about how your data is used, please refer to our Privacy Policy and Applicant Privacy Notice.

Retail FT Sales Supervisor at SMCP

Operational Excellence

Who You Are:

• Passionate about fashion, with a keen eye for Parisian chic and luxury retail.

• A natural leader—confident, inspiring, and eager to mentor others.

• A strong communicator—friendly, outgoing, and persuasive.

• Adaptable and flexible with scheduling to meet business needs.

Join a Career That Fits Your Life:

At SMCP, we provide more than just a job—we provide a path to grow, thrive, and be part of something exceptional.

Your talent and dedication are rewarded with competitive base hourly pay, individual commission, and sales incentives. With our 50% shopping discount and seasonal wardrobe offering, you’ll always feel confident in the latest collections—because style starts with you. We also provide a cell phone contribution.

With mentorship and professional development support, plus a dynamic, engaging workplace where your contributions truly matter, you’ll discover a career that’s as fulfilling as it is inspiring.

At SMCP, you’re not just an employee, you’re a valued part of a team that celebrates passion, creativity, and excellence. With a dynamic, engaging workplace and a people-first culture, you’ll find a career that’s as rewarding as it is inspiring.

Ready to lead with confidence and style? Apply today and become part of the SMCP Dream Team!

jobs.title: Manager, Accounting
jobs.description:
About Parabilis Medicines

Parabilis Medicines is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company dedicated to creating extraordinary medicines for patients with serious diseases by unlocking biologically important targets long considered undruggable. The company has pioneered a new class of alpha-helical peptides – Helicons™ – capable of modulating intracellular proteins that have historically been beyond the reach of conventional medicines. The company’s lead investigational medicine, zolucatetide, is the first and only direct inhibitor of the β-catenin:TCF interaction, a central node in the Wnt/β-catenin pathway that has eluded drug developers for decades. Zolucatetide is being evaluated in the clinic across multiple Wnt/β-catenin-driven diseases, including desmoid tumors, familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) and a range of other solid tumor indications. Beyond zolucatetide, Parabilis is advancing additional Helicon-based programs focused on other challenging targets where we believe our medicines could have life-altering impact. For more information, visit www.parabilismed.com or follow us on LinkedIn.

What’s the opportunity?

Parabilis Medicines is seeking a Manager, Accounting, who shares our passion to impact patients by drugging previously undruggable targets, inspires excitement and results in others and has the confidence and credibility to partner with all levels of the organization. The Accounting Manager will report to the Company’s Director of Accounting and will serve as a key contributor across a variety of accounting and finance activities. This role is an ideal opportunity for someone to grow their career in the biotech/life sciences industry.

Key responsibilities include:

• Prepare monthly journal entries, support schedules, account reconciliations, and other analyses covering a range of accounting areas including cash, investments, prepaids, fixed assets, accruals, and leases, among others.

• Prepare and maintain accounting schedules and transaction support related to multiple collaboration arrangements.

• Contribute to quarterly accrual meetings and journal entry preparation.

• Manage assigned responsibilities within the month-end and quarter-end closes, coordinating with the accounting team to ensure accurate and timely completion of all tasks.

• Support the company’s annual tax return filing and reporting processes.

• Execute and maintain internal controls over financial reporting as they relate to relevant functions.

• Assist with accounting/finance process improvements, including proactively identifying opportunities to simplify, standardize, and automate processes.

• Crosstrain on payroll processing and serve as backup equity administrator.

• Assist with ad hoc projects and initiatives as required.

• Collaborate with all finance team members and colleagues from other departments to support accurate financial reporting and effective accounting operations.

What you’ll need to be successful:

• Bachelor’s degree or higher in accounting or related area.

• 5+ years of relevant experience, preferably in public and/or biopharmaceutical company.

• CPA preferred.

• Extremely well-organized and goal-oriented, with the ability to deliver high-quality results on time and under tight deadlines.

• Willingness to be responsible for and perform tasks over a relatively wide spectrum; “roll-up-your-sleeves” attitude.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with exceptional attention to detail and the ability to identify inconsistencies, investigate issues, and develop practical solutions

• Exceptional work ethic and unquestionable integrity.

• Experience with NetSuite/Concur/ADP/FloQast is a plus.

• Excellent Excel and other Microsoft Office application skills.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

• Ability to utilize AI tools for day-to-day work; baseline proficiency is expected, and advanced or innovative use of AI is a strong plus.

• Able to work on-site and attend in-person meetings.

Core Values

Parabilis Medicines is a team of passionate pioneers who are trailblazing the future of precision medicine with the aim of making a meaningful difference in the lives of patients. The company is committed to promoting an inspiring and flourishing working environment for all employees across the business, in all departments, and driving innovation for patient benefit.

• Growth-Minded. We’re inventing a new class of medicines—one applicable to therapeutic targets that have been dreamt about, but always considered impossible to drug. Our work requires us to be curious, humble and adaptable.

• In(ter)dependent. We are fiercely independent as a leader in defying the limitations of current therapeutic modalities, and interdependent as a team as we work collaboratively to shift drug discovery paradigms and provide patients with better treatment options.

• Patient-focused. We are deeply focused on patient outcomes, and all energy in the company is focused on science as it translates to patient impact.

• All-In. We’re All-In on solving some of the hardest scientific challenges and delivering one of the most effective new classes of drugs in history.

The base salary range for this position is $125,000-$135,000, depending on experience, qualifications, and internal practices. Parabilis’s total compensation package also includes an annual target bonus, equity, and a comprehensive suite of competitive benefits designed to support our employees’ overall well-being.

As an equal opportunity employer, Parabilis Medicines values an inclusive workplace and welcomes applicants of all backgrounds and experiences. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other factors prohibited by law.

30 Acorn Park Drive    |     Cambridge, MA 02140    |    www.parabilismed.com

jobs.title: Technical Writer
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Alembic is the pioneering Causal AI platform. We help the world's largest enterprises move past correlation to prove what actually drives business outcomes — the question marketing and growth teams have never been able to answer with confidence. Fortune 100 companies including Nvidia, Delta Air Lines, and Mars use Alembic to make multimillion-dollar decisions on trusted, causal evidence.

We're backed by a $145M Series B from WndrCo (founded by Jeffrey Katzenberg), Jensen Huang, Joe Montana, Prysm Capital, and Accenture. Our models run on our own NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD built on Grace Blackwell infrastructure — one of the fastest private supercomputers in the world. (We've melted GPUs getting here.)




ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring a Technical Writer to build the single source of truth for Alembic's science. Our founder and CEO, the inventor behind our core technology, and our Chief Science Officer have produced years of research notes, testing and verification programs, and technical analyses. That work is spread across dozens of documents, and the links between them mostly live in their heads. You'll organize it into a verified, connected knowledge base the whole company can query and trust, run the internal peer review that every external technical claim passes through, and turn the strongest material into white papers and a technical blog.

We'll measure success by how much easier it becomes to find and trust what we know: fewer documents, each one canonical, sourced, and current. This role is onsite in San Francisco and reports to our Chief Science Officer, working day to day with our CEO and closely with Product, Engineering, and Customer Success.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Inventory our existing research and technical documents, map how they relate, and decide what is canonical, what is superseded, and what is missing.

 - Build and maintain Alembic's internal knowledge base in Google Workspace, including an AI layer (Gemini and NotebookLM) grounded in curated sources, so answers come back with citations to the documents behind them.

 - Run internal peer review for external technical content and LLM-assisted drafts: trace each claim to a source, flag what can't be traced, and route open questions to the right scientist.

 - Assess the external research we build on: summarize each paper's claims, known critiques, and open debates, and how our position holds up against them.

 - Launch and run Alembic's technical publishing, including blog posts, white papers, and articles drawn from existing material and cleared through review.

 - Extend the knowledge base into customer-facing documentation and training materials with Product and Customer Success.


WHAT WILL HELP YOU SUCCEED

 - 4+ years writing or editing technical or scientific material professionally, ideally in AI, data, research, or another field where accuracy gets checked.

 - Quantitative literacy: you can read a machine learning, statistics, or physics paper, explain its assumptions, and say where it is weakest.

 - Experience building a knowledge base, wiki, or documentation system out of scattered material, including taxonomy, naming, and upkeep.

 - Fluency with LLM tools, paired with the discipline to verify every claim they produce against a source.

 - The confidence to question a founder or scientist when a claim isn't supported, and the tact to keep that conversation productive.

 - Experience with an editorial or peer-review process (journal, research organization, medical or regulatory writing, or a docs team with formal review).

 - Published technical writing such as white papers, technical blog posts, or long-form articles.

 - Comfort with diagrams, process flows, Markdown, and docs-as-code tools; Python or scripting is a plus.

 - Familiarity with causal inference, experimentation, or marketing measurement is a plus.


THE ROLE IS RIGHT FOR YOU IF:

 - You've taken a scientist's scattered work and made it usable by an entire company, and you want to do that alongside the inventor of the technology.

 - You care more about whether a sentence is true than about how many sentences you shipped this week.




WHY YOU MIGHT BE EXCITED ABOUT ALEMBIC

 - In the room with the inventor: You'll work directly with our founder and CEO and our Chief Science Officer on next-generation attribution models grounded in mathematical physics.

 - Build the foundation: You'll define how Alembic stores, reviews, and publishes what it knows, from the knowledge architecture and review standard to the technical blog.

 - A science story with proof behind it: Causal AI running on our own NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD on Grace Blackwell infrastructure, one of the fastest private supercomputers in the world.

 - Accuracy that matters: Fortune 100 companies including Nvidia, Delta Air Lines, and Mars make multimillion-dollar decisions on this work.

 - Series B momentum, real ownership: Meaningful equity at a Series B company that's raised $145M, with proven product-market fit and Fortune 100 traction.




WHY YOU MIGHT NOT BE EXCITED

 - You measure your output in pages published. Here, merging three overlapping documents into one may be your best work of the week.

 - You want a finished style guide, toolchain, and review process on day one. You'll build them.

 - You prefer writing from finished specs to sitting with a scientist, interrogating rough notes, and pushing back when a claim isn't supported.

jobs.title: Source Selection and Acquisition Strategy Specialist
jobs.description:
Company Overview:

ANSER enhances national and homeland security by strengthening public institutions. We provide thought leadership for complex issues through independent analysis, and we deliver practical, useful solutions. ANSER values collaboration, integrity, and initiative and we are client focused in all that we do. Because we were established for the purpose of public service and not for profit, we measure our success in the impact of our service.

Position Overview

ANSER is seeking an experienced Source Selection and Acquisition Strategy Specialist to provide senior-level acquisition planning, source selection, and procurement strategy support to U.S. Space Force organizations.

In this role, you will support Government contracting officers and program leadership in developing and evaluating acquisition strategies, analyzing complex procurement requirements, and recommending effective source selection and negotiation approaches. You will apply Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) requirements, assess acquisition alternatives, and develop actionable recommendations that address cost, schedule, performance, and contracting risks. This position plays a key role in supporting compliant, efficient, and mission-aligned Government acquisitions throughout the procurement life cycle.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

• Develop, evaluate, and recommend acquisition strategies aligned with program objectives, mission requirements, Federal acquisition regulations, and Government procurement policies.

• Provide source selection and acquisition strategy support throughout the procurement life cycle, including requirements development, acquisition planning, solicitation, evaluation, negotiation, and award.

• Analyze complex acquisition requirements and apply analytical and evaluative techniques to develop innovative, effective, and efficient procurement approaches.

• Advise Government contracting officers on procurement methods, solicitation structures, contract types, competition strategies, and acquisition risks.

• Apply FAR Parts 8.4, 12, 13, 15, and 16.505 to support acquisition planning, solicitation development, source selection, and task and delivery order competitions.

• Develop and evaluate negotiation strategies for complex procurement actions, including sole-source acquisitions and negotiations involving cost, delivery schedules, performance requirements, and contractual terms.

• Recommend approaches to resolve negotiation challenges, reduce costs, adjust delivery schedules, improve contractual terms, and achieve favorable acquisition outcomes.

• Evaluate acquisition alternatives, market research, contractor capabilities, procurement methods, and cost and schedule considerations to inform Government acquisition decisions.

• Develop and review acquisition plans, source selection documentation, evaluation criteria, solicitation materials, negotiation objectives, and supporting award documentation.

• Support source selection processes that promote fairness, consistency, appropriate competition, and compliance with applicable acquisition requirements.

• Analyze technical, financial, schedule, performance, and contractual information to identify procurement risks, capability gaps, and opportunities for improvement.

• Collaborate with Government contracting officers, program managers, technical subject-matter experts, legal counsel, financial analysts, and other stakeholders to coordinate acquisition strategies and resolve procurement challenges.

• Prepare executive-level briefings, decision memoranda, reports, and recommendations communicating acquisition alternatives, negotiation considerations, and procurement risks.

• Review acquisition documentation for accuracy, completeness, regulatory compliance, and alignment with program objectives.

jobs.title: Nursing Faculty - Phoenix
jobs.description:
Empower the next generation of nurses. Inspire future healthcare leaders.

At Chamberlain University, our faculty are more than educators, they're mentors, scholars, and advocates for student success. As a Nursing Faculty member, you will play a vital role in shaping future healthcare professionals through high-quality teaching in the classroom, clinical, lab, and simulation environments, including flexible evening and weekend instruction.

This on-campus role offers the opportunity to make a meaningful impact through teaching, coaching, scholarship, service, and collaboration while supporting Chamberlain's mission to educate, empower, and transform healthcare.

What You'll Do

Deliver Exceptional Nursing Education

• Teach assigned nursing courses across classroom, clinical, laboratory, and simulation settings.
• Create engaging, student-centered learning experiences using innovative teaching strategies, technology, and evidence-based practices.
• Implement course curriculum and contribute feedback to support continuous course improvement.
• Bridge theory and practice to prepare students for safe, ethical, and professional nursing practice.

Support Student Success

• Build meaningful relationships with students and foster an inclusive, supportive learning environment.
• Evaluate student performance and provide timely, constructive feedback.
• Identify learning needs and develop remediation strategies that help students achieve academic success.
• Serve as a mentor and professional role model throughout the student journey.

Lead Clinical Excellence

• Facilitate clinical, laboratory, and simulation learning experiences.
• Collaborate with fellow faculty to ensure students develop the knowledge, critical thinking, and clinical competencies needed for practice readiness.
• Promote patient safety, evidence-based care, and professional standards in all learning environments.

Contribute to the Academic Community

• Participate in university committees, program evaluation activities, accreditation efforts, commencement ceremonies, and other professional service initiatives.
• Support the onboarding, development, and mentoring of new faculty members.
• Collaborate with colleagues and academic leaders to strengthen program outcomes and student experiences.

Advance Scholarship & Professional Growth

• Engage in scholarly and professional activities that advance nursing education and practice.
• Research, apply, and share emerging knowledge and best practices.
• Maintain clinical expertise, subject matter knowledge, and teaching effectiveness through ongoing professional development.

Ensure Academic & Regulatory Excellence

• Follow and enforce university policies related to attendance, grading, assessments, and student conduct.
• Maintain compliance with accreditation, licensure, regulatory, and institutional standards.
• Utilize technology, data, and AI-enabled tools to enhance teaching effectiveness and student outcomes.

What Makes a Successful Chamberlain Faculty Member?

Our faculty thrive when they:

• Put students first and proactively remove barriers to student success.
• Align their work with Chamberlain's mission, vision, and strategic priorities.
• Use feedback, data, and continuous improvement practices to enhance outcomes.
• Build strong partnerships with colleagues, leaders, and external stakeholders.
• Demonstrate accountability, integrity, collaboration, and respect.
• Embrace innovation and contribute to a culture of excellence.

What Success Looks Like

Successful faculty members consistently:

• Support strong student achievement, including NCLEX performance and other key academic success indicators.
• Foster student engagement and satisfaction, reflected in course evaluations and Net Promoter Scores (NPS).
• Deliver timely, accurate, and meaningful grading and feedback.
• Meet all accreditation, regulatory, and licensure requirements.
• Utilize technology and innovative teaching methods to improve learning outcomes.
• Contribute to scholarship, professional service, and academic leadership initiatives.
• Embody Chamberlain's values, culture, and leadership behaviors in all interactions.

Performs other duties as assigned and complies with all university policies, procedures, and standards.

Education

• Master's Degree in Nursing required

Nursing & Clinical Experience

• Minimum of 2 years of professional nursing experience related to the teaching discipline required
• Demonstrated clinical nursing expertise and experience in the specialty area(s) being taught
• Experientially prepared to teach assigned nursing courses
• Maintain current regulatory and clinical practice credentials, when appropriate, based on assignment
• Maintain appropriate, active, unencumbered nursing licensure or certification as required to practice and teach within the discipline required
• Ability to integrate clinical expertise, evidence-based practice, and real-world healthcare experiences into the learning environment

Teaching & Student Success Competencies

• Excellent communication skills, sound judgment, and a high level of initiative
• Ability to create engaging learning environments and effectively manage conflict
• Emotional and social intelligence to recognize student needs, respond with empathy, and foster a supportive, inclusive learning environment
• Commitment to student-centered learning and academic excellence

Technology & Innovation

• Technological expertise with learning management systems, simulation equipment, and online learning platforms
• Increasing ability to effectively leverage technology, data, and AI tools to support teaching and learning
• Collaboration & Relationship Building
• Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with faculty colleagues, Extended Service Team partners, and clinical partners
• Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to build productive relationships across diverse stakeholder groups

Scholarship Requirements

• Demonstrates scholarship congruent with faculty rank. Scholarship activities must:
• Be made public
• Be open to critical review and evaluation by knowledgeable peers
• Be accessible for exchange and use by others
• Faculty at the Instructor rank are required to demonstrate at least one example of professional development and scholarship within one of the following areas:
• Scholarship of Discovery
• Scholarship of Integration
• Scholarship of Practice/Application
• Scholarship of Teaching and Learning

Compliance & Additional Requirements

• Please refer to the state-specific addendum for any additional requirements needed to teach within your designated specialty.
• Education and experience must align with applicable state regulations.
• Faculty teaching in clinical settings must meet all additional requirements outlined in the Faculty Compliance Packet.

Actual pay will be adjusted based on job-related factors permitted by law, such as experience and training; geographic location; licensure and certifications; market factors; departmental budgets; and responsibility. • Health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance

jobs.title: Contracts Administrator
jobs.description:
Company Overview:

ANSER enhances national and homeland security by strengthening public institutions. We provide thought leadership for complex issues through independent analysis, and we deliver practical, useful solutions. ANSER values collaboration, integrity, and initiative and we are client focused in all that we do. Because we were established for the purpose of public service and not for profit, we measure our success in the impact of our service.

Position Overview

ANSER is seeking an experienced Contracts Administrator to provide senior-level government contracting expertise in support of U.S. Space Force mission requirements.

In this role, you will manage complex government contracts and subcontracts, providing expertise in contract negotiation, administration, compliance, and risk management. You will serve as a trusted advisor to Government and program leadership, evaluating contractual terms, performance requirements, costs, and delivery schedules while ensuring compliance with applicable regulations and contractual obligations. The ideal candidate brings extensive government contracting experience, strong business judgment, and the ability to independently navigate complex contractual challenges in a highly regulated, mission-focused environment.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

• Prepare, review, negotiate, and administer complex government contracts, subcontracts, modifications, and related contractual agreements throughout the contract life cycle.

• Ensure contracting activities comply with applicable laws, Government regulations, organizational policies, customer requirements, and contractual obligations.

• Evaluate contract terms and conditions, cost estimates, performance requirements, and delivery schedules to assess accuracy, feasibility, compliance, and potential risks.

• Advise Government and program leadership on contractual rights, obligations, risk exposure, interpretation of terms and conditions, and potential impacts to program execution.

• Identify and resolve complex contractual issues, ambiguities, and inconsistencies; develop recommendations and risk mitigation strategies.

• Support proposal development, pricing evaluations, contract negotiations, modifications, and other acquisition-related activities.

• Monitor contract performance, deliverables, schedules, modifications, and compliance requirements to support successful contract execution.

• Collaborate with program management, finance, procurement, legal counsel, technical teams, and other stakeholders to address contractual challenges and support mission objectives.

• Interpret and apply Government contracting regulations, acquisition requirements, and organizational policies to contract administration and compliance activities.

• Develop and recommend improvements to contracting policies, procedures, and processes to enhance operational effectiveness, consistency, and regulatory compliance.

• Provide guidance on contract administration practices, contractual requirements, and process improvements across assigned organizational functions.

• Maintain accurate and complete contract files, correspondence, records, and supporting documentation in accordance with applicable requirements.

• Independently manage complex contracting assignments, establish priorities, and provide timely analysis and recommendations to support leadership decisions.

Required Qualifications

• Active Top Secret security clearance with SCI eligibility (TS/SCI).

• Bachelor's degree or higher from an accredited college or university, with one of the following combinations of education and relevant professional experience:

• Bachelor's degree (BA/BS) and 10 or more years of relevant experience.

• Master's degree (MA/MS) and 8 or more years of relevant experience.

• Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) or Juris Doctor (JD) and 2 or more years of relevant experience.

• Demonstrated experience in government contracting, contract negotiation, contract administration, subcontract management, or a closely related discipline.

• Extensive knowledge of Government contracting regulations, acquisition requirements, contractual compliance, and contract life-cycle management.

• Experience preparing, negotiating, and administering government contracts and subcontracts in accordance with applicable regulations, organizational policies, and customer requirements.

• Experience evaluating contractual terms, cost estimates, performance requirements, and delivery schedules to identify risks and ensure contractual accuracy and completeness.

• Demonstrated ability to interpret complex contract terms and conditions and advise leadership on contractual rights, obligations, and business impacts.

• Experience identifying and resolving complex contractual issues, assessing proposed modifications, and developing appropriate risk mitigation strategies.

• Experience developing, recommending, and implementing contracting policies, procedures, and process improvements across organizational functions.

• Proven ability to collaborate with program management, finance, procurement, legal, and technical stakeholders to resolve contractual challenges.

• Strong analytical, negotiation, problem-solving, and decision-making skills, with the ability to exercise independent judgment on complex contracting matters.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex contractual information and recommendations to senior leadership.

• Ability to manage competing priorities, work independently, and deliver high-quality results in a fast-paced, mission-focused environment.

• Independently manage assigned acquisition activities, respond to leadership taskings, and deliver timely, accurate products in support of mission requirements.

Required Qualifications

• Active Top Secret security clearance with SCI eligibility (TS/SCI).

• Bachelor's degree or higher from an accredited college or university in management, business, economics, finance, accounting, mathematics, science, technology, engineering, statistics, or a related field.

• Minimum of 15 years of relevant professional experience, including significant experience supporting military or national security space programs.

• Demonstrated experience supporting program management, business management, acquisition, or operations activities for complex Government programs.

• Comprehensive knowledge of DoD acquisition processes, including acquisition planning, program execution, requirements management, and program oversight.

• Understanding of mission-critical aspects of military space launch, ground systems, and sustainment programs.

• Experience leading and executing complex projects, managing workflow taskings, and analyzing and synthesizing large volumes of acquisition and program data.

• Knowledge of Higher Headquarters, Department of the Air Force, and U.S. Space Force policies, processes, and procedures applicable to acquisition and program management.

• Proficiency with Government acquisition, cost, requirements, and reporting tools, including Cost and Requirements System (C&RS), MAR reporting software, Microsoft Office Suite, and Task Management Tool (TMT).

• Demonstrated ability to independently execute assigned acquisition and program management responsibilities with minimal supervision.

• Ability to effectively communicate using appropriate DoD, Air Force, and Space Force acquisition terminology in written reports, presentations, and leadership engagements.

• Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to assess complex acquisition challenges and develop actionable recommendations.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience preparing and delivering briefings to senior Government leadership.

• Ability to manage competing priorities, collaborate across multidisciplinary teams, and deliver high-quality results in a fast-paced, mission-focused environment.

jobs.title: Enterprise SSD Development Project Manager - Contract (3-month contract-to-hire)
jobs.description:
** Please note: Professional proficiency in Korean is required for this role. **

About the Company

At SK hynix memory solutions, we're at the forefront of semiconductor innovation, developing advanced memory solutions that power everything from smartphones to data centers. As a global leader in NAND flash technology and memory solutions, we drive the evolution of advancing mobile technology, empowering cloud computing, and pioneering future technologies. Our cutting-edge memory technologies are essential in today's most advanced electronic devices and IT infrastructure, enabling enhanced performance and user experiences across the digital landscape.

We're looking for innovative minds to join our mission of shaping the future of technology. At SK hynix memory solutions, you'll be part of a team that's pioneering breakthrough memory solutions while maintaining a strong commitment to sustainability. We're not just adapting to technological change – we're driving it, with significant investments in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and eco-friendly solutions and operational practices. As we continue to expand our market presence and push the boundaries of what's possible in semiconductor technology, we invite you to be part of our journey to creating the next generation of memory solutions that will define the future of computing.

About the Team:

The Enterprise SSD Development Project Manager will deliver value to customers by leading enterprise SSD development at SKHMS A (SK hynix memory solutions America).

We are looking for project manager to work with enterprise SSD development which requires cross-functional and multi-site collaboration.

Responsibilities:

• In this role, you will work closely with development managers, engineers, and multi-functional partners in Hardware, Firmware, Operation and customer facing teams.

• Development and management of project schedule and work, along with managing the associated tasks and dependencies to ensure we are on track for the program achievements.

• Participate in key design reviews and handle scope changes efficiently. Identify project dependencies, risks and bring up to leadership in a timely manner.

• Provide status updates and communicate issues internally providing recommendation as a key part of team.

• Working closely with Korea HQ engineering and manufacturing teams.

Minimum Qualifications:

• At least 2 years of relevant experience in project management or SSD product development; 4–6 years preferred.

• Ability to manage the full Enterprise SSD development lifecycle, including product planning, prototype builds, development, validation, qualification/certification, and technical discussions with customers.

• Foundational understanding of hardware operation, including SSD architecture, NAND, DRAM, and NAND storage firmware.

• Understanding of product development processes and ability to track, coordinate, and drive resolution of development issues.

• Bilingual in Korean and English, with professional working proficiency in both languages, to facilitate communication between headquarters and the local engineering subsidiary.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Technical knowledge of Solid State Drive (eSSDs) and/ or SoC, HW and FW

• Customer facing experience

COMPENSATION: $80,000/yr - $133,000/yr

REGARDING COMPENSATION:

SK hynix memory solutions America Inc. offers you the opportunity to apply your skills to exciting projects while working with innovative teams. Our compensation package is complimented by a generous benefits package including medical, dental, vision, life insurance and a company 401(k) match, as well as cafeteria, onsite gym and much more. If you are motivated by technical challenges, we offer a collaborative work environment that encourages career growth.

The salary offered to a selected candidate will be tailored based on several factors, including the location, job grade, relevant knowledge, skills, and experience. We also take into account the internal equity among our current team members to ensure fairness and competitiveness.

• 1+ years of direct paid search client management including paid search strategy development, execution & client relationship management

• Passion for crunching numbers, analyzing data, and navigating Excel/Google sheet spreadsheets

• Possess high attention to detail and be able to execute with a high degree of accuracy

• Performance Max experience is a must

• You are a communication guru both on calls and through written communication

• ‘Driven’ and ‘Innovative’ are attributes commonly associated with you

• Highly collaborative & works well with a team

• 4-year college degree or equivalent work experience

#LI-OG1 #LI-Remote

Benefits

• Work-life balance with an emphasis on personal well-being

• Career growth in a disruptor space & entrepreneurial opportunities within the Monks network

Finally, Monks achieved a record-breaking number of FWAs and continues to hold the most of any partner.

Including fresh voices and unique points of view in all aspects of our business not only creates an environment where we can all grow and thrive but also increases our potential to produce work that better represents—and resonates with—the world around us.

jobs.title: Counsel, Product
jobs.description:
Perplexity is AI for people who expect more. More accuracy. More agency. More signal, less noise. Our answer engine handles hundreds of millions of queries every month for people whose questions spark change and whose decisions bend the world toward progress.

Our legal team works side by side with product and business teams. We help the company move quickly, make sound risk decisions, and build legal requirements into products and operations from the start.



About the Opportunity

We are looking for a practical, versatile attorney to join our Product, Privacy and Regulatory Legal team. You will have a clear center of gravity in consumer protection and a flexible mandate across product counseling, privacy, regulatory matters, marketing, subscriptions, and international expansion.

This is not a narrow subject matter role. You might advise on a new consumer product flow one day, assess an advertising or subscription practice the next, and help respond to a regulator or customer escalation after that. You will work directly with Product, Engineering, Growth, Marketing, Support, Security, GRC, Policy, and Communications.

The right person can identify the legal issue quickly, learn the product deeply, and give the business a practical path forward. You will own matters independently and help turn recurring questions into clear guidance and durable systems. This role Reports to the Senior Director, Product, Privacy and Regulatory Legal.



What You Will Do

 - Serve as a primary legal partner for consumer products and features from early design through launch and post-launch review

 - Advise on consumer protection issues, including unfair and deceptive practices, disclosures, pricing, subscriptions, renewals, refunds, promotions, advertising claims, dark patterns, and customer support practices

 - Review marketing, growth, and advertising initiatives, including adtech and martech integrations, audience practices, email and messaging campaigns, and product claims

 - Counsel product and engineering teams on privacy, data use, consent, retention, security, AI transparency, age-related protections, and other legal requirements

 - Lead legal review of cross-functional launches and translate complex requirements into practical product and operational choices

 - Support responses to consumer complaints, state attorneys general, competition authorities, privacy authorities, and other regulators around the world, in partnership with the regulatory lead and outside counsel

 - Assess incidents and escalations that cross product, privacy, consumer protection, contractual, and regulatory lines

 - Monitor legal developments affecting AI products and online services, then convert them into clear advice, playbooks, and product requirements

 - Help build scalable legal infrastructure, including templates, review standards, decision records, training, and self-service guidance

 - Flex across the broader Product, Privacy and Regulatory Legal portfolio as company priorities and risk change



What We Are Looking For

 - J.D. from an accredited law school, or an LL.M. or equivalent law degree, and current authorization to practice law in the U.S. state where you are located

 - At least five years of relevant legal experience at a law firm, government agency, or in house, with meaningful consumer protection or product counseling experience

 - Strong command of U.S. consumer protection law and enforcement principles, including Section 5 of the FTC Act and state unfair or deceptive acts and practices (UDAP) laws

 - Experience with several of the following areas: subscriptions and auto-renewal, advertising and marketing, privacy and data protection, payments, promotions, platform regulation, or AI governance

 - Ability to lead a product or regulatory matter independently, from fact development through recommendation and execution

 - Excellent judgment. You know what to decide, what to escalate, and how to explain risk without slowing the business unnecessarily

 - Clear, direct writing and the ability to translate legal requirements for product, engineering, and business teams

 - Comfort learning technical systems and asking precise questions about how products, data flows, and controls actually work

 - Hands-on attitude, low ego, intellectual curiosity, and comfort with ambiguity in a fast-moving environment

 - Genuine interest in AI products and the legal questions created by how people use them

Bonus

 - Experience at the FTC, a state attorney general's office, or another consumer protection or privacy regulator

 - In-house experience at a consumer technology company, online platform, marketplace, or subscription business

 - Experience handling regulator inquiries, investigations, or consumer class action risk

 - Working knowledge of the CCPA/CPRA, GDPR, state privacy laws, ROSCA, CAN-SPAM, TCPA, COPPA, state auto-renewal laws, or similar international consumer regimes

jobs.title: Acquisition Manager / DAG Chief
jobs.description:
Company Overview:

ANSER enhances national and homeland security by strengthening public institutions. We provide thought leadership for complex issues through independent analysis, and we deliver practical, useful solutions. ANSER values collaboration, integrity, and initiative and we are client focused in all that we do. Because we were established for the purpose of public service and not for profit, we measure our success in the impact of our service.

Position Overview

ANSER is seeking an experienced Acquisition Manager / DAG Chief to provide senior-level acquisition management and advisory support to the Space Systems Command (SSC), Space Domain Awareness and Combat Power (SSC/SZ). In this role, you will support Government leadership in managing and aligning acquisition strategies, resources, requirements, funding, contracts, and program milestones across a complex portfolio of classified and unclassified space programs. You will serve as a trusted advisor, providing strategic analysis, actionable recommendations, and cross-functional coordination to support program execution, resolve acquisition challenges, and inform senior leadership decisions.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

• Advise SSC/SZ leadership and program managers on acquisition strategy, planning, execution, and portfolio management across complex space programs.

• Assess and recommend alignment of acquisition activities, manpower, funding, requirements, and program objectives to support mission priorities.

• Develop, maintain, and analyze acquisition forecasts, including current and future contract actions, program milestones, key decision points, and execution risks.

• Identify acquisition gaps, schedule risks, integration challenges, and program execution issues; develop recommendations and coordinate resolution with Government stakeholders and mission partners.

• Support the development, review, coordination, and execution of acquisition strategies, requirements documentation, and program management plans throughout the acquisition life cycle.

• Integrate force design considerations, operational imperatives, combatant command priorities, and future force requirements into acquisition planning and recommendations.

• Evaluate cost, schedule, performance, funding, contracting, and requirements tradeoffs to inform Government acquisition decisions.

• Coordinate acquisition and sustainment activities across SSC organizations, Government agencies, contractors, and mission partners to promote program alignment and execution.

• Support integrated product teams, working groups, program management reviews, and other cross-functional acquisition forums.

• Assist with authorized source-selection support activities, including acquisition documentation, source-selection plans, acquisition strategies, and proposal evaluation materials.

• Prepare executive-level briefings, reports, analyses, decision packages, and correspondence for senior Government leadership.

• Support high-visibility acquisition initiatives, leadership engagements, congressional-level activities, and time-sensitive Government taskings.

• Provide acquisition management and advisory support throughout the program life cycle, from initial planning and development through execution, transition, and sustainment.

Required Qualifications

• Active Top Secret security clearance with SCI eligibility (TS/SCI).

• Master's degree (MA/MS) from an accredited college or university.

• Minimum of 20 years of relevant professional experience, including significant experience supporting military or national security space programs.

• PMT 4010 Certificate (or predecessor course), demonstrating qualification to support DoD ACAT I and II acquisition programs.

• Demonstrated experience supporting complex Department of Defense (DoD) acquisition programs, preferably ACAT I and II programs within the space domain.

• Extensive knowledge of DoD acquisition processes, acquisition strategy development, program execution, requirements management, and life-cycle sustainment.

• Proficiency with DoD acquisition, cost, requirements, and reporting tools, including Cost and Requirements System (C&RS), MAR reporting software, Microsoft Office Suite, and Task Management Tool (TMT).

• Demonstrated ability to integrate cost, schedule, performance, funding, contracting, and requirements information to assess program risks and support acquisition decisions.

• Experience developing, reviewing, and coordinating acquisition strategies, program documentation, executive briefings, analytical reports, and decision-support materials.

• Proven ability to collaborate with senior Government officials, program managers, contractors, and mission partners to identify challenges, evaluate impacts, and coordinate solutions.

• Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including experience preparing and presenting complex acquisition information to senior Government leadership.

• Ability to manage competing priorities, exercise sound judgment, and deliver high-quality work in a fast-paced, collaborative environment supporting classified space acquisition programs.

Individual salaries are determined by a variety of factors including but not limited to: business considerations, local market, internal equity, candidate qualifications such as skills, education and experience. jobs.title: Staff Product Manager, Brand Success
jobs.location: New York City, NY; San Francisco, CA
jobs.description:
About Faire

Faire is a technology wholesale platform built on the belief that the future is local. Independent retailers around the globe collectively represent a multi-hundred-billion-dollar wholesale market that has historically been fragmented and offline. At Faire, we're using the power of tech, data, and machine learning to connect this thriving community of entrepreneurs across the globe. Picture your favorite boutique in town — we help them discover the best products from around the world to sell in their stores. With the right tools and insights, we believe that we can level the playing field so businesses can grow and local communities can thrive.

We’re looking for smart, resourceful and passionate people to join us as we power the shop local movement. If you believe in community, come join ours.

About this role

You’ll own making sure all brands can succeed on Faire, whether they are just starting out or driving millions a year. Faire has a robust suite of programs and tools that help brands grow, and when brands take our guidance, they grow measurably faster - driving top actions is worth an estimated 15-30% increase in brand lifetime value. The catch is that today, most guidance comes from calls with account managers, and brands have no reliable way to discover or act on it themselves: our notifications, nudges, and emails deliver disjointed advice, don’t give sufficient context, and aren’t personalized to what matters most for a given brand’s shop setup and goals.

Your job is to build a system that can score a brand’s shop, measure the value of potential actions, identify the top opportunities, and communicate those to our brands at the right time and in a compelling way. You’ll work closely with the pods that built the programs to deeply understand the mechanics and the adoption blockers, and with our Success, Product Marketing, and Sales teams to deliver an omnichannel strategy for driving adoption.

If you love figuring out what makes users successful, building systems that change behavior, working across product and GTM teams, and you get excited about creating real, measurable value for small business owners, this is the role for you.

What you'll do

• Set the strategy for brand success. Deeply understand which behaviors make brands successful on Faire, what blocks brands from adopting them, and where guidance should come from product versus a person.

• Own the brand success roadmap end-to-end. Define strategy and sequencing across rebuilding key systems, shipping contextual nudges, and deep-diving into top actions.

• Go deep on the highest-value actions. Understand blockers, build education and reasons to believe, determine contextual moments to target, and make each action as close to one click as possible, starting with what new brands need in their first 30 days.

• Build the targeting and triggering system. Estimate the LTV impact of each action, rank each brand's personalized top opportunities, and fire on the behavioral moments when a brand is most likely to act.

• Own the growth hub and rationalize our nudge systems. Give brands a single place to see what is limiting their growth and their top actions, and consolidate today's banners, emails and in-portal prompts into one prioritized system that other pods contribute to.

• Partner with GTM. Work with Success, Marketing, and Sales to learn what works in the human-led motion, bring it into product, and ensure our account managers and the self-serve system complement each other. Define a long-term OS between the teams, and drive alignment on the type of actions that belong in-product vs. should remain human-led.

Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.

• You have 8+ years of experience in product at a high-growth tech startup, as a startup founder, or in a top tech company.

• You have set direction in an ambiguous space, not just executed a roadmap you inherited. You can decide what's worth working on and explain why.

• You are good at deeply understanding customer needs and underlying motivations, especially in spaces where customers aren't great at predicting how changes will impact their behavior.

• You work well across teams. You've aligned other product teams and go-to-market partners on shared systems.

• You are analytically rigorous. You define the right metrics, design experiments, and know the difference between adoption you caused and adoption that would have happened anyway.

• You're an inspiring leader who is excited about the day-to-day of understanding our customers and working with a strong team to build improvements for them.

• You're an extraordinarily fast learner. You have the natural curiosity and intellectual horsepower to deeply understand new topics and pick up new skills in a very short time.

• You are relentlessly resourceful. When something needs to get done, you always find a way to make it happen. Even when the work is hard, you power through it and execute with limited information and ambiguity.

• You are a creative problem-solver. You excel at identifying unintuitive solutions to tough problems.

• You are passionate. You are optimistic with a positive energy that other people draw upon.

• You care deeply about developing products and solutions that will create the best experience for our customers.

Salary Range

San Francisco, CA/New York City, NY: The pay range for this role is $220,000 - $302,500 per year.

This role will also be eligible for equity and benefits. Actual base pay will be determined based on permissible factors, including transferable skills, work experience, market demand, and primary work location. The base pay range provided is subject to change and may be modified in the future.

Hybrid Faire employees currently go into the office 3 days per week on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and a third flex day of their choosing (Monday, Wednesday, or Friday). Additionally, hybrid in-office roles will have the flexibility to work remotely up to 4 weeks per year. Specific Workplace and Information Technology positions may require onsite attendance 5 days per week as will be indicated in the job posting.

Why you’ll love working at Faire

• Flexible paid time off, plus company-wide recharge days

• Paid parental leave up to 16 weeks

• Comprehensive health coverage, with options varying by location

• Fertility and family-building benefits through Carrot, including a lifetime reimbursement allowance

• Mental health support and coaching through Modern Health

• Stipends to support your professional development, wellness, and work from home needs

• Employer-sponsored retirement plan, dependent on country of employment

Faire was founded in 2017 by a team of early product and engineering leads from Square. We’re backed by some of the top investors in retail and tech including: Y Combinator, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Forerunner Ventures, Khosla Ventures, Sequoia Capital, Founders Fund, and DST Global. We have headquarters in San Francisco and Kitchener-Waterloo, and a global employee presence across offices in Toronto, London, and New York. SR. COUNSEL, DATACENTER DEVELOPMENT & INFRASTRUCTURE

• Provide expert legal guidance on matters related to developing large-scale datacenter infrastructure and supporting utilities — acquisition and development of land, construction of datacenters and associated facilities, on-site power generation (including gas turbines and backup systems), electrical transmission and distribution infrastructure, gas pipelines and fuel supply systems, water supply and wastewater treatment (especially for high-density cooling), communications/fiber infrastructure, transportation access, and worker accommodations. This role also supports spaceport and other advanced critical infrastructure development projects as needed

• Draft and negotiate land purchases, easements (including power line, gas pipeline, and utility rights-of-way), rights-of-way, leases, power purchase agreements (PPAs), interconnection agreements, fuel supply contracts, pipeline capacity agreements, and other real estate and commercial transaction documents required to bring datacenter and infrastructure projects fully online

• Advise on municipal, county, State, and Federal requirements related to zoning, building and construction permitting, environmental reviews, power generation and utility interconnections, gas pipeline development and safety, water rights and wastewater treatment, air permitting for turbines/generation, and related infrastructure for datacenters and large industrial projects

• Collaborate with internal stakeholders to brief county, State, and Federal regulators on applicable matters, including public utility commissions, environmental agencies, pipeline safety regulators, and permitting authorities

• Negotiate complex construction contracts, engineering-procurement-construction (EPC) agreements, vendor and supply contracts related to datacenter buildout, power generation facilities (turbines, substations, switchgear), utility infrastructure (gas pipelines, high-voltage power lines, water systems), fuel procurement and delivery, and spaceport development

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• JD or foreign equivalent from an ABA-accredited law school

• Active licensed attorney

• 7+ years of legal experience

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• 7+ years of experience with real estate, land use, and/or large-scale power and utility infrastructure development issues, preferably including hyperscale datacenter or major industrial project development

• Knowledge and/or experience with natural gas project development, power generation contracts and operations (including on-site turbine generation), gas pipeline and fuel supply agreements, power purchase agreements (PPAs), utility interconnection processes, transmission planning, and mineral rights or surface use agreements

• Familiarity with Texas regulatory environment, including Public Utility Commission requirements, Texas Railroad Commission rules for oil and gas operations, and air/water permitting for power generation facilities is highly desirable

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

• Must be admitted to the bar, in good standing, in at least one U.S. state

• Willingness to travel occasionally to project sites and different offices for a week at a time

• Must be willing to work extended hours and/or weekends as needed

• This position is based in Bastrop, TX and requires being onsite – remote work not considered

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

• To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

CORE JOB DUTIES

REQUIRED EXPERIENCE, EDUCATION AND SKILLS
