jobs.title: Team Lead
jobs.description:
Career Team is a leading workforce development organization on a mission to transform lives.  We blend cutting-edge technology with compassionate, high-touch services to drive real, measurable outcomes in the lives of job seekers across the country.  At Career Team, we’re solving today’s unemployment challenges with smart software, world-class trainers, dedicated case managers, dynamic job developers, and innovative partners. If you're passionate about making a difference and believe in the power of technology to transform lives, you’ll feel right at home here.

TITLE: Team Lead

REPORTS TO: Executive Director

LOCATION: Merced, CA

EMPLOYMENT TYPE: Full-Time, Exempt Employee

Career TEAM is looking to hire a dynamic Team Lead to support and lead a team of Career Advisors serving WIOA Adult and Dislocated Workers and Unemployed Job Seeker customers and connect them to high-quality jobs across Merced County, CA. Work will be performed under the WIOA (Workforce Innovation Opportunity Act) Program underneath the WorkSource umbrella in Atwater, Los Banos in Merced County. The Team Lead will be responsible for providing oversight and coaching to the Career Advisors, approving enrollment applications and funding requests for training and support services, assessing caseload shape and report out monthly, training in case management activities related to the WIOA program design, and assisting with day-to-day operations of the Career Advisors.

This position is expected to be 100% onsite. The selected candidate will be required to work onsite at the listed location.

The Team Lead is an integral part of our team and will assist us with our mission of accelerating the human condition! If you have the heart to serve this community and the drive to do so, we want to meet you. Experience is not mandatory; however, character is.

Career Team also offers a competitive package including:

• 401k with a generous employer match;

• Medical, dental, and vision insurance with an employee-sponsored HSA on any qualifying plans;

• Disability insurance;

• Supplemental insurance

Your Impact on Career TEAM’s Success:

• Oversee a team of Career Advisors staff who work in an integrated service delivery model.

• Assess, manage, and maintain a caseload of new customers as well as carryover participants, track customers’ progress in training and job search activities on a monthly basis. Case notes all interactions with customers.

• Develop and implement casework service plans for complex cases and assist Career Advisors to remove customer barriers.

• Develops and implements strategies to incorporate a focus on performance objectives in the daily operations of organizational staff.

• Helps drive customer success and positive outcomes for contractual measures.

• Provides training and career coaching on assessments to help establish career goals aligned with the skill needs of area business and industry.

• Prepares and presents reports of activities and accomplishments.

• Build strong partnerships with community organizations to provide outreach and engagement for local WIOA programs.

• Support Career Advisors who work in the community to ensure connectivity and strong partnerships.

• Ensure compliance and data tracking metrics for outreach and funding source initiatives.

• Provide staff development, coaching and training to the team.

• Generate and perform staff evaluations.

• Provide leadership and direction to maximize performance forecasting and to ensure financial sustainability and success.

• Work in partnership with quality assurance and leadership team to build processes and team cultural understanding.

• Support Executive Director in day-to-day operations, program development, and staff development.

• Approach each day and task with a “ZAG” mindset.

• Other duties and projects as needed.

The Ideal Qualifications for this Position Include:

• Associate’s degree or higher or an equivalent combination of education and experience required;

• Experience and knowledge of WIOA and workforce development contracts/programs

• Ability to give presentations and workshops (public speaking)

• Demonstrated ability to be highly detail oriented in order to successfully meet program requirements.

• One year of experience working with unemployed and underemployed individuals

• Exceptional time management skills to meet deadlines and work under pressure.

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills

• A Valid Driver’s License

Salary: $63,000–$65,000 annually

Travel: Position may require local travel up to 40% of the time.

Employment Type: Full-Time, Non-Exempt

About Career Team:
Founded in 1996, Career Team, LLC is a private workforce development organization.

Career Team’s outstanding record of building the modern infrastructure powering America's workforce has resulted in numerous honors:

• Named by Inc. Magazine as one of America's 500 fastest growing privately held companies

• Recipient of the US Chamber of Commerce Blue Chip Enterprise Award for innovation

• Featured by 60 Minutes, CNN, Money Magazine, Inc. Magazine and the British Broadcasting Network as an innovative, government funded solutions program

• Invited to the White House after being cited by the National Welfare-to-Work Partnership and National Alliance of Business as a top 10 US training provider

As a socially conscious organization, Career Team has found a healthy balance between for-profit innovation and community enrichment. Looking ahead, the organization will continue to close the nation’s opportunity divide with additional government-funded workforce sites; while also building staff capacity of workforce funding sources and industry providers. See www.careerteam.com for more information.

Career Team is an Equal Opportunity Employer.  All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, or national origin.

Background Check Requirements. Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a background check (including criminal, prior employment and education verification). Failure to satisfactorily complete the background check may affect the application status of applicants or continued employment of current employees who apply for the position.

California Consumer Privacy Act ("CCPA").  Career Team is committed to complying with the CCPA and all data privacy and laws in the jurisdictions in which it recruits and hires employees. Career Team collects and uses Personal Information for human resources, employment, benefits administration, health and safety, and business-related purposes and to be in legal compliance. Below are the categories of Personal Information we collect and the purposes for which we intend to use this information:

Identifying information, such as your full name, gender, date of birth, and signature; Demographic data, such as race, ethnic origin, marital status, disability, and veteran or military status; Contact information, such as your home address, telephone numbers, email addresses, and emergency contact information; Dependent's or other individual's information, such as their full name, address, date of birth, and Social Security numbers (SSN); National identifiers, such as SSN, passport and visa information, and immigration status and documentation; Educational and professional background, such as your work history, academic and professional qualifications, educational records, references, and interview notes; Employment details, such as your job title, position, hire dates, compensation, performance and disciplinary records, and vacation and sick leave records; Financial information, such as banking details, tax information, payroll information, and withholdings; Health and Safety information, such as health conditions (if relevant to your employment), job restrictions, workplace illness and injury information, and health insurance policy information; Information Systems (IS) information, such as your search history, browsing history, login information, and IP addresses on the Company's information systems and networks; Biometric information, such as facial recognition, fingerprints, iris or retina scans, keystroke, or other physical patterns; and Geolocation data, such as time and physical location related to use of an internet website, application, device, or physical access to a Company office location.

The Company collects Personal Information to use or disclose as appropriate to:

(1) Comply with all applicable laws and regulations; (2) Recruit and evaluate job applicants and candidates for employment; (3) Conduct background checks; (4) Manage your employment relationship with us, including for: (a) onboarding processes; (b) timekeeping, payroll, and expense report administration; (c) employee benefits administration; (d) employee training and development requirements; (d) the creation, maintenance, and security of your online employee accounts; (e) reaching your emergency contacts when needed, such as when you are not reachable or are injured or ill; (f) workers' compensation claims management; (g) employee job performance, including goals and performance reviews, promotions, discipline, and termination; and (h) other human resources purposes; (5) Manage and monitor employee access to company facilities, equipment, and systems; (6) Conduct internal audits and workplace investigations; (7) Investigate and enforce compliance with and potential breaches of Company policies and procedures; (8) Engage in corporate transactions requiring review of employee records, such as for evaluating potential mergers and acquisitions of the Company; (9) Maintain commercial insurance policies and coverages, including for workers' compensation and other liability insurance; (10) Perform workforce analytics, data analytics, and benchmarking; (11) Administer and maintain the Company's operations, including for safety purposes; (12) For client marketing purposes; (13) Exercise or defend the legal rights of the Company and its employees, and affiliates, customers, contractors, and agents; and (14) to comply with requirements of government grants, including, but not limited to, program and audit requirements.

jobs.title: Sr. Firmware Engineer II
jobs.description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

Samsara's AI has helped prevent accidents that would have harmed an estimated 380,000 people per year. Every model we ship runs in the real world, on real roads, protecting real drivers. Every Samsara dash cam, gateway, and industrial sensor runs AI at the edge. These models detect distracted driving, prevent collisions, and keep workers safe, all in real time on constrained hardware.

You will lead the development and deployment of next-generation intelligent safety features and video processing by integrating high-performance camera systems and real-time edge computing into Samsara’s fleet and industrial products. In addition, you will help execute the technical strategy, cross-functional relationships, and operational cadence required to launch low-latency, high-quality hardware programs at scale.

We build AI-first, using AI tools to develop, test, and ship features to customers quickly.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role.

Scale: Millions of AI dash cams, 100B+ miles/year (~99% of U.S. roads), 25T+ data points

You should apply if:

• You want to impact the industries that run our world: The software, firmware, and hardware you build will result in real-world impact – helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.

• You are a life-long learner: We have ambitious goals. Every Samsarian has a growth mindset as we work with a wide range of technologies, challenges, and customers that push us to learn on the go.

• You believe customers are more than a number: Samsara engineers enjoy a rare closeness to the end user and you will have the opportunity to participate in customer interviews, collaborate with customer success and product managers, and use metrics to ensure our work is translating into better customer outcomes.

• You are a team player: Working on our Samsara Engineering teams requires a mix of independent effort and collaboration. Motivated by our mission, we’re all racing toward our connected operations vision, and we intend to win – together.

In this role, you will:

• Influence a team of engineers on our Video-Safety products, solving complex technical problems, guiding architectural decisions, improving quality, and owning key aspects of our tech stack.

• Assume ownership in maintaining the production systems managed by your team and provide operational support and supervision when necessary.

• Participate in roadmap planning sessions, collaborating with cross functional peers to define key areas of our roadmap and the technical direction and priorities for Safety products, including tooling and release infrastructure, automated test strategy.

• We operate significant AI algorithms on the edge, and you will play a key role ensuring their accuracy and that they run within the constraints of the devices.

• Partner closely with our Hardware, backend, and ML team in defining and building next generation devices that can support the company’s objectives.

• Mentor other engineers on the team, helping us raise our technical standards.

• Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices.

Minimum requirements for the role:

• 8+ years of relevant experience in embedded software development, preferably with a focus on embedded Linux systems.

• Strong experience in programming with Golang, C/C++, Rust, or similar.

• Strong experience with media pipelines, multimedia frameworks and deploying CV/ML models on edge devices in real-world applications.

• Proven experience defining and implementing scalable embedded software architecture.

• Proven experience planning, designing, scoping and delivering complex, multi-team, or cross-system long-term projects, involving external dependencies.

• A desire to mentor and grow engineers of all levels.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work with senior executives as well as junior engineers.

• Commitment to rigorous testing & validation practices.

• Experience working with teams across multiple disciplines, including but not limited to Product Management, Cloud Software, Machine Learning, and Hardware.

An ideal candidate also has:

• Experience working on products from concept to mass production.

• Proficiency in gstreamer, Google MediaPipe, or similar edge AI/Media frameworks.

• Experience with data analysis using tools such as Databricks, SQL queries, Tableau.

• Experience with one or more of the following technologies: Edge Camera Systems, Video Capture, Video Encoding, Embedded AI.

• Familiarity with a diverse set of quality/testing practices, continuous integration tooling, etc.

• Bachelors or Masters degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering or equivalent field.

The compensation range shown spans approved pay zones for this role. Your primary work location determines the range applicable to you, which may be narrower than the full range displayed.

The range of annual base salary for full-time employees for this position is below. Please note that base pay offered may vary depending on factors including your city of residence, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. This role is also eligible for an initial RSU grant with no vesting cliff, and ongoing refresh opportunities tied to performance, subject to plan terms and conditions. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.

Annual Base Salary

$154,700—$260,000 USD

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email accessibleinterviewing@samsara.com or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

Fraudulent Employment Offers

Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in @samsara.com, @us-greenhouse-mail.io or @mail3.guide.co. For more information regarding fraudulent employment offers, please visit our blog post here.

jobs.title: Real Estate Accounting Manager
jobs.description:
Why AIR?

At AIR Communities, we're building more than apartment communities. We're building careers.

As a Blackstone portfolio company, AIR Communities combines the stability and resources of a globally recognized investment organization with the entrepreneurial environment of a growing real estate company. You'll have the opportunity to learn from experienced professionals, contribute meaningful work from day one, and gain exposure to a sophisticated real estate accounting environment.

What sets us apart:

• Opportunity to grow your accounting career within a respected real estate organization
• Exposure to corporate accounting, debt management, financial reporting, and analysis
• Collaborative, supportive team culture focused on development and mentorship
• Fast-paced environment where your contributions matter
• Work alongside talented professionals who are passionate about excellence
• Strong focus on professional growth and continuous learning

What You Will Do

• Lead a team of property accountants, providing guidance, insight, and opportunity for growth and development.
• Manage accounting and financial analyses in one or more financial areas including auditing, budgeting, cost accounting, general accounting, and program cost control and scheduling.
• Be a driving resource to improve processes and communicate policies and procedures to team and other departments.
• Applying advanced accounting concepts, theories and principals to develop solutions to problems. Adhering to FASB guidelines and GAAP, company policies and procedures and other regulations in the performance of duties.
• Setting department and staff goals based on overall department or company goals.
• Providing advice as subject matter expert in the development of accounting software and property operating systems.
• Supervising assigned staff including hiring, training, overseeing and reviewing performance, promoting and terminating or reassigning.
• Performing technical reviews of complex joint venture accounting transactions, including drafting and finalizing Accounting whitepapers.
• Assisting with quarterly and annual technical accounting analyses.
• Assisting the reporting team during quarter end (as needed)
• Representing the Accounting team as the primary contact for explaining current period actual results to outside teams (FP&A, Operations Finance, etc.)
• Leading complex Corporate accounting functions including accruals, debt, equity, and cash flows.
• Assisting with monthly and quarterly fluctuation analyses and prepare key deliverables for Management team.
• Performing SOX control procedures, including performing walkthroughs and providing relevant information to internal and external auditors.

Keys to Success:

• Leader: You lead by example, possess a clear vision, have humility and like help people reach their goals
• Detail Oriented: You are consistently accurate, have an eye for detail and would always spot an error.
• Nimble Problem Solver: You proactively call out problems, while also providing recommendations and solutions. You are optimistic and say "Yes!" to finding an answer.
• Team Focused: You help team members see the importance of what they are doing. You provide guidance when needed, and have a track record of developing others; providing both constructive feedback and encouragement.
• Energized and Resilient: You are optimistic and display a positive attitude. You're determined and maintain composure under stress.
• Winner: You are driven and want to be known for your best work and working for a winning team. You are someone who wants to make an impact!

• Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field and hold a CPA.
• 6+ years of experience with complex accounting, GAAP and regulatory accounting, budgeting and financial management. Experience related to cost allocations and elimination entries highly preferred.
• Proven success with managing a team of finance professionals through ambiguity while still driving results.
• Prior experiencing working in Real Estate or Public Accounting (Big 4) industries is highly preferred.
• Confident communicator with the level of maturity and presence necessary to influence senior executives and business leaders.
• Thrives on driving innovation and change that will propel the business forward.
• Consistently practices strategic thinking and nimble problem-solving tactics to stay ahead of business priorities.

Ready to Build Your Career?

If you're looking for an opportunity to join a high-performing team, learn from talented professionals, and build a strong foundation for a long-term accounting career, we encourage you to apply.

At AIR Communities, we're looking for motivated individuals who are eager to grow, take on new challenges, and make a meaningful impact from day one.

What We Offer:

AIR offers attractive total compensation packages designed to recognize and reward performance including:

• Expected pay rate of $120,000- $140,000 plus annual target bonus. You will be provided a pay rate that is in line with your skills and experience as they relate to the requirements of the job.
• 25% Rent Discount at any AIR community (a rental application is required, and certain exclusions apply).
• Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance options, HSA/FSA plans, short and long-term disability paid by the company.
• 401(k) plan with employer contribution up to 6%.
• Paid time off including vacation, sick time, and 14 holidays.
• Paid parental leave of up to 16 weeks.
• Tuition assistance program and up to 100% reimbursement for job-related certifications and licenses.
• 15 hours of paid time annually for community service.
• Commuter benefits and pet insurance.
• Consumer discounts on various products and services.
• Opportunities for ongoing professional development, leadership training, and career growth.

What You Need to Know

Application Deadline: The initial deadline for applications is 11/11/2026. Applications submitted after this date may still be considered on a rolling basis until the position/program is filled. We encourage all interested candidates to apply as early as possible. If a final decision has not been made by the initial deadline, subsequent applications will be reviewed as they are received.

Candidates extended an offer will be required to undergo pre-employment screening that includes checking references, a four-panel drug screening that excludes marijuana testing, employment verification & criminal background check.

AIR values diversity and provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment. AIR prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

jobs.title: Facilities Operations Leader
jobs.description:
About Stitch Fix, Inc.

Stitch Fix (NASDAQ: SFIX) Stitch Fix is redefining retail by combining human creativity with advanced data science and Generative AI. As we build the future of personalized shopping, we’re equally committed to building yours.  We believe in investing in our team as much as our technology. Join us to be a trendsetter in the industry and help us redefine what’s possible for our clients, while we help you reach your full potential.

About the Role

At Stitch Fix, our Fulfillment Center teams power a personalized styling experience that helps clients feel confident and seen. The Facilities Operations team (FacOps) is responsible for maintaining the equipment, systems, and infrastructure that keep our fulfillment operations running safely and efficiently. As a Facilities Operations Leader, you will lead maintenance and facilities operations across the site, ensuring equipment reliability, operational uptime, and a safe working environment for employees. This role partners closely with Operations, Safety, Supply Chain, and external vendors to support business continuity, drive continuous improvement, and develop a high-performing maintenance team.

Responsibilities

• Develop a culture of safety and maintenance excellence within the facilities and maintenance team.

• Oversee maintenance, automation, and facility operations to ensure equipment reliability, infrastructure readiness, and business continuity

• Prioritize maintenance resources, vendor management, and operational needs to balance safety, service, cost, and productivity goals.

• Provide strategic oversight of third-party vendor partnerships, ensuring adherence to contractual obligations, service-level agreements, and operational standards. Drive financial accountability by managing vendor spend against budget, evaluating performance metrics, and partnering with vendors to optimize cost, service quality, and operational effectiveness.

• Partner with Operations, Safety, and cross-functional leaders to resolve complex issues, improve processes, and support fulfillment center performance

• Utilize root cause analysis and data to solve problems, identify trends, improve reliability, and drive continuous improvement initiatives

• Lead a cross functional equipment performance team to drive productivity and eliminate waste in our automated processes.

• Create preventative maintenance plans and audit task completion to ensure the reliability of our equipment.

• Manage a spare parts and supplies system that utilizes data and a risk evaluation to optimize local inventories.

• Manage service vendors and negotiate equipment service contracts.

• Implement a technical skills development program for our technicians. Provide on-the-job training and coaching to support team development and growth.

• Be available for or delegate weekend and after-hours on-call support.

How Tools and Technology Show Up in Your Day-to-Day Work

• Management and administration of the network computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) to prioritize work, monitor performance, manage spare parts, and drive decision-making

• Analyze equipment, maintenance, and operational data to identify trends, improve reliability, and support continuous improvement efforts

• Use AI-enabled tools and technology to improve communication, planning, problem-solving, and operational efficiency

• Learn and apply new technologies, systems, and automation tools that support fulfillment center operations and facilities management

• Leverage predictive maintenance methods and analytics, such as infrared thermography, vibration analysis, and ultrasonic detection.

About You

Requirements

• Previous leadership or supervisory experience in a maintenance, facilities, engineering, manufacturing, distribution, or warehouse environment

• Experience leading teams in a fast-paced operational setting with a strong focus on safety, reliability, and performance

• Knowledge of preventative maintenance programs, equipment reliability, and facilities operations

• Experience managing multiple priorities, projects, and operational issues simultaneously

• Strong problem-solving, communication, coaching, and collaboration skills

• Experience working with contractors, vendors, and external service providers

• Ability to analyze operational data and use insights to drive business decisions

• Proficiency with maintenance systems, reporting tools, and Google Workspace applications

Nice to Have

• Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Facilities Management, Industrial Technology, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience

• Experience leading maintenance operations in a fulfillment center, distribution center, manufacturing facility, or highly automated environment

• Experience with computerized maintenance management systems (CMMS), enterprise asset management (EAM) platforms, or related technologies

• Knowledge of material handling equipment, conveyors, HVAC systems, electrical systems, or automated warehouse technologies

• Experience supporting continuous improvement, reliability-centered maintenance, or Lean operational initiatives

• Professional certifications related to facilities, maintenance, engineering, safety, or project management

Compensation and Benefits

This role will receive a competitive salary, benefits, and equity. The salary for US-based employees hired into this role will be aligned with the range below, which includes our three geographic areas. A variety of factors are considered when determining someone’s compensation–including a candidate’s professional background, experience, location, and performance.This position is eligible for new hire and ongoing grants of restricted stock units depending on employee and company performance. In addition, the position is eligible for medical, dental, vision, and other benefits. Applicants should apply via our internal or external careers site.

Salary Range

$71,300—$95,000 USD

jobs.title: Strategic Finance & Business Operations Lead
jobs.description:
Blossom Health exists to solve the mental health epidemic in America by partnering with psychiatrists to expand access to affordable, timely, clinically-effective mental healthcare. Our AI-native care platform is loved by hundreds of clinicians and tens of thousands of patients.

We’re a Series A company with $20M+ raised from Headline, Village Global, and the founders of General Catalyst, Flatiron Health, Sword Health, Fay, Elemy, Zip, Blank Street, Assured, Bridge, Birches Health, and Enzo Health.

 


THE ROLE:

We’re looking for a Strategic Finance & Business Operations Lead to own the financial and analytical work behind some of Blossom’s most important business decisions and revenue drivers.

This is not a generic BizOps role. You’ll spend a significant amount of your time digging into the economics of the business: understanding our revenue structure, building financial models, evaluating new opportunities, and turning complex financial and operational data into decisions. You'll also directly own key commercial aspects of the business including relationships and workflows with health insurance payors and other strategic counterparties.

You’ll report directly to our Founder and work closely with leaders across the company as we scale.

 


WHY YOU SHOULD WORK HERE:

 - 🚀 Be early in a hyper-growth startup: Join the foundational team of a rapidly scaling company and help build the financial and operational infrastructure behind our next stage of growth

 - 📈 Work on decisions that matter: Your analysis won’t live in a deck. You’ll help answer questions that directly influence how we grow, where we invest, and how we build the business

 - 🤝 High trust and autonomy: Own meaningful work from day one, with the freedom to shape how problems are approached and solved

 - 🧠 Talent-dense team: Work alongside a top-percentile team with high standards, intellectual curiosity, and a shared ambition to build something consequential

 - 🏃 We move with speed and purpose: We value people who can move quickly, get deep into the details, and turn analysis into action


WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Own financial analysis and modeling across revenue, growth, unit economics, and strategic initiatives

 - Develop a deep understanding of Blossom’s revenue structure and identify opportunities to improve the economics of the business

 - Build models and analyses that inform company-level decisions around growth, investment, resource allocation, and new opportunities

 - Partner with the Founder and business leaders on high-priority strategic and operational projects

 - Translate complex financial and operational data into clear recommendations and actionable decisions

 - Build reporting, forecasting, and analytical processes as the company scales

 - Evaluate new business opportunities, partnerships, markets, and strategic initiatives from both a financial and operational perspective

 - Move beyond the analysis and execute on the opportunities you identify


YOU'LL BE A GOOD FIT IF:

 - You have 2–6 years of professional experience, with a strong foundation in finance and financial analysis

 - You have experience in investment banking, equity research, private equity, hedge funds, or another rigorous investing/financial environment

 - You’re exceptionally strong in financial modeling and comfortable getting deep into revenue structures, unit economics, and business performance

 - You have a track record of outperforming in highly selective, demanding environments

 - You can take a complicated or ambiguous question, structure it quickly, and arrive at a thoughtful answer

 - You’re commercially minded. You care about what the numbers actually mean for the business, not just producing the analysis

 - You have a strong bias for action and are excited to operate beyond the traditional boundaries of a finance role

 - You communicate clearly and can turn detailed analysis into a compelling recommendation

 - You’re excited by the opportunity to work directly with a Founder and take on increasingly broad ownership as the company grows

 - You’re authorized to work in the United States

 - You’re excited to be in-person in New York City 5 days a week

Bonus: You’ve spent several years in investment banking or another rigorous finance environment and have since moved into strategic finance, business operations, or a similar role at a high-growth startup.

 


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR:

 - Highly motivated, ambitious, and capable - you want to tackle large, meaningful problems and hold yourself to a high bar

 - Ownership mindset - you think long-term and put the business and our customers first

 - High velocity and high excellence - you move with urgency without sacrificing the quality of your work

 - Analytically rigorous - you’re comfortable going several layers deeper than the obvious answer

 - Commercially curious - you want to understand how and why a business works, not just report what happened

 - An explorer - you’re comfortable with ambiguity, autonomy, and questions that don’t have an existing playbook

 - Humble - you use your strengths in service of the team and understand that success is an output, not an input


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS:

 - $120,000–$180,000 base salary

 - Meaningful equity ownership

 - Significant growth opportunities as the company scales

 - Beautiful, sunshine and snack-filled office in the heart of Flatiron, Manhattan

 - Health, dental, and vision insurance

 - A focus on outcomes, not hours

 - Team outings, offsites, and unlimited PTO

jobs.title: Demand Generation Manager
jobs.description:
Documo is on a mission to help businesses digitize and streamline their document workflows. As a fast-growing B2B SaaS company, our platform makes it easier to handle unstructured files like faxes and forms through tools like Intelligent Document Processing - turning messy paperwork into structured, usable data. We believe great products start with great people. That’s why we invest in top talent, value strong culture, and prioritize customer success and design excellence.

If you’re excited to do impactful work and want to grow with a team that values innovation, collaboration, and purpose - we’d love to meet you!

About Documo

Documo helps healthcare organizations turn information into action. Referrals, records, and authorizations still arrive as faxes and forms, and someone has to read, sort, and key in every page. We automate that manual document work. Our platform combines HIPAA-compliant cloud fax, Direct Secure Messaging, and AI-powered document and workflow automation, so critical work moves faster and care teams get time back for patients.

We’re a small team, so everyone has real ownership and can see the impact of their work. We hire people who care about customers, sweat the details, and want to build something that matters in healthcare. If that sounds like you, we’d love to meet you.

The role

This is a pipeline generation role. You will decide who we target, when, why and with what message, then run integrated campaigns that carry that plan across our channels. Those channels include BDR outreach, events, LinkedIn and social, partner marketing, marketplaces, review sites, email, the website and paid media.

The job is campaign strategy and execution, not just channel management. You will need enough digital skill to work hands-on across web, email, social and paid, and you will help manage our paid media agency. You will work daily with the BDR team and sales, and with content, product marketing and SEO. Your ultimate KPI is pipeline.

What you'll own

Integrated and account-based campaigns

• Own the integrated campaign calendar: one theme and offer per campaign, sequenced across outbound, website, events, email, LinkedIn, paid media (with our agency) and content.

• Build and run our ABM program with sales: target account list, tiers (1:1 for top enterprise accounts, 1:few clusters by EHR or segment, 1:many for the broader ICP), and a play for each tier.

• Launch a go-to-market campaign for each new EHR integration: buy and enrich lists of that EHR's customers, target the right ICP titles and specialties, and brief content on EHR-specific messaging and assets.

• Build automated sales enablement that gives BDRs and AEs timely reasons to reach out to prospects and open opportunities, such as intent signals, EHR and technology fit, hiring, funding and event attendance.

• Brief content, product marketing and web on the assets and landing pages each campaign needs.

• Track engagement and pipeline at the account and buying-group level, not just leads.

BDR programs and outbound campaigns

• Be marketing's partner to the BDR manager: you build the lists and messaging, they run the team and the daily outreach. You work side by side on what each segment needs.

• Build target segments by ICP, EHR, specialty, organization size and buying trigger, with sales and the BDR manager.

• Source, enrich and maintain prospect lists using Salesforce, HubSpot, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, enrichment tools and intent data; keep data clean and routed.

• Write messaging and multi-touch sequences (email, phone, LinkedIn) for each segment with the BDR manager; test, measure and retire what doesn't book meetings.

• Run campaign sprints with the BDRs: account lists, talk tracks, offers and event follow-up plays.

• Report weekly on meetings booked, meeting-to-opportunity conversion and pipeline by segment.

Inbound lead programs

• Work with the website manager on campaign offers and CTAs, so each campaign's landing experience matches its segment and message.

• Run nurture for leads that aren't ready to buy, and track MQL-to-SQL-to-pipeline conversion with sales.

Events

• Own pipeline generation for every event on our calendar: industry shows such as HIMSS, EHR and partner events such as PointClickCare, and category events. Event selection, logistics and booth setup are run by our Content Marketing Manager.

• Before the show: build target attendee and account lists, and run pre-event outreach with the BDRs to book meetings.

• At the show: staff the booth, run booked meetings and capture leads (roughly 25% travel).

• After the show: run follow-up sequences with the BDRs within days, and track meetings and opportunities to close.

• Report meetings, pipeline and cost per meeting for each event, and recommend which events to keep, add or drop.

Paid media partnership

• Help manage our paid search and paid social agency: shape campaign ideas, set targeting and offers, and review results against pipeline.

• Align paid retargeting and ABM audiences with outbound and event target lists.

Reviews, marketplaces, partner marketing and LinkedIn

• Own our G2 profile and presence on other review sites (Capterra, TrustRadius, KLAS where relevant); keep listings, categories and screenshots current.

• Run an always-on review program with CS and sales: ask timing, incentives and quarterly targets; use reviews in campaigns and sales materials.

• Manage marketplace listings with EHR and technology partners and keep them generating leads. Support partner marketing with those partners: co-branded campaigns, joint webinars and partner events, and partner lead follow-up with the BDRs.

• Use LinkedIn (company page, Sales Navigator, employee and executive posting, events) as a pipeline channel, not just an awareness channel.

How we'll measure success

Pipeline is the measure that matters. Supporting indicators:

• Marketing-sourced and influenced pipeline against target, by campaign, segment and channel.

• Engagement, meetings and pipeline in target ABM accounts.

• Meetings and sales-accepted opportunities from BDR outreach, events and inbound, including MQL-to-SQL conversion.

• Pipeline per dollar for each event and campaign.

• Review count, rating and G2 category position, and leads from marketplaces, partners and LinkedIn.

What you bring

• 4–6 years in B2B SaaS marketing with direct ownership of field/event marketing and outbound or SDR programs.

• A record of running integrated, multi-channel and account-based campaigns, and of building lists and messaging that measurably increased meetings and pipeline.

• Hands-on with Salesforce and HubSpot. Required: building and enriching lists with LinkedIn Sales Navigator and data or enrichment tools such as Seamless.AI, ZoomInfo, Clay or Apollo.

• Experience driving pipeline from trade shows: pre-show outreach, booth work and post-show follow-up.

• A collaborative working style: you will share ownership of outbound with a BDR manager and must work well as a peer. Clear, concise writing for outbound email, LinkedIn and event invites.

• Comfort using AI tools to speed up research, list work and copy testing.

• Digital marketing fluency across web, email, social and paid, and comfort reporting on pipeline, not just activity.

Bonus points

• Healthcare, health IT or EHR-ecosystem experience (HIMSS, EHR user groups, KLAS).

• Experience running a G2 or review program.

• Experience with partner or app marketplaces.

The annual base salary range for this remote, US-based role is $110,000.00 to $120,000.00 USD. Actual compensation within this range will depend on relevant experience, skills, and qualifications, with consideration for internal equity.

In addition to base salary, this role offers bonus potential and benefits.

Why join Documo?

• Competitive U.S. benefits: medical, dental, vision, and a 401(k) with a strong match.

• Annual bonus program based on role and company performance.

• Annual performance reviews with merit increases.

• In-person company kick-off to connect, collaborate, and celebrate.

• Equity opportunities to grow with us.

• Flexible remote work that fits your life, plus flexible paid time off.

• Competitive paid parental leave, mental health support, and Employee Assistance Programs (EAP).

• Be part of a small, fast-growing tech company with a supportive, inclusive, and fun culture.

We celebrate differences.
Documo welcomes applicants from all backgrounds, especially those underrepresented in tech. We do not discriminate based on ancestry, race, place of origin, political belief, religion, marital or family status, physical or mental ability, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, or any other legally protected characteristic. Documo is an equal opportunity employer.

jobs.title: Lot Assistant - ADESA Tracy
jobs.description:
Pay range: $19.50-$20 hourly

Schedule: Monday - Friday between 7:00am-5:00pm (8 hours per day)

About Us

ADESA, a Carvana-owned company, currently operates in over 50 locations throughout the US. Our auto auctions, some up to 200 acres, provide a wide array of vehicle services, including repair, reconditioning, and auction remarketing, and many of our sites serve as market hub distribution centers. Our inventory comprises hundreds of thousands of vehicles across North America, from retail to commercial, OEM & more.

We work in a service industry and embrace a “we” versus “I” culture – help others, and they will help you. Our industry is fun, fast-paced, and competitive – and filled with the best people who are passionate about what they do.

We’re excited about the future! As an industry leader, ADESA is poised for a multi-year expansion, including huge investments in facilities, massive sales growth, and an ever-increasing inventory of vehicles! We are looking for great people who want to take this journey with us! Get a sneak peek into life at ADESA!

Role and Team

• Reporting to the Lead Lot Operations or other designated manager, you will assist with outside functions to support lot movements and general operations before, during, and after sale day. In this role, you will assist on the lot, including driving the service truck, lot tow truck (non-DOT), and forklift, to ultimately maintain accurate inventory flow and ensure vehicle readiness.

Responsibilities

• Lot Operations Support: Support lot operations by preparing and staging vehicles for sale, including stickering (run and customer stickers), marking vehicles on the spot, moving vehicles using a lot tow truck or forklift, and operating the service truck to support the driver team.

• Inventory Accuracy: Scan the lot and use electronic devices to record the movement of vehicles on the property.

• Vehicle Readiness: Assist with vehicle readiness tasks such as jumping vehicles and adding fluids (gas, water, etc), adding air to tires, and verifying vehicle status while maintaining accurate lot organization.

• Property Management: Handle the removal of personal property from vehicles.

• Operational Flow: Communicate with shop and operations teams to ensure an efficient flow of inventory from vehicle check-in to the auction sale line.

• Customer & Admin Support: Provide customer service support and coordinate with administrative teams to ensure efficient execution of sale day activities.

• Vehicle Identification: Confirm vehicle mileage, make year, and VIN to ensure accurate record-keeping.

• Safety & Maintenance: Maintain work areas to ensure a safe environment and report any incidents or hazards to the designated manager.

• General Duties: Perform any other duties assigned by the designated manager.

Skills and Attributes

• Teamwork: A team player who can collaborate well with multiple departments, customers, and vendors.

• Customer Focus: Strong customer service skills.

• Detail-Oriented: Proven ability to multitask while maintaining strict attention to detail.

• Efficiency: Proven ability to manage deliverables and metrics against aggressive targets and timelines.

• Adaptability: Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and handle outside conditions.

• Communication: Effective interpersonal skills with excellent verbal and written communication.

Qualifications

• High School diploma or GED preferred

• Must be 18 years of age and have a valid driver’s license that meets the requirements

• Able to safely drive a variety of vehicle makes, models, and sizes, including tow trucks, forklifts, and the service truck

• Automotive or auction experience preferred

• Proficiency with computer systems and applications

• Obtain and maintain forklift certification

ADESA Values

• Our Next Customer May Be Your Mom: Every customer deserves the same level of care and respect one would give to their own mother.

• We’re All in This Together: The company is unified by the shared goal of providing fantastic customer experiences, achieved through mutual trust, respect, and understanding.

• There Are No Sidelines: Employees are encouraged to be proactive, work hard, and take ownership of what needs to be done in a fast-paced environment.

• Be Brave: Employees should not fear taking risks, pushing themselves outside their comfort zones, or being decisive, even if they stumble along the way.

• Zag Forward: The company empowers creative and passionate thinking to find meaningful ways to be different and deliver amazing experiences.

• Don’t Be a Richard: A simple guiding principle to act appropriately and professionally.

• Stay Scrappy: This value rejects mediocrity and "good enough," pushing employees to do more with less to pass savings on to customers.

ADESA Benefits and Perks

Competitive Pay | Quality Benefits | Holiday and Paid Time Off | Education and Equipment Reimbursement Programs | Matching 401(k) | Career Path Opportunities | And More!

Other Requirements

To be able to do your job at ADESA, there are some basic requirements we want to share with you. Of course, we’ll make any reasonable accommodations for those with disabilities to perform the essential functions of their jobs.

• The physical activity requirements of the position range from Light to Medium Physical Work.

• Constant - standing, watching, touching, listening, walking, talking

• Frequent - bending, stooping, kneeling, lifting, grasping, pushing, pulling

• Potential – running, jumping, yelling, or other rapid or forceful movement in emergencies

• Visual acuity requirements include color, depth perception, and field of vision comparable to definitions for Clerical, Administrative, and Machine Operators (including inspection) positions.

Physical Working Conditions

This position is subject to both inside and outside environmental working conditions, including temperature changes, outside weather conditions, slightly elevated ambient noise levels, and minor atmospheric conditions affecting skin or respiratory systems, such as fumes, odors, and dust associated with internal and external service station/convenience food and petroleum dispensing operations.

To be able to do your job at ADESA, you must be able to read, write, speak, and understand English. Of course, we’ll make any reasonable accommodations for those with disabilities to perform the essential functions of their jobs.

Legal Stuff

Hiring is contingent on passing a complete background check.  This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

jobs.title: Workplace & Event Operations Manager
jobs.description:
Field sales powers the economy — but most teams are struggling. Reps are buried in admin work, managers are stretched thin, and leaders can’t see what’s really happening in the field.

Siro is redefining how field sales teams learn, perform, and win.

We started as an AI-powered coaching platform that helped reps improve their outcomes in the field.

Today, we’re something much bigger — an intelligent companion that automates sales reps’ tedious admin work, gives managers real-time visibility, and helps executives see around corners.

Our platform integrates with systems like Salesforce, analyzing thousands of in-person sales conversations to surface insights, automate workflows, and drive better outcomes across the org. Think Iron Man’s Jarvis for sales — proactive, personalized, and built directly into the tools teams already use.

Siro has raised $75M and is backed by world-class investors like Index, Fika, CRV, and SignalFire. We are trusted by leading home-improvement, retail, hospitality, and automotive brands, and powered by a lean team from Meta, McKinsey, Doordash, and Uber.

We’re building the future of human-AI collaboration in sales — and we’re just getting started.

Siro runs on experiences: the office our team walks into every morning, the moments that pull us together, and the conferences where we meet customers. We're hiring one person to own the operations behind all three.

You'll run our NYC office end to end, plan the team events that make Siro feel like Siro, and be the operational right hand to our Director of Events on every conference and trade show we attend.

This is not a coordinator role. You'll own budgets, vendors and outcomes, make calls without waiting for direction, and escalate only what truly needs a second opinion.


WHAT YOU'LL OWN


1. HOW OUR NYC WORKPLACE OPERATES AND FEELS.

 - Visitors: the VIP end-to-end experience for every customer, candidate, and investor who walks through the door: welcome, room, food, and a lasting first impression.

 - Facilities: HVAC, cleaning, maintenance, security, building management, health, safety compliance. When something breaks, you own the fix and the follow-up with the building.

 - Space: seating plans, furniture, workstation installs, conference rooms and A/V, and space planning as the team grows.

 - Supplies and food: snacks, drinks, kitchen, and office supplies, managed to budget.

 - Atmosphere: decor, plants, seasonal and holiday decorations, and the small touches that make the office a place people want to be.

 - Vendors and budget: own the office budget and every office vendor contract, and renegotiate them

 - Systems: an office calendar, SOPs, and self-service guides so the office runs well even on the days you're not around.


2. PLANNING & EXECUTING THE MOMENTS THAT BRING SIRO TOGETHER

 - Monthly socials and happy hours, our holiday parties, seasonal events, and milestone celebrations.

 - Company offsites: venue sourcing, group air and hotel blocks, F&B minimums, runs of show

 - New-hire welcome moments

 - Expense tracking against the socials and offsite budgets, reconciled with finance.


3. THE LOGISTICS & OPERATIONS FOR CONFERENCES

 - Booth and shipping: booth builds, freight, material handling, swag and collateral, and getting everything there and back on time.

 - Travel and hotels: flights, hotel room blocks and staffing logistics for the Siro team at each show.

 - Some: Vendors: source and negotiate with venues, caterers, AV, printers, exhibitor services and contractors.


WHO YOU ARE

 - A critical thinker. You question the quote, the plan and the assumption. You can spot the clause that will cost us later, and decide what to escalate and what to just handle. You think in second and third order consequences, and understand when and how to build in optionality.

 - Hospitality at your core. You notice the cold conference room, the dietary restriction, and the visitor looking lost before anyone else does. Every guest and teammate should feel anticipated and taken care of.

 - Incredibly organized. You run multiple vendors, timelines, and budgets at once. Your trackers are current, your follow-ups go out before anyone asks, and nothing falls through the cracks.

 - A fierce negotiator. You've negotiated hotel blocks, F&B minimums, venue buyouts and vendor contracts, and you can name the dollars you saved. You ask for the discount, the waived fee and the better terms every time, and you walk away when the deal isn't right.


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 4+ years in workplace or office management, event operations, or hospitality, ideally in a high-growth startup.

 - Hands-on experience with conference logistics: booth shipping, exhibitor services, room blocks and on-site execution.

 - A track record of owning budgets and vendor relationships end to end

 - Experience running a large-scale project such as an office buildout, move, or company offsite.

 - Warm, polished communication with executives, vendors, guests and teammates.

 - Comfort with AI tools and a habit of automating repeatable work.

 - NYC-based, in office 4-5 days/week

At Siro, we are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment where all people feel that they are equally respected and valued, whether they are applying for an open position or working at the company. We provide equal employment opportunities to all applicants without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

jobs.title: Director of Commercial Business Development
jobs.location: Washington, District of Columbia, United States
jobs.description:
Katalyst Description:

Katalyst is an American technology company focused on dynamic space operations.  We are building a fleet of dual-use multipurpose robotic space vehicles to create the future where maneuvering, upgrading, refueling, resupply and exploration are as routine as they are on Earth. Getting to space and overcoming the gravity well is only half the story. What you do there is the future. We are not building the trains. We are building the machines that lay down the tracks. By developing the foundational capabilities that make sustained, responsive operations possible, we enable a new era of space exploration that strengthens national security and ensures freedom of action in an increasingly contested domain.

Katalyst Culture:

Working at Katalyst is intense, hands-on, and deeply rewarding. You’ll take real ownership and see your work move from concept to operations in an environment where the problems are hard and the impact is real. We value humility, craftsmanship, and doing things the right way, even when it’s harder. You’ll work closely with thoughtful, driven teammates who push each other to do their best.  Oh, and we're dog friendly!

Benefits:

• Stock options & equity

• Medical, dental, and vision coverage

• 401(k)

• Unlimited PTO

• Catered lunches

What You’ll Do

• Build, maintain, and own strategic relationships across the commercial space ecosystem, including satellite operators, spacecraft manufacturers, mission providers, logistics and infrastructure companies, insurers, investors, and other partners relevant to Katalyst’s mission portfolio.

• Develop account and market strategies for priority commercial segments, identifying economic buyers, technical influencers, operators, procurement stakeholders, budget owners, decision timelines, buying criteria, and barriers to adoption.

• Shape opportunities early by connecting commercial customer pain points and business objectives to credible Katalyst solutions, developing clear value propositions, business cases, and mission concepts, and creating the internal alignment needed before formal proposals or purchasing decisions.

• Own or lead business development strategy from opportunity qualification through contract, including customer engagement plans, competitive positioning, partnership strategy, pricing inputs, negotiation support, executive actions, and post-signature follow-through.

• Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Programs, Mission Operations, Finance, Contracts, and executive leadership to ensure external commitments are technically feasible, properly scoped, commercially sound, resourced, and aligned with company strategy.

• Support and lead customer briefings, capability demonstrations, proposals, statements of work, commercial negotiations, industry engagements, conferences, and executive-level meetings; communicate Katalyst’s technical, operational, and economic value with precision and credibility.

• Create repeatable business development and partnership mechanisms that allow Katalyst to scale commercial growth without becoming dependent on informal relationships or individual heroics.

What We’re Looking For

Required

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience. Technical, aerospace, engineering, business, finance, or related degrees are all relevant if paired with strong commercial and mission fluency.

• Prior experience in commercial business development, sales, partnerships, strategy, space technology, aerospace, satellite services, or a closely related role.

• Prior experience at a high-growth commercial space, aerospace, robotics, or deep-technology company where business development, product, engineering, and program execution had to operate closely with limited process and high ambiguity.

• Demonstrated experience developing senior customer relationships and converting market needs into funded opportunities, contract awards, strategic partnerships, revenue, or measurable advancement toward a commercial objective.

• Strong understanding of commercial space markets and the practical differences between user need, economic buyer, budget availability, procurement process, technical evaluation, business case, contracting structure, and signed revenue.

• Ability to lead business development activities from ambiguous early-stage opportunity through qualification, strategy, internal alignment, proposal, pricing, negotiation, contract, and transition into execution.

• High technical and mission fluency: able to understand complex spacecraft, autonomy, RPOD, mission operations, software, robotics, or on-orbit services well enough to ask credible questions, identify constraints, and communicate value without misrepresenting engineering reality.

• Excellent executive communication and writing skills, including customer briefings, proposals, account plans, business cases, meeting preparation, commercial negotiations, and clear internal synthesis of external information.

• Ability to comply with applicable export-control, customer-access, confidentiality, and contracting requirements.

Your Ideal Background

Preferred

• Experience structuring and negotiating strategic partnerships, commercial contracts, joint go-to-market arrangements, anchor-customer agreements, or other complex business relationships.

• Understanding of commercial contracting fundamentals including scope, statements of work, pricing, payment milestones, intellectual property, data rights, liability, insurance, export controls, and transition from business development into program execution.

Additional Requirements: Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed.

Compensation and Benefits: Your base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience. The anticipated salary range for this role is $199,000 - $250,000 annually.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at Katalyst. You will also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of the Employee Stock Option and Equity Plan, as well as a relocation bonus and other discretionary bonuses. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, and unlimited Paid Time Off.

At Katalyst our work on projects involving the U.S. Department of Defense requires adherence to International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), 22 C.F.R. Parts 120-130, which requires compliance with U.S. export laws before allowing employees to perform certain positions. Currently, our available roles necessitate access to ITAR-controlled information, and as a result, Katalyst would have to ensure any non-US person is authorized access to ITAR information before the commencement of employment. We are committed to equal employment opportunities and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, or national origin.

jobs.title: Senior Security Engineer, DFIR
jobs.description:
At ClickUp, we're building the future of work: the first truly converged AI workspace unifying tasks, docs, chat, calendar, and enterprise search, all supercharged by context-driven AI. We are an AI-native company. Every team member is expected to leverage AI daily, and we evaluate AI fluency as part of our hiring process. Join us and help redefine what's possible. 🚀



Security at ClickUp

Security at ClickUp is engineering-focused. We partner with teams across the company to protect our platform, our internal systems and our customers through secure design, defensive controls, detection and response. We build tooling and automation, including AI-powered workflows, to turn what we learn into lasting improvements.

 

About the team

Application Security at ClickUp investigates threats, platform abuse and security incidents affecting our product and internal systems. We turn investigation findings into response tooling, automation and stronger product defenses, partnering with engineering and product teams to prevent repeat issues. This is an engineering-first team that uses AI tools and agentic workflows to improve how we investigate and respond.

 

You will support this mission by thinking like a developer, breaking down a problem that we face, testing a method to approach it with automation, and implementing solutions that yield compounding value. Your skills to uncover threat indicators will be the foundation of this work.

 

The role

 - Digital forensics and incident response. Investigate threats affecting the ClickUp platform and internal systems, collect and analyze relevant evidence, and establish what happened and its impact. Lead investigations through findings, response and root cause, working with the owning teams to follow remediation through to completion.

 - Platform abuse investigations. Identify and respond to abuse of the ClickUp platform. Uncover threat indicators and recurring patterns, develop actionable threat intelligence, and use the findings to improve detection and prevent repeat abuse.

 - Agentic security tooling. Build and improve AI-assisted and agentic workflows for incident response, digital forensics and ongoing audits. Automate repeatable investigation work, validate outputs against evidence, and keep human review and appropriate access controls around consequential actions.

 - Product defenses and security controls. Design, develop and deploy controls that protect our product and internal systems. Turn investigation findings into software changes, response tooling and automated checks that address the underlying issue rather than just the individual incident.

 - Engineering partnership. Work directly with engineering, product, data and operations teams as a security player-coach. Explain observed threats with clear evidence, help teams design practical defenses, and mentor others so the improvements last beyond a single investigation.
   
   

Qualifications

 - Multiple years of experience in technology or software development, including building and maintaining tooling or automation that solves operational problems.

 - Practical experience using AI-assisted development or agentic workflows for engineering or security work, with an ability to validate their output and recognize when human review is needed.

 - Experience investigating security threats or platform abuse: analyzing logs and other evidence, identifying threat indicators, and explaining findings and impact.

 - Ability to translate a security finding into a practical software design change, response improvement or automated control.

 - Experience working with cloud or SaaS systems, including using their application, identity or audit data to investigate suspicious activity.

 - Clear written communication: findings and recommendations that another team can act on, supported by evidence.

 - Ability to build relationships and mentor others on technical topics, including security.

Desirable

 - Experience using AI agents in a SOC or other incident response workflows.

 - Understanding of agent security risks, including the confused deputy problem and the lethal trifecta.

 - You can facilitate a conversation rather than dictate it.

 - 3+ years of software development experience and 1+ year of security-specific experience.

 - Experience with security tools such as SAST, DAST, RASP, dependency checkers and SIEM.

 - 1 year of AWS experience, including IAM and least-privilege architectures.

 

Our stack

Cloud and SaaS environments, software development and security automation, AI-assisted and agentic workflows, and security investigation tooling.

 

If you are a software engineer who is only starting to learn security, please do apply!



Equal Opportunity Employer 

ClickUp is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, or national origin.
