jobs.title: Mechanical Engineer, Power Generation
jobs.description:
About the Team

OpenAI, in close collaboration with our capital and delivery partners, is building the infrastructure required to support frontier AI systems. The Data Center Engineering team defines repeatable technical standards and carries them through design, construction, commissioning, and operational readiness. The team works across data center facilities, power generation, compute infrastructure, construction, procurement, and operations to deliver reliable capacity at unprecedented scale and speed.

About the Role

We are seeking a Mechanical Engineer to design and integrate power-generation and balance-of-plant systems for large AI data center campuses. You will work across prime movers, fuel systems, exhaust, ventilation, cooling, water treatment, heat recovery, acoustics, fire interfaces, and plant auxiliaries. The role combines first-principles engineering with practical vendor and field execution to deliver systems that are safe, efficient, maintainable, and ready for demanding operating profiles.

Travel: 50%

Key Responsibilities

 - Develop mechanical basis-of-design documents, process flow diagrams, P&IDs, specifications, calculations, and equipment requirements for power generation facilities.

 - Design and review prime-mover auxiliaries, fuel gas or liquid fuel systems, exhaust, ventilation, cooling, lubrication, compressed air, water treatment, and heat-recovery systems.

 - Evaluate thermal performance, hydraulic behavior, pressure drop, vibration, acoustics, emissions interfaces, redundancy, and maintenance requirements.

 - Translate generation duty cycles and data center load profiles into equipment sizing, operating envelopes, and control requirements.

 - Review OEM and EPC proposals, equipment selections, test plans, failure modes, service strategies, and lifecycle tradeoffs.

 - Support procurement, factory acceptance testing, construction, startup, commissioning, performance testing, and root-cause investigations.

 - Coordinate interfaces with electrical, controls, CSA, fuel supply, environmental, fire protection, and data center mechanical teams.

 - Create repeatable mechanical reference designs and standards for future generation deployments.

Qualifications

 - 8+ years of mechanical engineering experience on power generation, oil and gas, industrial utilities, central plants, or mission-critical projects.

 - Strong knowledge of rotating equipment, piping, heat transfer, fluid systems, thermal performance, ventilation, and mechanical auxiliaries.

 - Experience with combined heat and power, heat recovery, modular generation, or microgrids.

 - Experience with gas turbines, reciprocating engines, generators, or comparable large industrial equipment.

 - Ability to evaluate vendor data, equipment curves, operating scenarios, failure modes, and maintenance constraints.

 - Experience carrying designs through construction, startup, commissioning, and performance validation.

 - Knowledge of applicable ASME, API, NFPA, ASHRAE, and environmental requirements.

 - Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering or a related field.

Preferred Skills

 - Professional Engineer license.

 - Experience with process simulation, hydraulic modeling, CFD, or equipment-performance modeling.

jobs.title: Director, Content (FloTrack)
jobs.description:
FloSports is a world-class sports media company strategically positioned to be the essential  destination for passionate sports fans, delighting them with live event coverage, breaking news,  highlights, stats, rankings, and team and player profiles. We are growing Our Sports every day  by continuing to invest in our ever-expanding ecosystem, which consists of over a dozen sport  verticals and hundreds of streaming partners. FloSports is creating the home for college  conferences/leagues and sports like grappling, hockey, track & field, racing, cheer, wrestling,  and more, and we are looking for innovative and passionate people like you to help us! 



THE ROLE: 

FloSports is a world-class sports media company dedicated to serving passionate sports fans through live events, original content, breaking news, highlights, rankings, and in-depth coverage across more than 25 sports.

We are seeking an experienced, strategic, people-first Director, Content (FloTrack) to lead the content strategy and day-to-day creative operations of FloTrack, a destination for track and field, cross country, and road/trail racing coverage.

This leader will be responsible for growing FloTrack's audience, strengthening its content authority, driving subscription acquisition and engagement, and maximizing the impact of our content across digital and social platforms.

The ideal candidate combines a deep understanding of track and field with strong content instincts, commercial awareness, operational discipline, and exceptional people leadership. They will establish a clear vision for FloTrack, empower a high-performing team, and foster a collaborative, accountable, and inclusive culture.



RESPONSIBILITIES: 

 - Content Strategy & Leadership
   
   - Provide hands-on creative leadership at priority FloTrack events, working directly with content teams to identify compelling stories, maximize athlete access, and develop differentiated coverage experiences.
   
   - Establish a credible and authoritative voice for FloTrack that goes beyond reporting news and results to consistently provide the context, analysis, and storytelling that help audiences understand why performances, athletes, and moments in the sport matter. Ensure this perspective is reflected across all content, particularly social media, video descriptions, and event coverage.
   
   - Own and execute FloTrack's content strategy, establishing a compelling year-round content calendar spanning professional, collegiate, high school, and international track and field. Develop and lead comprehensive annual and seasonal content strategies, establishing clear themes, original programming priorities, and storytelling plans well in advance of major events. Ensure the team has the time, direction, and creative freedom necessary to develop differentiated coverage.
   
   - Lead coverage planning for major competitions, championships, athlete storylines, breaking news, and FloSports rights properties.
   
   - Establish content priorities that balance audience demand, subscription opportunities, brand authority, and available resources.
   
   - Oversee the development and execution of original storytelling, news coverage, analysis, rankings, interviews, and event-related content.
   
   - Maintain high standards for content quality, accuracy, timeliness, creativity, and storytelling.
   
   - Identify emerging athletes, narratives, formats, and audience trends that strengthen FloTrack's position within the sport.
   
   Audience Growth & Business Performance
   
   - Develop and execute content strategies that grow FloTrack's audience, deepen fan engagement, and drive measurable business results.
   
   - Partner with Sales, Marketing, Rights Acquisition, Global Partnerships, Live Production, and other cross-functional teams to maximize content reach, discovery, and conversion.
   
   - Support subscriber acquisition, retention, and engagement through compelling content coverage and effective promotion of live events.
   
   - Use audience analytics, subscription performance, search trends, and social metrics to inform content decision-making.
   
   - Identify opportunities for original programming, content monetization, sponsorship integration, and new audience development.
   
   - Establish and monitor clear performance goals across content traffic, social engagement, video consumption, audience growth, and subscription contribution.
   
   - Lead the development of a dedicated YouTube strategy focused on original programming, audience growth, discoverability, monetization, and maximizing the value of FloTrack's live event and archival content.
   
   Team Leadership & Development
   
   - Lead, coach, and develop FloTrack's content team, establishing clear expectations, accountability, and opportunities for professional growth.
   
   - Establish regular creative development and brainstorming processes that empower team members to originate ideas, contribute to strategic direction, and take pride and ownership in the content they produce.
   
   - Foster a culture built on trust, transparency, collaboration, constructive feedback, and mutual respect.
   
   - Conduct regular one-on-ones, performance conversations, and professional development planning.
   
   - Empower team members to take ownership of their work while providing the direction, support, and resources needed to succeed.
   
   - Build strong communication and collaboration across team members, shared Content functions, and other FloSports departments.
   
   - Proactively address challenges, resolve conflicts, and create an environment where employees feel heard, supported, and motivated.
   
   - Attract, develop, and retain talented content professionals who share a passion for digital storytelling.
   
   Operational & Financial Management
   
   - Oversee FloTrack's day-to-day content operations, content workflows, staffing priorities, and coverage assignments.
   
   - Develop and manage content budgets, including travel, freelance contributors, contract labor, and promotional investments.
   
   - Allocate resources based on strategic priorities, anticipated business impact, and operational needs.
   
   - Establish effective processes for planning, communication, execution, and performance reporting.
   
   - Coordinate content and organic promotional coverage of FloSports events with internal stakeholders, ensuring clear responsibilities and efficient execution.
   
   - Maintain operational flexibility to respond to breaking news, emerging opportunities, and changes in the competitive landscape.
   
   - Identify opportunities to improve productivity, streamline workflows, and maximize return on content investment.
   
   Cross-Functional Collaboration & Industry Relationships
   
   - Serve as FloTrack's primary content leader, collaborating with FloSports leadership and teams across Marketing, Rights Acquisition, Product, Sales, and other functions.
   
   - Build strong relationships with athletes, coaches, agents, and other industry personalities to develop exclusive access, original storytelling opportunities, and recurring content franchises that strengthen FloTrack's connection with its audience.
   
   - Partner with rights holders, event organizers, athletes, coaches, agents, and industry stakeholders to strengthen FloTrack's coverage and relationships.
   
   - Collaborate with Creative and Social teams on original video, digital franchises, promotional campaigns, and emerging content formats.
   
   - Support commercial partnerships and sponsored content opportunities while maintaining integrity.
   
   - Represent FloTrack and FloSports professionally within the broader track and field community.



KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:  

Required

 - 7+ years of experience in digital media, content, or a related field, including meaningful people-management experience.

 - Demonstrated success developing and executing content strategies that drive measurable audience growth and engagement.

 - Strong knowledge of the track and field landscape, including major competitions, athletes, governing bodies, and relevant media platforms.

 - Proven ability to lead, motivate, and develop teams while building a positive, high-performing work environment.

 - Exceptional content judgment, storytelling instincts, and understanding of digital content production.

 - Experience managing budgets, prioritizing resources, and overseeing multiple simultaneous projects.

 - Strong analytical skills and the ability to translate performance data into actionable content strategies.

 - Excellent communication, organizational, relationship-building, and problem-solving skills.

 - Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment, including occasional nights, weekends, and travel around major sporting events.

 - Demonstrated experience developing and launching original content concepts, programming formats, and creative franchises that differentiate a media brand, build audience engagement, and establish a distinctive content identity and voice.

 - Experience leading content and creative coverage of major live sporting events, including on-site production, athlete interviews, breaking news, and real-time storytelling.

 - Proven experience leading and developing creative teams, fostering a culture of collaboration, experimentation, original thinking, and individual creative ownership.

 - Strong content judgment and demonstrated ability to communicate the significance of sports performances and storylines through compelling, context-rich storytelling across digital and social platforms.

Preferred

 - Experience leading content teams within a sports media organization.

 - Established relationships within the track and field community.

 - Experience developing content strategies that support subscription-based digital media businesses.

 - Strong understanding of organic social media, SEO, audience development, and digital video distribution.

 - Experience managing coverage of major international, collegiate, or professional sporting events.

 - Familiarity with content monetization, branded content, and cross-functional commercial partnerships.

 - Proven experience developing platform-specific video and social content strategies, particularly on YouTube, with demonstrated success in audience development, engagement, and monetization.



BONUS

What Success Looks Like

The Director, Content (FloTrack) will be evaluated on their ability to deliver results across four core areas:

1. Content Excellence & Brand Leadership

 - Deliver distinctive, timely, and high-quality coverage that strengthens FloTrack's authority in track and field.

 - Establish a clear content identity and content strategy that consistently serves passionate fans.

 - Establish a comprehensive annual and seasonal content strategy, including new original programming concepts and clearly defined content priorities.

 - Establish FloTrack as a trusted and authoritative voice in the sport, consistently delivering the context, analysis, and perspective that help audiences understand why performances, athletes, and moments matter—not simply what happened.

2. Audience Growth & Business Impact

 - Grow qualified audiences across owned and distributed platforms.

 - Demonstrate measurable contributions to subscription acquisition, audience engagement, and content monetization.

 - Optimize content and promotional investments against business priorities.

 - Implement a distinct YouTube growth and monetization strategy, with measurable progress against agreed performance targets.

 - Demonstrate how content initiatives are contributing to audience development, subscriber engagement, sponsorship opportunities, and increased value from media rights.

3. Team Leadership & Culture

 - Build and maintain an engaged, collaborative, and accountable team.

 - Develop employees through meaningful coaching, clear communication, and consistent performance management.

 - Foster a culture of trust, ownership, and continuous improvement.

 - Encourage and foster employee engagement, creative ownership, collaboration, and retention.

4. Operational Execution

 - Consistently deliver effective content coverage and promotional execution around priority events and storylines.

 - Manage budgets and resources responsibly while adapting to evolving business needs.

 - Establish efficient, scalable workflows and strong cross-functional partnerships.

 - Establish advance coverage plans for major events, with clear creative direction and differentiated storytelling opportunities.



OUR COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY:

At FloSports, we are bonded by our passion for sports and our purpose to unite communities around experiences that finally give underserved sports the love they deserve. We recognize the need to build a company that seeks out, embraces, and celebrates our individual differences, ideas, and talent. FloSports is committed to the pursuit of a fair, equal and inclusive workplace where everyone is given the opportunity to grow to their fullest potential. 

 

OUR BENEFITS:

 - Recognized three years in a row as a Top Workplace by the Austin-American Statesman

 - Flexibility at work - you can take control of your profession and personal schedule

 - All-hands events hosted in beautiful Austin, Texas 

 - Annual equity awards for all top performers

 - Competitive and comprehensive medical, dental and vision plans

 - Peace of mind through company-paid short-term disability, long-term disability and life insurance

 - Generous 401(K) company match vested immediately

 - Progressive parental leave policies

 - Flexible paid time off

 - Hack-a-thons and a full calendar of team-building and social events

 - Company donation to youth teams and leagues that our employees coach

 - Stocked snack bar, catered lunch and breakfast tacos every week

jobs.title: Senior Director, Investigator Grants
jobs.description:
Job Summary:

The Senior Director, Global Investigator Grants is the senior leader accountable for the strategy, governance, and performance of Precision's global investigator grants and site payment organization. Reporting directly to the VP, Operational Finance, this role leads the Global Investigator Grants team across all regions, ensuring investigator payments, prepaid fund management, forecasting, accruals, and reconciliations are delivered accurately, on time, and in compliance with Clinical Trial Agreements (CTAs), sponsor contracts, and applicable regulations.

The Senior Director leads the integration of acquired and partner site networks into Precision's investigator grants operating model and is accountable for the overall integration of the site payment process within the Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS). As a partner to Clinical Operations, Project Management, Site Contracts, Finance, Information Technology, and sponsors, the role builds scalable processes, strong financial controls, and a sponsor experience grounded in transparency, predictability, and audit readiness.

Main Responsibilities:

• Lead the Global Investigator Grants organization across all regions, setting the strategic vision, operating model, and multi-year roadmap in alignment with Operational Finance and Clinical Solutions objectives.

• Lead, develop, and retain a global team of an Associate Director, managers, financial analysts – grants and investigator grants associates, including workforce planning and resource allocation to support portfolio growth.

• Lead the integration of acquired and partner site networks into Precision's investigator grants model, including assessment of existing site payment practices, harmonization of processes, systems, and controls, transition of open site payment obligations and prepaid balances, and post-integration performance monitoring.

• Serve as the accountable owner for the overall integration of the site payment process within the CTMS, including requirements definition, configuration, data migration, validation, user acceptance testing, go-live readiness, user adoption, and ongoing optimization in partnership with Information Technology, Business Systems, Clinical Operations, and Finance.

• Establish global governance, policies, SOPs, and financial controls for investigator payments, prepaid fund management, accruals, reconciliations, aggregate spend and transparency reporting (e.g., Sunshine Act), and study closeout to ensure audit and inspection readiness.

• Provide oversight of investigator grant budgets, forecasting, and accruals across the portfolio, including grant budget impacts within change orders, and report on performance, risks, and prepaid fund positions to the VP, Operational Finance and senior leadership.

• Serve as the senior escalation point and trusted advisor to sponsors, site networks, and internal leadership on complex grant administration, site payment, contractual, and compliance matters, and participate in executive sponsor meetings and Quarterly Business Reviews.

• Partner with Business Development, Proposals, and Contracts to shape investigator grant and site payment strategy within proposals, bid defenses, and contract terms, including advance and prepaid funding structures and fair market value approach.

• Define and monitor global KPIs, service levels, and executive dashboards (e.g., payment cycle times, prepaid fund coverage, forecast accuracy, site satisfaction), and drive continuous improvement, automation, and organizational change management.

Qualifications:

Minimum Education & Experience:

• Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field.

• Minimum of 18 years of progressive experience in investigator grants, site payments, or clinical trial finance within a CRO, pharmaceutical, or biotechnology environment, including at least 10 years leading global teams through managers and directors.

• Demonstrated experience leading a clinical systems implementation (CTMS or site payment platform) and/or the integration of acquired operations.

Preferred Education & Experience (optional):

• MBA, PMP, or equivalent advanced degree or professional certification preferred.

• Experience integrating site networks or acquired businesses into a global operating model required.

• Hands-on experience with Veeva Vault Clinical (CTMS and Clinical Finance), Medidata Rave Grants Manager, and ERP/PSA platforms.

Knowledge, Skills and Competencies:

• Executive Leadership and Vision – Sets strategy and leads a global function through managers and directors, aligning investigator grants operations with Operational Finance, Clinical Solutions, and corporate growth objectives.

• Integration Leadership – Proven ability to assess, plan, and execute the integration of site networks or acquired operations, harmonizing processes, systems, data, and controls with minimal disruption to sites and sponsors.

• Clinical Systems Transformation – Deep expertise leading CTMS and site payment system implementations, including requirements, configuration, data migration, validation, and adoption.

• Global Investigator Grants Expertise – Expert knowledge of CTAs, site budgets, fair market value, payment triggers, prepaid funds, multi-currency payments, and country-specific tax and regulatory requirements.

• Financial Acumen – Strong command of forecasting, accruals, pass-through cost management, change order impacts, and cash management across a global portfolio.

• Governance, Compliance and Risk Management – Builds and sustains robust financial controls, SOPs, and audit-ready processes, including aggregate spend and transparency reporting obligations.

• People Leadership and Talent Development – Develops leaders, builds succession, and fosters a culture of accountability, collaboration, and operational excellence across geographies.

• Sponsor and Stakeholder Influence – Establishes trusted executive relationships with sponsors, site networks, and cross-functional leaders, and influences outcomes without direct authority.

• Change Management and Continuous Improvement – Leads organizational change, process standardization, and automation initiatives that deliver measurable gains in quality, efficiency, and scalability.

• Advanced Communication Skills – Listens for understanding, asking clarifying questions and confirming perspectives before responding, to fully grasp sponsor, site, and stakeholder needs. Communicates clearly and concisely with executive leadership, sponsors, and global teams, translating complex financial and operational information into decision-ready insights.

• High Emotional Intelligence (EQ) – Demonstrates strong self-awareness, empathy, and composure, building trust across cultures and functions, navigating sensitive sponsor and site conversations with diplomacy, and leading teams through change with resilience and sound judgment.

jobs.title: Director, Workforce Planning & Organizational Design
jobs.description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.



We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.



We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.



If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.



About the Role:

We are seeking a Director, Workforce Planning & Organizational Design to build and lead Crusoe’s enterprise workforce planning capability and help shape how our organization scales.

 

This leader will partner closely with Finance, People, and business leaders to translate business priorities into workforce plans, investment decisions, organizational structures, and operating models. The role spans long-range strategic workforce planning, annual headcount planning, and organizational design, ensuring we have the right talent, capabilities, and organizational structures to support business growth and execution.

 

You will advise leaders on where to invest in talent, how to plan for future workforce needs, and how to structure teams for effectiveness and scale. You will also establish the planning processes, frameworks, and governance needed to make workforce decisions more consistent, data-driven, and financially disciplined.

 

Success in this role requires close partnership with Finance, People Success, Talent Management, Compensation, Recruiting, People Operations and People Science & Workforce Intelligence. You will bring specialized workforce planning and organizational design expertise to help business and functional leaders make informed decisions, while ensuring clear ownership and accountability across teams.

 
 

What You'll Be Working On:

 - Strategic Workforce Planning
   
   - Lead enterprise strategic workforce planning, translating company strategy, growth forecasts, and operational priorities into multi-year workforce strategies and capability requirements.
   
   - Establish a continuous planning process, anchored by biannual planning cycles, quarterly business reviews, and ongoing monitoring of workforce trends, risks, and business needs.
   
   - Partner with Finance and business leaders to forecast workforce demand, assess supply and capacity, identify capability gaps, and model alternative workforce scenarios.
   
   - Evaluate workforce composition, talent deployment options, and build-versus-buy scenarios in partnership with business and functional leaders.
   
   - Partner with Finance, Compensation, Recruiting, and Workplace to inform geographic workforce strategy, balancing talent availability, labor costs, office capacity, and business needs to guide long-term workforce investment decisions.
   
   - Partner with Talent Management to connect workforce plans with performance insights, succession planning, internal mobility, and talent development strategies, ensuring workforce decisions reflect current capabilities and future business needs.
   
   - Translate long-range workforce strategies into recommendations that inform hiring plans, capability development, organizational design, and workforce investments.

 - Operational Workforce & Headcount Planning
   
   - Own the enterprise workforce planning framework, connecting long-range strategies with annual budgets, quarterly forecasts, and in-year workforce decisions.
   
   - Serve as a key People partner to Finance, establishing workforce planning methodologies, assumptions, and operating rhythms aligned with financial planning governance.
   
   - Partner with People Success, Finance, Recruiting, and business leaders to develop and maintain integrated headcount plans aligned with financial targets and business priorities.
   
   - Facilitate workforce prioritization and trade-off discussions with Finance, People Success, and business leaders, supported by scenario modeling to inform staffing levels, hiring timing, and resource allocation.
   
   - Monitor plan performance, analyze variances, and recommend adjustments as business needs evolve, connecting approved plans to recruiting execution and workforce reporting.

 - Organizational Design & Operating Models
   
   - Advise business and People leaders on organizational design, structure, and effectiveness as Crusoe scales.
   
   - Lead organizational assessments and design engagements in partnership with People Success and business leaders, evaluating spans and layers, management structures, role clarity, decision rights, accountability, and capacity.
   
   - Partner with business leaders and People Success to develop and evaluate operating models that align organizational capabilities, workflows, governance, and talent with business strategy.
   
   - Identify opportunities to simplify structures, improve organizational effectiveness, and strengthen cross-functional execution.
   
   - Support organizational transformations, new capabilities, functional redesigns, and integration activities arising from growth, international expansion, and acquisitions.
   
   - Translate design recommendations into practical implementation plans with business leaders and People partners.

 - Workforce Intelligence & Enterprise Partnership
   
   - Partner with People Science & Workforce Intelligence, Finance, and business leaders to develop forward-looking insights on workforce capacity, productivity, cost, organizational efficiency, and talent needs.
   
   - Apply quantitative analysis, scenario planning, and business judgment to complex workforce decisions, making assumptions, risks, and trade-offs transparent.
   
   - Develop executive-ready recommendations that connect workforce and organizational choices to financial outcomes and operational performance.

 

What You'll Bring to the Team:

 - 10+ years of progressive experience in strategic workforce planning, organizational design, business strategy, strategic finance, management consulting, or related disciplines, including significant experience advising senior leaders.

 - Demonstrated experience leading both long-range strategic workforce planning and operational headcount planning in complex, rapidly scaling organizations.

 - Deep expertise in organizational design and operating models, including structural analysis, organizational effectiveness, governance, and decision rights.

 - Strong financial and commercial acumen, with the ability to partner fluently with FP&A on budgets, forecasts, workforce costs, and investment trade-offs.

 - Advanced analytical capabilities in workforce modeling, demand and capacity forecasting, scenario analysis, and evidence-based decision-making.

 - Experience building scalable planning frameworks, governance, and processes in evolving or ambiguous environments.

 - Exceptional consulting, influencing, facilitation, and executive communication skills, with the ability to translate complex analysis into clear business recommendations.

 - A builder's mindset, intellectual curiosity, sound judgment, and the ability to move seamlessly between enterprise strategy, detailed planning, and hands-on execution.

 

Bonus Points

 - Experience in technology, cloud infrastructure, engineering, manufacturing, energy, or other capital-intensive or high-growth environments.

 - Background in management consulting, corporate strategy, strategic finance, or a sophisticated strategic workforce planning function.

 - Familiarity with Workday or other workforce and headcount planning tools.

 - Experience with international workforce planning, location strategy, M&A, or organizational integration.

 - Academic background in human resources, organizational effectiveness, industrial-organizational psychology, economics, business analytics, or a related discipline.

 

Benefits:

 - Competitive compensation and equity packages

 - Restricted Stock Units

 - Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

 - Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

 - Employer contributions to HSA account

 - Paid parental leave

 - Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

 - Professional development & tuition reimbursement

 - Mental health & wellness support

 - Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

 - Cell phone stipend

 - 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

 - Volunteer time off

 - Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

 - Daily meals allowance

 - Additional perks & programs specific to location

 

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $215,000 - $255,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Electrical Engineer II, Advanced Product Development
jobs.description:
Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form! 



In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by TIME as a “Best Invention”, MIT Technology Review as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and Fast Company as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia. 



Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing -  might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.



Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.




ROLE DESCRIPTION

Form's Advanced Product Development team is responsible for architecting and designing the next generation of our iron-air battery system — the cell, module, pack, and the support systems that keep them running reliably for decades in the field. We work ahead of our production programs, translating breakthrough electrochemistry and system requirements into electrical, controls, and test systems that can scale to high-volume manufacturing.

We're hiring an Electrical Engineer II to design, build, troubleshoot, and test the control systems and test assets that support development of our next generation of iron-air batteries. As part of our Advanced Product Development team in Somerville, MA, you will spend much of your time in the lab: wiring and commissioning control systems, bringing up new hardware, diagnosing electrical and controls faults, and running system-level tests. You will work with guidance from senior electrical engineers and alongside mechanical and systems engineers and technicians to turn test requirements into safe, reliable, well-documented hardware. This is an exciting opportunity to deliver our sustainable multi-day energy storage solution to the grid!

Relocation assistance is available. 




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Design, build, wire, and check out control systems for test assets, working from schematics and BOMs through fabrication and documentation.

 - Troubleshoot electrical and controls issues on test assets and prototype hardware, finding root causes with scopes, meters, and data logs and implementing fixes.

 - Bring up and commission new test assets in the lab, including point-to-point checkout, sensor and instrument verification, and functional testing of safety interlocks.

 - Plan and run system-level tests: write test procedures, collect and review data, and report results and issues to the team.

 - Program and modify PLC and HMI logic for test assets with guidance from senior engineers, and keep eCAD schematics, BOMs, and cable/harness documentation current.

 - Partner with mechanical, systems, and test engineers and technicians on tight timelines, and champion lab and electrical safety when introducing new processes, prototype hardware, or test methods.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - Degree in Electrical Engineering or related field; Bachelor's with 1+ years experience in control panel design, PLC programming, or test/automation equipment, or Master's with research or professional engineering experience.

 - Experience with PLC programming (e.g., Beckhoff TwinCAT, Allen-Bradley, or similar) and HMI development, including debugging logic on live hardware.

 - Ability to read and work from electrical schematics; experience with an eCAD package (AutoCAD Electrical, ePLAN, or SolidWorks Electrical) is a plus.

 - Hands-on lab skills: panel wiring, troubleshooting with scopes and meters, commissioning hardware, and planning and running system-level tests.

 - Familiarity with NFPA 70/79 and UL 508A practices for industrial control panels.

 - Exposure to sensors, data acquisition, power distribution, and industrial communication protocols (e.g., EtherCAT, Modbus, CAN).

 - Experience in energy storage, batteries, or another safety-critical hardware industry is a plus.

 #LI-Onsite



Humanity is a cornerstone of Form Energy’s culture, and we make sure our compensation and benefits reflect that. Form Energy offers competitive salaries, stock options, and a holistic benefits package to ensure all employees have what they need to thrive while working here. 



When it comes to you and your family’s health, we cover 100% of medical, dental, and vision premiums for full-time employees - and 80% of healthcare premiums for dependents. This starts from day one. We also offer at least 12 weeks of paid leave for new parents (up to 20 weeks for birthing parents), and generous vacation policies to give employees time to recharge when needed. 



To build America’s energy future, we need everyone at the table. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply to our open jobs.




If you may require reasonable accommodations to participate in our interview process, please contact accommodations@formenergy.com. Requests for accommodations will be treated with discretion.

jobs.title: Solution Architect (AWS / AI)
jobs.description:
Specialization: Cloud-Native & AI

Platform focus: AWS Deep

Location: Remote (US), with travel to client sites as needed

CapNexus is an AWS consulting partner specializing in AI and cloud engineering. We build and deliver software through agentic engineering: we build and operate the systems that produce code, direct AI tooling to accelerate delivery, and exercise the judgment that keeps AI-generated work correct. Everyone at CapNexus works fluently inside our delivery system, which combines agentic tooling, spec-driven development, evidence-based quality, and AI-augmented delivery governance.

Who You Are and What You'll Do:

CapNexus is looking for a Solutions Architect to translate client problems into technical solutions and own the architecture the engineering team builds against.

In this role, you'll focus on cloud-native applications with AI built in: serverless and container services, APIs, front ends, and the generative and agentic AI features inside them.

Your time splits evenly. About half is billable client delivery as the architect on an engagement. The other half is pre-sales, where you scope the opportunity and design the solution before the work is sold.

Responsibilities:

• Lead solution design for an engagement: architecture, technology choices, integration, security, and cost.

• Author the technical specifications the engineering team validates and builds from.

• Translate business requirements into designs and roadmaps, and explain trade-offs in business terms.

• Partner with the Lead Engineer as a peer: you decide the architecture, and they decide the implementation approach.

• Support pursuits with solution design, estimates, and technical credibility.

• Mentor engineers on design patterns and architectural thinking.

• Design cloud-native application architectures on AWS (serverless, event-driven, and container-based) with generative and agentic AI features built in, including retrieval, agents, evaluation, and guardrails.

• Design end-to-end AWS architectures across compute, data, networking, security, and AI services, and review them against the AWS Well-Architected Framework.

• Lead discovery with client stakeholders and scope the systems involved: current state, requirements, constraints, integrations, and risks.

• Produce the architecture and design documents an engagement is built from: solution architecture documents, architecture decision records, non-functional requirements, and diagrams.

• Turn a scoped design into effort estimates and the technical content of proposals and statements of work.

• Lead technical presentations, demos, and proof-of-concept builds that show clients how the solution works.

• Partner with the Client Leader on pursuits. You own the solution and the estimate; pricing and contract terms are handled separately.

How You'll Work: Agentic Engineering:

You translate client problems into technical solutions and own the architecture the team builds against.

• Solution design through agentic delivery. Design solutions that assume agentic engineering as the delivery model: account for what AI tooling accelerates, what it can't do, and where human judgment gates belong.

• Delivery-approach design. Specify the delivery tooling for the engagement: the agent roles, conversion tools, templates, and validation gates the team builds through.

• Agentic tooling fluency. Use Claude Code and Kiro to prototype architecture decisions, generate reference implementations, and test design assumptions before committing the team.

• AI integration judgment. Decide where AI fits in the solution, and where it doesn't, and own the integration, data, security, and cost implications.

• Quality standard ownership. Define the architecture quality bar the team builds against. The Lead Engineer executes to your standard; you own the standard.

What doesn't change at any level: judgment over correctness, the ability to tell when confident, plausible-looking AI output is quietly wrong. Tooling does the mechanical work; you're accountable for whether it's right.

Qualifications:

• 10+ years of software, infrastructure, or data experience, including significant solution architecture work.

• Experience designing end-to-end solutions across application, data, infrastructure, and security.

• Strong client communication: you can run an architecture review with executives and engineers in the same room.

• Hands-on experience prototyping or testing designs with AI development tools such as Claude Code or Kiro, and a clear view of what AI tooling can and can't be trusted with in a production architecture.

• A hands-on background building full-stack, cloud-native applications with AI features (for example, React or Angular front ends, Python or TypeScript services, and Amazon Bedrock) before moving into architecture.

• 5+ years designing production architectures on AWS, with a working understanding of cost, scaling, security, and failure modes.

• A current AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional certification.

• Strong written and verbal communication: clear design documents, proposals, and executive presentations.

• Solid business acumen: you connect architecture choices to cost, risk, time to value, and the client's business case.

• Proven experience scoping systems and producing architectures and design documents that teams build from.

• Pre-sales or consulting experience: discovery workshops, solution proposals, estimates, and demos.

Nice to Have:

• AWS Certified Generative AI Developer – Professional (AIP-C01).

• AWS Certified Security – Specialty.

• Experience engaging AWS Professional Services during scoping.

• Background in retail.

Our Culture:

Four keystones guide how we work:

• Customer obsessed, delivery focused. We deliver what we promise. Trust = consistency × time.

• Learning and sharing. We hire lifetime learners, and teaching others matters as much as knowing.

• Growth and scalability. We value cross-functional skills over role boundaries, and simple solutions over clever ones.

• All work is strategic. Every engagement, big or small, is a chance to earn trust that lasts.

We offer:

Job Type: Full-time

Benefits: Medical, dental, 401(k), and more

CapNexus is an equal opportunity employer. We embrace and celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive and safe environment for all employees. Experience comes in many forms, and we’re dedicated to adding new perspectives to the team. We encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn’t perfectly align with what we have listed. We look forward to hearing from you.

No Agencies Please!

jobs.title: Senior Project Manager
jobs.description:
About the Positions

We’re seeking Senior Project Managers to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. Your primary focus will be centered on underground and tunneling on major rail and mobility programs, including bored and mined tunnel, cut-and-cover structures, shafts, cross passages, and underground station work, along with the ground improvement, dewatering, and instrumentation that go with it.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area. We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.

Responsibilities may include, but are not limited to, the following:

• Manage the delivery of underground and tunneling packages from preconstruction through closeout, tracking scope, budget, schedule, and risk against contract commitments.

• Review design submittals, shop drawings, and technical deliverables for tunnel, shaft, cut-and-cover, and ground improvement work against program criteria and agency requirements.

• Perform constructability and biddability reviews on underground packages, track comment resolution to closure, and support bid-phase addenda, bidder questions, and bid evaluation.

• Oversee the designer of record and the contractor on excavation sequencing, ground support, and settlement control commitments, and hold them to scope, criteria, and schedule.

jobs.title: IT Field Solutions Engineer II
jobs.description:
Meriton is a national team of experts driving HVAC innovation through a network of high-performing companies. From strategy and support to systems and solutions, we work behind the scenes to strengthen operations and build value—for our partners and our people.

If you’re looking to make an impact, we’re glad you’re here. At Meriton, you’ll join a team that believes in big ideas, doing great work, and building careers that matter—every step of the way.

IT Field Solutions Engineer II

Reports to: Senior Manager, IT Field Solutions

FLSA Status: Full time, Exempt

Salary: $75,000-105,000

The Opportunity

The IT Field Solutions Engineer II provides live, hands-on desktop, laptop, and software support for Meriton’s HVAC Service and Control Technicians, who work on rooftops, in mechanical rooms, and out in the elements to service critical equipment. This position ensures technicians have reliable access to the tools, software, and connectivity they need to perform at an elite level, day or night.

The IT Field Solutions Engineer II is a dependable, field-facing IT partner for Service and Controls, supporting specialized technician software, laptops/tablets, VPN, controller and gateway connectivity, and remote monitoring systems, with after-hours coverage as field demand requires. The scope of this role is deliberately broad while the team is built out: the engineer will start by taking direct field cases, shadowing current support, and learning the real demand, then grow into owning complex field cases as repeatable patterns emerge. This role works side by side with IT Service Delivery and partners closely with Service and Controls leadership and with platform teams such as Network, Cloud, and Cybersecurity. Our goal is simple: support the technician and scale the knowledge.

The ideal candidate is as passionate about being out in the field as they are about IT — a curious, methodical troubleshooter who takes ownership, communicates clearly with both technical and non-technical audiences, and enjoys learning unfamiliar technology. Team members in this role may also have the opportunity to progress into Control Technician roles through the IT Field Solutions apprenticeship pathway, if desired.

Responsibilities

Field Technician Support & Service Delivery

• Provide live, hands-on support to Service and Control Technicians through phone, chat, email, and ticketing, with a focus on fast response and practical resolution while the technician is on site.

• Triage incoming requests, capture impact and context, gather evidence, and take ownership of assigned issues through resolution, growing into ownership of complex field cases as repeatable patterns emerge.

• Remain the technician’s engaged point of contact, owning communication and follow-through while platform teams (Network, Cloud, Cybersecurity, and others) work changes within their own systems; hand off ownership only through a clear handoff with full context.

• Troubleshoot technician laptops, tablets, and mobile devices, including hardware, operating system, drivers, firmware, and application dependencies in rooftop, outdoor, and mechanical room conditions.

• Support technician-specific software, including HVAC controls programming tools, building automation and service applications, and remote monitoring systems.

• Troubleshoot the IT side of field connectivity, including USB/serial adapters and drivers, controller and gateway access, VPN, cellular, and Wi-Fi. Controls specialists retain responsibility for HVAC control logic and mechanical systems.

• Participate in a rotating on-call schedule to provide after-hours support for critical technician issues, with rotation and escalation details clarified as staffing and field demand become measurable.

• Travel approximately 25% to branch locations and customer sites to provide on-site support, deploy equipment, and assist technicians directly.

Equipment, Software & Asset Management

• Complete new technician equipment and account setup, including build, imaging, deployment, access management, and license management.

• Support device management and enrollment, including Intune, Jamf, and MDM compliance, policy, and standard device actions.

• Support Microsoft products such as Windows, Office 365, and other cloud-based applications, and support various vendor applications as needed.

• Perform hardware and software configuration, driver and firmware updates, maintenance, and upgrades for field-facing systems.

• Manage inventory of technician hardware and software assets, including tracking, lifecycle, and refresh.

• Interact with vendors to facilitate repairs and replacements of field hardware, such as laptops, tablets, rugged devices, docks, and accessories.

• Support pilots and field rollouts of new hardware, software, and MDM deployments, gathering technician feedback and validating compatibility in practice.

Security, Compliance & Safety

• Support approved endpoint security tools on field devices and collaborate with Cybersecurity, which owns the security platforms, on malware, vulnerability, and anti-phishing issues.

• Follow safety policies, codes, and regulations for rooftop, outdoor, and site work.

Knowledge, Process Improvement & Development

• Recognize emerging repeat issues, record root causes, and tag field cases by location, device, application, and owning team to help the team learn where demand actually comes from.

• Document known fixes, validated procedures, and runbooks, and build knowledge base content where none exists yet.

• Track support trends and metrics such as response times, resolution rates, repeat incidents, and technician satisfaction, and recommend improvements to field support workflows.

• Evaluate tools, products, and IT processes, share technician feedback, and recommend changes and technology standards that improve technician productivity and experience.

• Train field technicians in the use of equipment, software, and approved support processes.

• Grow technical depth through pairing and shadowing within IT Field Solutions, share troubleshooting methods with teammates, and participate in cross-training and job shadowing with Control Technicians.

Qualifications

• Experience in an IT services or field support role, typically 2+ years or equivalent hands-on experience.

• Strong troubleshooting fundamentals across Windows 10/11, networking, drivers, endpoints, and application dependencies, with sound, methodical diagnostic habits.

• Knowledge of TCP/IP, LAN, WAN, wLAN, and vLAN technologies, and working knowledge of VPN and remote access technologies.

• Knowledge of MS Active Directory infrastructure.

• Ability to learn unfamiliar technology quickly. HVAC and Controls-specific products will be taught; curiosity and methodical troubleshooting are what we are looking for.

• Ownership and adaptability: takes responsibility for assigned issues, communicates clearly, and flexes between support, discovery, and project work as demand becomes clearer.

• Curiosity and good judgment, including recognizing repeat issues, documenting findings, and helping establish procedures where none exist yet.

• Strong collaboration, communication, and customer service skills with technicians and operational leaders.

• Capable of working independently with minimal supervision.

• Valid driver’s license and ability to travel approximately 25% to branch and customer locations.

• Genuine interest in supporting field technicians and thriving in a fast-paced environment with evolving priorities.

Preferred Skills

• Associate degree in Information Technology or a related field.

• Scripting and automation experience, such as PowerShell.

• Experience supporting mobile field workforces, tablets, or ruggedized devices.

• Experience with USB/serial and IP communications to controllers or similar field devices.

• Experience supporting technicians or skilled trades (HVAC, controls, building automation, or similar).

• Intune, Jamf, MDM, MacOS, and iOS experience.

• Office 365 administration, Azure, and Windows Server experience.

• Familiarity with cellular and mobile device technology.

• Microsoft (MCP) Certification and/or ITIL (fundamentals level).

• MSP experience.

Why Meriton?

• Medical Insurance, Dental Insurance, Vision Insurance

• 100% company match on 401(k) contributions, up to 6% of pay.

• Tuition Reimbursement

• Company-paid Disability insurance (short-term and long-term)

• Company-paid group life insurance

• Paid Time Off & Holidays

• Volunteer Hours

• Employee-paid supplemental insurance options

• Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

• FSA, HSA and commuter benefits options

• Paid parental leave

• Career growth and learning

• …and so much more!

Additional Information

This position may be based in locations across the United States and requires approximately 25% travel to Meriton locations and customer sites, including rooftop and outdoor work in varying weather conditions. Rotating on-call and after-hours work is required.

Physical demands include frequent standing, walking, and sitting, and occasional climbing (including ladders and roof access), balancing, stooping, kneeling, crouching, or crawling. Must be able to work at heights and in outdoor conditions, including heat and cold, and to regularly lift and/or move up to 25 pounds and frequently lift and/or move up to 50 pounds.

As part of the interview process, candidates may participate in a technical assessment based on practical troubleshooting scenarios relevant to the role.

jobs.title: Enterprise Solutions Engineer, Clinical & EHR Systems
jobs.description:
OUR VISION

Health systems still run critical operations like staffing, labor planning, and capacity on spreadsheets, phone calls, and guesswork.

Vitalize is building the AI operating system for how health systems manage labor and capacity. The impact is real: we save hospitals millions in unnecessary labor spend, give clinical leaders back 10–20 hours every week, and are often the reason staff and leaders stay.

We’re trusted by leading health systems across the country and have raised more than $32M from top healthcare and technology investors, including our own customers.

 


OUR VALUES

We hire and grow everyone against the same four values. Each one comes from a real Vitalize story. Interview with us to hear them!

 - 🚗 Push the Car. Step in regardless of role. We help wherever we're needed, own problems end to end, and don't stay in our lane. People can count on us.

 - 🏥 Premier 1K. We show up for our customers, always. Nearly everyone visits a customer site in their first month, and customer feedback informs everything we do.

 - 🗣️ Run Towards the Ugly. Name the ugliest truth first, then propose the fix. Candor over comfort — we call out what's broken, and never get complacent. This shapes our craft.

 - 💡 Think Bigger Fridays. See the gap, fill it — no permission required. Every decision is an experiment: we run it, let the results decide, and drive real impact from day one.

 


ABOUT VITALIZE'S ENTERPRISE SOLUTIONS TEAM

Our customers operate complex technology environments spanning workforce management, HR, payroll, EHRs, identity, security, and other enterprise systems. As Vitalize takes on larger health systems and expands what our platform can do, the technical complexity of selling, deploying, and supporting our product grows with it.

Enterprise Solutions exists to make that complexity scalable. The function bridges Growth and Post-Sales — ensuring we understand what's technically possible before we sell it, customers are technically ready to go live, and the hardest problems we encounter become repeatable solutions the broader team can own. Done well, Enterprise Solutions helps us activate revenue faster, make deployments more predictable, and scale to increasingly complex customers without scaling technical support linearly.




THE ROLE

You’ll be one of the first two Enterprise Solutions hires at Vitalize, building the function from scratch alongside a peer focused on workforce and payroll systems. Together you’ll define what Enterprise Solutions becomes as our customer base and Post-Sales organization grow.

You’ll own the clinical systems that tell a hospital how much care it needs to staff for: EHRs (Epic, Oracle Health, Meditech, and similar), the interface engines around them, and adjacent acuity and assignment tools. Today that means real-time census, ADT, and acuity data that drives staffing decisions. As Vitalize expands into patient flow and capacity management, your scope grows with it.

Success means EHR integrations that are feasible, secure, and repeatable; deployments that aren’t stalled by interface-team backlogs or security reviews; and a team that becomes increasingly self-sufficient on clinical data because the hardest problems you solve become playbooks, tools, and repeatable capabilities.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own clinical-data solutioning across the customer lifecycle: Bridge Growth and Post-Sales so that what we sell can be deployed and supported, carrying critical technical context from pre-signature discovery through implementation and post-launch

 - Lead EHR discovery on enterprise deals: Partner with Growth before commitments are made to understand EHR vendor and version, interface engine (Epic Bridges, Rhapsody, Cloverleaf, Mirth, or similar), available feeds (HL7 v2 ADT, FHIR, vendor APIs), where acuity and assignment data lives, interface-team capacity, and security and privacy requirements

 - Get hospital interface and security teams to “yes”: Scope the smallest useful feed, minimize the patient data we take in, and guide integrations through security, privacy, and compliance review

 - Partner with Deployments to drive clinical-data readiness: Set the standards for unit and department mapping, feed testing, and census validation against what managers actually see. Step into complex deployments where needed while enabling Deployment Strategists to own increasingly sophisticated workstreams

jobs.title: Enterprise Solutions Engineer, Workforce Management & Payroll (UKG)
jobs.description:
OUR VISION

Health systems still run critical operations like staffing, labor planning, and capacity on spreadsheets, phone calls, and guesswork.

Vitalize is building the AI operating system for how health systems manage labor and capacity. The impact is real: we save hospitals millions in unnecessary labor spend, give clinical leaders back 10–20 hours every week, and are often the reason staff and leaders stay.

We’re trusted by leading health systems across the country and have raised more than $32M from top healthcare and technology investors, including our own customers.




OUR VALUES

We hire and grow everyone against the same four values. Each one comes from a real Vitalize story. Interview with us to hear them!

 - 🚗 Push the Car. Step in regardless of role. We help wherever we're needed, own problems end to end, and don't stay in our lane. People can count on us.

 - 🏥 Premier 1K. We show up for our customers, always. Nearly everyone visits a customer site in their first month, and customer feedback informs everything we do.

 - 🗣️ Run Towards the Ugly. Name the ugliest truth first, then propose the fix. Candor over comfort — we call out what's broken, and never get complacent. This shapes our craft.

 - 💡 Think Bigger Fridays. See the gap, fill it — no permission required. Every decision is an experiment: we run it, let the results decide, and drive real impact from day one.




ABOUT VITALIZE'S ENTERPRISE SOLUTIONS TEAM

Our customers operate complex technology environments spanning workforce management, HR, payroll, EHRs, identity, security, and other enterprise systems. As Vitalize takes on larger health systems and expands what our platform can do, the technical complexity of selling, deploying, and supporting our product grows with it.

Enterprise Solutions exists to make that complexity scalable. The function bridges Growth and Post-Sales — ensuring we understand what's technically possible before we sell it, customers are technically ready to go live, and the hardest problems we encounter become repeatable solutions the broader team can own. Done well, Enterprise Solutions helps us activate revenue faster, make deployments more predictable, and scale to increasingly complex customers without scaling technical support linearly.




THE ROLE

You'll be one of the first two Enterprise Solutions hires at Vitalize, building the function from scratch alongside a peer focused on clinical and EHR systems. Together you'll define what Enterprise Solutions becomes as our customer base and Post-Sales organization grow.

You'll own the systems our customers run their workforce on: workforce management and timekeeping (UKG Dimensions / Pro / Workforce Central, API Healthcare, and similar) and HCM, HRIS, and payroll (Workday, Oracle, Infor, and similar). These are the systems of record Vitalize reads from and writes back to — schedules, punches, pay codes, accruals, org hierarchies, and employee data. Getting them right decides whether a deployment goes live on time and whether a nurse's incentive pay lands correctly on her paycheck.

Success means fewer deployments delayed by workforce-system readiness, tighter alignment between what Growth sells and what Post-Sales can deliver, and a team that becomes increasingly self-sufficient on UKG, Workday, and payroll work because the hardest problems you solve become playbooks, tools, and repeatable capabilities.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own workforce-system solutioning across the customer lifecycle: Bridge Growth and Post-Sales so that what we sell can be deployed and supported, carrying critical technical context from pre-signature discovery through implementation and post-launch

Step into complex deployments where needed while enabling Deployment Strategists to own increasingly sophisticated workstreams

 - Build technical leverage across Vitalize: Create vendor-specific playbooks, discovery guides, documentation, and training so Growth, Deployments, Support, and Customer Success can handle standard UKG, Workday, and payroll workflows on their own

 - Turn customer requirements into product signal: Identify recurring workforce-integration requirements and blockers across our pipeline and customer base. Partner with Product and Engineering to decide when the answer is better enablement, a new integration, or a scalable platform capability




WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - You can lead technical solutioning with enterprise customers: You’re comfortable with CIO organizations, HRIS and payroll leaders, integration teams, and security teams, from pre-sales through implementation and escalation
