jobs.title: Quality Engineer
jobs.description:
Icarus was founded on the belief that the Stratosphere is the Forgotten Frontier and that reclaiming it will define the next era of aerospace and what is possible from the sky. We build solar-powered aircraft that fly at 60,000 ft for weeks at a time, delivering persistent, affordable, and scalable presence from this layer of the atmosphere.

Mission

Re-establish and maintain dominance in the Stratosphere.

Levels

We are hiring at Level I, Level II, and Level III through this posting. Your level will be determined during the interview process based on your technical skills, relevant experience, and demonstrated scope of ownership.

What you’ll do

• Own build quality from incoming parts through aircraft assembly, working hands-on with manufacturing, engineering, test, and supply chain.

• Create practical inspection criteria for purchased parts, composite structures, avionics, wiring, and mechanical assemblies; establish first-article checks for new suppliers and design changes.

• Contain and document nonconforming material, coordinate engineering disposition, and verify corrective actions before the issue reaches another build.

• Work directly with suppliers to resolve recurring defects and improve the consistency of parts arriving at the factory.

• Turn build and test findings into clearer work instructions, in-process checks, and feedback to the design team.

• Keep inspection records, material traceability, and configuration records connected to the aircraft being built, using ION and supporting tools.

• Use defect, rework, and yield data to identify the most valuable improvements and confirm that fixes work.

• Support calibrated measurement tools, production readiness reviews, and flight-hardware acceptance as the build rate grows.

What we’re looking for

• A degree in mechanical, electrical, aerospace, manufacturing, or a related engineering field, or equivalent hands-on experience.

• Experience building, inspecting, testing, or improving real hardware; internships and substantial project work count for Level I.

• Ability to read engineering drawings and specifications and use appropriate measurement and inspection tools.

• Strong problem-solving skills: distinguish a symptom from a root cause, document evidence, and follow corrective actions through to completion.

• Clear communication with technicians, engineers, and suppliers, and a willingness to spend time on the factory floor.

• Ability to work on-site at Icarus in El Segundo and take ownership of quality as designs and production processes evolve.

Bonus

• Experience with aerospace or other complex electromechanical products, composites, or supplier quality.

• Familiarity with first-article inspection, manufacturing quality systems, or statistical process analysis.

• Experience using ION, an ERP/MES, or Python/SQL to improve traceability and quality reporting.

Our culture = elite sports team. Winning = having fun

• Hyperfocus

• Extreme Ownership

• Radical Transparency

Why Icarus

• Meaningful equity

• Top market salary and bonuses

• Health, dental, and vision insurance

• Factory in El Segundo

• Real ownership, real hardware, real flight

• Small team, massive responsibility

• High signal (engineering) to noise (management) culture

• Dream desk setup

• Daily lunch

• Unlimited celsius

This is not a normal engineering job

• We are pioneers, not corporate managers. Icarus deliberately optimizes for a high signal (engineers) to noise (management) ratio, where engineering, flight, and execution matter more than process, politics, or management overhead.

• You will work side by side with the CEO and a small team of world-class builders. You will own your work end to end. Test it. Break it. Find the failure. Fix it. Validate it. Then do it again, faster.

• We expect full extreme ownership. This is a high-trust, no-BS team, and everyone pulls their weight.

• We are hiring across the stack: mechanical, aerodynamics, RF, GNC, electrical, avionics, power electronics, energy storage, software, and systems.

• We want builders. No hand-holding. No fluff. No fake projects. No slide decks. No sitting in meetings all day. Just raw engineering, real hardware, and real flight.

• You must thrive under pressure, learn fast, troubleshoot in the field, and push hardware to its limits. We move fast. We go to Mojave at 4 am in the morning. We expect results and an obsession with quality and speed.

• You will be a core part of getting flight systems from concept to reality, proving they work and driving rapid iteration loops. If you want real ownership, real hardware, and real flight, this is it.

No tourists. No bystanders. Only builders.

Hiring process

• Technical interview

• One-on-one with CEO

• Meet the team in-person

US salary range

• Level I: $100,000 - $140,000 USD per year

• Level II: $140,000 - $180,000 USD per year

• Level III: $180,000 - $220,000 USD per year

These ranges reflect annual base salary. Final level and base salary will be determined individually based on relevant skills, experience, and the scope of responsibility.

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are considered part of Icarus' total compensation package.

We’re an equal opportunity employer. We welcome all applicants without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status.

jobs.title: Controls Engineer, Power Generation and Microgird
jobs.description:
About the Team

OpenAI, in close collaboration with our capital and delivery partners, is building the infrastructure required to support frontier AI systems. The Data Center Engineering team defines repeatable technical standards and carries them through design, construction, commissioning, and operational readiness. The team works across data center facilities, power generation, compute infrastructure, construction, procurement, and operations to deliver reliable capacity at unprecedented scale and speed.

About the Role

We are seeking a Controls Engineer to design, program, integrate and commission on-site power generation and microgrid control systems serving large AI data center campuses. You will own control architecture and functional requirements across generation packages, balance-of-plant systems, electrical protection, microgrid controls, and data center monitoring. You will work from concept through factory testing, site commissioning, performance validation, and operational improvement.

This role requires hands-on experience with industrial control systems, including PLC and DCS programming, plant-level control sequences, equipment integration, simulation, testing and commissioning. The engineers will work with equipment vendors, system integrators and the broader data center team to make sure the complete power system operates safely and reliably across normal and failure conditions.

Travel: 50%

Key Responsibilities

 - Power Generation and Microgrid Controls
   
   - Design, program and commission plant power controllers (PPCs) and microgrid control systems for gas turbine and reciprocating engine power plants.
   
   - Develop control sequences for grid-connected, islanded and transition modes, including startup, shutdown, synchronization, load sharing, import/export control, load shedding, black start, restoration and resynchronization.
   
   - Coordinate active power, reactive power, voltage and frequency controls across generators, energy storage, MV UPS and other distributed energy resources.
   
   - Define how the plant responds to generator trips, loss of utility power, large load changes, equipment failures and loss of communication.
   
   - Work with OEMs to define the boundaries between turbine or engine controls, generator controls, the PPC, protection systems and data center controls.

 - Electrical systems and utility interconnection
   
   - Review utility and transmission-provider interconnection requirements and translate them into plant control, protection, metering, communications and testing requirements.
   
   - Work with utility and equipment vendors to define controls and interfaces at the point of interconnection, including power limits, voltage and frequency response, reactive, power factor, telemetry and dispatch.
   
   - Review interconnection studies, operating procedures and test requirements, and track the actions needed to demonstrate compliance.
   
   - Work with Engineer-Of-Record (EOR) to review load-flow, short-circuit, stability, step-load and electromagnetic transient (EMT) studies. Use the results to develop control settings, sequences and test cases.

 - Control Architecture:
   
   - Develop and review functional design specifications (FDS), sequences of operation, network architecture diagrams, I/O lists and alarm philosophies.
   
   - Review P&IDs and instrumentation for generation-plant systems, including fuel gas, cooling, lubrication and other balance-of-plant equipment.
   
   - Define equipment interfaces, control modes, permissives, interlocks and failure responses between OEM packages and the plant control system.

 - Real-Time Simulation and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing:
   
   - Develop and execute real-time simulation and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) tests for generation and microgrid control systems using RTDS and RSCAD.
   
   - Work with internal engineering teams and equipment vendors to build and validate representative models of the electrical system, from the generation plant and utility interconnection through the data center distribution system to representative GPU rack loads.
   
   - Develop and execute test cases for normal operation, mode changes, load steps, trips, faults, and system failures.
   
   - Compare simulation and HIL results with equipment data, factory test results and field performance. Document model assumptions and limitations.

 - Testing, commissioning and delivery
   
   - Develop and review FAT, SAT and integrated systems test plans for plant and microgrid controls.
   
   - Participate in factory testing, site testing, energization support, tuning and commissioning of generation and data center power systems.
   
   - Troubleshoot controls and system-integration issues using controller data, alarms, event records, trends and test results.
   
   - Work with OEMs, EPCs, utilities and system integrators to resolve interface gaps and track issues through closure.
   
   - Coordinate the handover of final project deliverables, including software, configurations, backups, test records, operating instructions and training, to the data center operations team.

Qualifications

 - 8+ years of hands-on experience designing, programming, integrating and commissioning industrial controls for power generation, industrial plants, utilities, or mission-critical infrastructure.

 - Strong hands-on experience with PLC, DCS, SCADA, historian, industrial-networking, and control-system integration.

 - Experience with plant power control, generator controls, synchronization, load sharing, islanding and load-shedding schemes.

 - Experience integrating controls with power generation equipment, protective relays, SCADA/EPMS and other plant systems.

 - Experience developing functional specifications, sequences, I/O, alarms, graphics, and factory or site test procedures.

 - Ability to troubleshoot across software, instrumentation, electrical, mechanical, communications, and operating-process boundaries.

 - Understanding of industrial cybersecurity, redundancy, failover, and change-control practices.

 - Bachelor's degree in controls, electrical, mechanical, chemical engineering, computer engineering, or a related field.

Preferred Skills

 - Experience with major turbine or reciprocating-engine control platforms and microgrid controllers.

 - Experience with data center power systems and rapidly changing AI or GPU loads.

 - Experience integrating gas generation with BESS, MV UPS and grid-forming or grid-following inverters.

 - Experience with EMT studies and model validation for weak-grid or islanded power systems.

 - Experience developing automated simulation tests and regression test libraries.

 - Experience with network redundancy, industrial protocols, OT cybersecurity and remote support for critical facilities.

 - Experience transitioning from temporary generation to permanent power systems.

 - Experience with IEC 61850 (MMS, GOOSE, SV), Modbus, OPC UA, DNP3, EtherNet/IP, or comparable industrial protocols.

 - Professional Engineer license, functional-safety training, or industrial-cybersecurity certification.



About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Metadata Platform
jobs.description:
WHAT IS BOX?

Box (NYSE:BOX) is the leader in Intelligent Content Management. Our platform enables organizations to fuel collaboration, manage the entire content lifecycle, secure critical content, and transform business workflows with enterprise AI. We help companies thrive in the new AI-first era of business. Founded in 2005, Box simplifies work for leading global organizations, including JLL, Morgan Stanley, and Nationwide. Box is headquartered in Redwood City, CA, with offices across the United States, Europe, and Asia.

By joining Box, you will have the unique opportunity to continue driving our platform forward. Content powers how we work. It’s the billions of files and information flowing across teams, departments, and key business processes every single day: contracts, invoices, employee records, financials, product specs, marketing assets, and more. Our mission is to bring intelligence to the world of content management and empower our customers to completely transform workflows across their organizations. With the combination of AI and enterprise content, the opportunity has never been greater to transform how the world works together and at Box you will be on the front lines of this massive shift.

WHY BOX NEEDS YOU

Metadata is a key component of the Box Content Cloud, enabling customers to add additional context to their files and transforming them into actionable content. In the current iteration, it's used to organize, discover, annotate, secure, and retain content. Metadata Platform adoption continues to grow exponentially as more Box products, like Shield, Relay, Sign, Governance, etc, rely on it internally and as our customers continue to build custom applications leveraging it.

But, we've only scratched the surface of what's possible. That's where you come in!

As we embark on the mission to deliver a next-generation Metadata Platform, we're looking for a Senior Engineer to join us and play a pivotal role. You'll have the opportunity to work with a small team of talented, collaborative, and fun engineers, solving some of the toughest challenges, as we build out the future of content management in the cloud. The work you do will have an immediate and lasting impact on the productivity of millions of users, at some of the most important enterprises of our time.

• Design and implement scalable services with a focus on reliability, observability, operability and efficiency.

• Work with cutting-edge technologies like Kubernetes, Docker, BigTable, and Istio.

• Be heavily involved in setting the platform vision and defining feature roadmaps.

• Mentor other engineers and contribute to team growth and development.

jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

PROPULSION ENGINEER, AVIONICS MANUFACTURING (RAPTOR)

The Raptor Avionics team is responsible for the design, manufacturing and test of all the avionics installed on Raptor engines. As propulsion engineer on the Raptor avionics manufacturing team, you will be working to development, qualification, automation various manufacturing and test processes as well as scale up our in-house production capability across a wide range of avionics hardware including PCBAs, sensors, harnessing, and more.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Build the line that builds the parts.

• Develop and qualify manufacturing processes necessary for avionics production. Question requirements, delete parts & processes, simplify & optimize, accelerate, and automate

• Maintain a sense of holistic ownership over the production line, including process consistency, quality, tooling, capital equipment, ergonomics, and safety

• Create and maintain production work instructions, training documents and maintenance planning

• Oversee introduction and implementation of new products and product revisions, frequently multiple at a given time

• Interface with vendors, supply chain and internal teams for new product & change introduction

• Partner with production teams to ensure on-time delivery of flight-ready hardware

• Investigate failures, document findings, and drive corrective actions

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline

• 1+ years of experience working within a manufacturing environment (internships may be included)

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Advanced knowledge of various physical sensors and how they are operated, designed, and manufactured

• Experience with instrumentation and electronics packaging for harsh environments

• Experience in a high volume manufacturing environment

• Experience with specialize processes such as wire bonding, laser welding, epoxy dispense, or soldering

• Ability and desire to work in a dynamic, fast-paced, team environment

• Data analysis experience with Python, MATLAB, Minitab or other data analysis tools

• Excellent communication and teamwork skills

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• This is a hands-on position that will require standing for long durations of your day and working directly with hardware on the floor

• Position may require occasional travel, long hours, or weekend work

Level 2: $115,000.00 - $160,000.00

Role Overview:

The Accounts Payable (AP) Analyst is responsible for performing full-cycle accounts payable functions, including processing, verifying, and reconciling invoices and payments for vendors and service providers across all dental practices within the organization. jobs.title: Senior Staff Privacy Engineer - Moveworks
jobs.description:
Our AI products rely on sensitive data to enable customers to get work done. With this in mind, privacy is a crucial part of ensuring that data is handled properly throughout the workflow, from what we collect and how we use it to the controls we apply across models, tools, logs and data pipelines. In this role, you will be a key privacy engineer, writing code and shaping the architecture and protections across our products. You will improve sensitive data detection and masking, assess the privacy risks of ML models, and own the implementation of customer data-use and retention controls. You will work with our Privacy, ML, Security, Product and Infrastructure teams from design through production.

This is a Senior Staff individual contributor role. You will be hands on, setting technical direction across teams and writing production code.

What you get to do in this role:

• Assess, benchmark and select ML models and techniques that meet our privacy requirements. Build representative evaluation datasets and compare detection coverage, false positives, latency, cost and the impact on product quality.
• Own the implementation of those models in our products, from prototype through production. Train or fine-tune where needed, build the surrounding services and APIs, and optimize inference performance and reliability.
• Build and deploy sensitive data detection, masking, redaction and tokenization for structured and unstructured data across logs, traces, APIs, analytics and annotation tools. Implement consistent controls for when data is masked and who can access the unmasked content.
• Build privacy evaluations for ML models and the systems around them, including memorization, training-data extraction, membership inference and sensitive data disclosure through retrieval or tool use. Implement mitigations and add regression tests to model and product release workflows.
• Write and maintain code that enforces customer requirements for data use, access, retention and deletion across services and data stores, including the distinction between permitted inference, evaluation, annotation and training.
• Prototype and implement privacy-preserving approaches to evaluation and synthetic data. Measure privacy risk and utility, validate the assumptions behind the approach, and integrate suitable solutions into our ML pipelines.
• Conduct privacy design reviews with engineering, identify gaps in proposed data flows and architectures, and own or partner on the code changes needed to address them. Build reusable components and engineering standards that help teams apply these protections consistently.
• Monitor privacy controls and models in production, investigate failures, and ship improvements. Use error analysis and production feedback to improve detection quality, address regressions and close customer-reported privacy issues.

What success looks like in your first year:

• ML models selected and deployed for priority privacy use cases, with measured improvements in detection quality and acceptable production latency and cost.
• Shared masking and data protection components integrated into the highest-priority product surfaces, with automated tests for coverage and access behavior.
• Repeatable privacy evaluations running as part of model and product releases, with findings translated into shipped fixes.
• Priority data-use, retention and deletion requirements implemented and verified in production, with monitoring that identifies failures.

To be successful in this role you have:

• Typically 7+ or more years building production software, including substantial experience in privacy engineering and applied ML.
• Strong Python skills and experience with Go, Java, C++ or another production systems language. You have shipped, tested and operated production software.
• Hands-on experience evaluating, selecting and deploying ML models, including dataset curation, model adaptation or fine-tuning, error analysis and model serving.
• Experience building sensitive data detection and masking systems, including their accuracy, performance and integration tradeoffs.
• Experience assessing privacy risks in ML and LLM systems and implementing mitigations. You can explain what your tests establish and where uncertainty remains.
• Deep understanding of data minimization, pseudonymization, anonymization and re-identification risk, including the limits of removing direct identifiers.
• Experience building data protection and lifecycle controls in distributed cloud systems.
• A record of taking ambiguous engineering problems from design through delivery, setting technical direction across teams and mentoring engineers.

Preferred experience:

• Applying differential privacy or other privacy-enhancing technologies, including evaluating their assumptions and privacy-utility tradeoffs.
• Privacy engineering for agentic systems, retrieval-augmented generation, embeddings or synthetic datasets.
• Experience in enterprise, multi-tenant or regulated environments, and translating privacy requirements such as GDPR and CCPA into technical controls.

jobs.title: Business Operations Lead
jobs.description:
GiveCampus is the world's leading fundraising platform for non-profit educational institutions. Trusted by millions of donors and 1,300+ colleges, universities, and K-12 schools, our mission is to help advance the quality, the affordability, and the accessibility of education. At our current pace, we will facilitate $100 billion in charitable giving over the next decade–enough money to send more than 1 million students to college, tuition-free.

GiveCampus is backed by leading investors including Y Combinator, but we’re also practitioners of Sustainable Growth: we’ve made the Inc. 5000 list of America's fastest-growing private companies each of the last five years and we’ve been profitable nine of the last 10. In 2025, we celebrated a $140 million growth investment that included a major liquidity event for GiveCampus employees–the second in less than three years.

Our purpose-driven team of 130+ is located in 30+ states across the US: team members work from anywhere they choose. We have a beautiful 12,000sf office in Washington, DC that is available for people to use whenever they want, and we regularly organize team meet-ups, visit partner institutions, and host retreats in various locations.

While we operate at meaningful scale, we’re still small relative to the commercial and social good opportunities in front of us. Every GiveCampus employee plays a meaningful role in shaping what comes next, and we're growing the team in support of our ambitious plans–including a $100 million investment in AI product development. If you believe in the transformative power of education and want to join a fast-growing, mission-driven company, you’ll fit right in.

Location: This is a remote-first role based in the U.S. While we embrace flexible, distributed work, we also value in-person connection. Team members are expected to attend multiple company-wide and team-specific onsites throughout the year.

GiveCampus is looking for a Business Operations Lead. Business Operations at GiveCampus is inspired by Claire Hughes Johnson’s take in Scaling People, where she describes it as “a team staffed with folks who have a mix of consulting and entrepreneurial backgrounds, who thrive on new situations and on solving problems.”

Many job descriptions contain the phrase “other duties as assigned.” In Business Operations, that is your job description, with one important caveat: you play an important role in assigning, too. In other words, Business Operations team members solve challenging problems our company needs them to prioritize, and they also identify problems we should be solving, raise them, get buy-in, prioritize, take ownership, and partner across the company to solve them.

We expect the impact of you joining the team to be immediate and felt across the organization: as you succeed, team members will report that we execute better, we execute faster, we make better decisions, and we serve our partners (customers) better, all in pursuit of our vision.

Finally, you will work with our partners. We believe the only way you can identify the problems to solve is by talking to – and listening – to our users. You will do both, regularly, and use their insights to shape and prioritize our work. Many people who meet our Business Operations team ask, “why do you spend so much time with users?” That is in fact the primary way we learn how to positively impact our team and partners.

What we’re looking for:

• 12+ years of related experience, including SaaS experience in B2B or B2C companies, with experience ranging anywhere from 0 to 1 all the way to scaling larger organizations

• Someone who gets it done. We will do whatever it takes to help our company and our partners succeed. As the adage goes, “if you want to get something done, find the busiest person, and ask them to do it.” We’re looking for you, “get stuff done” person.

• A point of view on our industry: what does the future of fundraising look like? What role does GiveCampus play? And what do we need to do today to move the industry forward?

• A passion for strategy, execution, and data. We will think big about the future. We will execute with rigor (tight plans, high expectations, and exceptional focus) with a focus on business outcomes. You are comfortable communicating with impact in front of leadership while simultaneously digging deep in Claude, Snowflake, Salesforce, Notion, and other tools, interpreting financial data, and understanding nuances in our business model.

• Someone who looks at a goal that seems impossible to achieve and by default asks their peers “well, what would it take to double it?”

• The experiential learning pro. You know how to create amazing experiences for our people during in-person and virtual experiences.

• Strong business acumen: communicate with impact across the organization, and translate complex OKRs / KPIs into meaningful tactics and areas of focus for our team; leverage your understanding of the macro environment, industry trends, and business performance and translate that into “what does this mean for me?”

We have only one quality that is non-negotiable: consistently bring energy, optimism, and enthusiasm to your work and our team.

The ultimate measure is our ability to hit our KRs. Overall responsibilities to achieve them may include:

• Make things work better: Identify opportunities to improve the way we work and operate: become more efficient, effective, and scalable. This may include scoping out the vision for a new process or system, partnering with other teams to implement, and / or removing friction and inefficiency between departments throughout the company, etc. Develop new ways of doing things: Plan, lead, and execute on strategic projects, determined in collaboration with Department and Company Leadership. Validate the ROI is there: Confirm initiatives are having intended impact by seeking feedback, reviewing usage, and measuring results at defined points after projects are completed. Communicate with GiveCampers: Identify and prioritize key communications vehicles and share our progress with the company, creating meaningful experiences for our people

Please note this role requires travel of 20%.

Location Preference: This is a remote position, with a strong preference for candidates residing in Chicago.

Ready to apply?

Be sure to keep an eye on your spam and promotions boxes in case our emails end up there!

At GiveCampus, we value diversity and we pledge to foster an environment of support, inclusivity, and learning, both on the job and throughout the application process. In this spirit, we encourage candidates of all backgrounds to apply.

GiveCampus is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Applicants and employees are not discriminated against because of race, color, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, religion, national origin, citizenship status, disability, ancestry, marital status, veteran status, medical condition or any protected category prohibited by local, state or federal laws.

If you feel like you don't meet all of the requirements for this role, please apply anyways. We know confidence gaps and imposter syndrome often get in the way of connecting with incredible people, and we don't want them to prevent us from meeting you.

jobs.title: Account Manager - Charleston SC
jobs.description:

jobs.description:
Primary function of position

The Technical Program Manager for Country-Specific Labeling (CSL) owns end-to-end delivery and long-term support of Intuitive’s custom CSL system, from architecture and design through implementation and at sites throughout the world and manage continuous improvements and feature enhancements. You will translate multi-country Regulatory Affairs requirements into scalable system requirements, labeling schemas, and templates, and drive integration with SAP and warehouse management systems. You will lead cross-functional execution across IT, Quality, Regulatory, warehouse logistics, and label suppliers, including UAT planning and go-live readiness, to ensure compliant and efficient labeling. This role sits within Technical Services, reporting to the Product Labeling & Packaging Operations Manager.

Roles and responsibilities

Essential duties

• Own the end-to-end CSL program, serving as the primary driver for planning, execution, delivery, and stakeholder alignment across RA, IT, Quality, Operations, suppliers, and logistics sites.
• Lead Country-Specific Labeling requirements management, partnering with Regulatory Affairs (RA/RSAs) to interpret country regulatory assessments and convert them into clear, testable requirements.
• Drive schema development with IT/engineering teams by defining requirements, acceptance criteria, traceability, and change impacts; ensure schemas are scalable and aligned to enterprise standards.
• Lead integration delivery for labeling capabilities with SAP and warehouse management systems, coordinating dependencies, interface readiness, and cutover planning.
• Coordinate with warehouse logistics teams and external partners to implement labeling workflows, including label printing/handling, verification steps, exception management, and training/readiness.
• Facilitate label template design discussions to ensure templates work as expected across countries, products, printer constraints, and warehouse execution.
• Manage workstreams related to supplier-printed labels, including specifications alignment, readiness tracking, issue triage, and operational deployment coordination.
• Define and structure User Acceptance Testing (UAT) for labeling (test strategy, test cases, traceability, execution coordination, defect management, and sign-off).
• Partner with Quality to manage labeling-related non-conformances (NCs) and CAPAs, supporting investigation coordination, corrective action execution, and effectiveness checks.
• Establish and maintain program documentation (program plans, RAID logs, requirements traceability, SOP/work instructions impacts, release notes) and drive standardization of CSL delivery processes.
• Drive continuous improvement initiatives to reduce labeling errors, shorten cycle times, improve audit readiness, and strengthen operational controls.

Education, experience, skills and training

Education and experience

• Minimum of bachelor’s degree in engineering or a related field.
• Minimum of 8+ years of experience working in labeling, hardware, system production, or test environment primarily in healthcare industry.

Technical skills

• Lead technical, cross-functional programs end-to-end (requirements → build/config → testing → deployment) in a regulated and/or operationally complex environment.
• Strong ability to translate regulatory labeling requirements into system requirements, schemas, templates, and warehouse-operational processes.
• Demonstrated ability to coordinate across RA, IT/engineering, Quality, warehouse operations/logistics, suppliers, and external partners (3PLs).
• Hands-on experience running UAT (planning, traceability, execution coordination, defect triage, and release readiness).
• Experience building and maintaining enterprise program artifacts: requirements traceability, release governance, cutover plans, training/readiness, and stakeholder reporting.

Other skills and abilities

• Able to learn and apply established procedures in a reliable and consistent manner.
• Strong communication skills (written and verbal) with the ability to drive alignment, decisions, and execution across multiple stakeholders.
• Ability to lead and deliver in a matrix environment.
• Strong problem-solving skills and ability to be self-managed in a fast-paced environment utilizing agile/sprint methodologies.
• Quick learner with ability to understand complex products and processes.
• Ability to work in a team environment.
• High level of attention to technical details and accuracy.
• Ability to work independently and with minimal supervision
• Ability to multitask, and handle tasks with competing priorities effectively
• Proficient with MS Office applications

jobs.title: Associate Director, Policy
jobs.description:
About Us

Social Finance is a national nonprofit and registered investment adviser expanding economic opportunity in America. We bring government, philanthropy, and business leaders together to improve systems and put capital to work in new ways. Since our founding in 2011, we have mobilized more than $500 million to create measurable results in workforce and education, health, and housing.

We are driven by the belief that social and economic systems should enable all people to thrive, and the conviction that we can create the most meaningful and measurable change in our communities when governments and markets work together. Our organization is built upon five core values: people, performance, integrity, collaboration, and inclusion.

Our work spans four areas: Impact-first Investing, Workforce and Education Investments, Advisory & Public Sector Practice, and the Social Finance Institute. Our Impact-first Investment team designs, launches, and manages investments that provide solutions for effectively deploying impact capital across a range of social outcomes. Our Workforce and Education Investments team designs, launches and manages financial solutions focused on addressing workforce challenges, including skills acquisition and training access. Our Advisory team partners with government and philanthropy leaders to implement data-driven programs for advancing social impact. And through the Social Finance Institute, we aim to build the field and change systems through actionable research, communities of practice, and educational outreach.

The Opportunity

The Social Finance Institute is seeking an Associate Director of Policy to help advance a growing portfolio of policy research, analysis, and engagement. Working closely with the Head of Policy and other Institute team members, the Associate Director will support projects that translate research and practice into actionable insights for policymakers and other influential audiences.

The ideal candidate brings a strong understanding of the federal policymaking process, excellent writing and analytical skills, and experience engaging policymakers and diverse external stakeholders. Congressional experience (legislative assistant, policy adviser, or committee staff) is highly valued, particularly in domestic policy areas related to finance, economic development, workforce development, government effectiveness, or philanthropy.

This is an opportunity for a thoughtful and entrepreneurial policy professional to help shape a growing policy function and advance ideas with the potential to improve public systems and expand economic opportunity.

Responsibilities

Project Management

• Coordinate targeted applied research projects led by external researchers, policy experts, and partner organizations

• Develop project plans, timelines, research questions, and deliverables; coordinate contributors; keep projects on schedule and to high standards of quality

• Support the Institute’s research portfolio by identifying emerging questions, potential research partners, and opportunities to connect research with policy and practice

Policy Research and Analysis

• Monitor and analyze federal and state legislative, regulatory, and policy developments relevant to Social Finance’s work, including impact investing and outcomes-based funding for economic mobility in workforce development, housing, and public safety net programs

• Contribute to policy research, landscape analyses, and other projects that inform the Institute’s research and policy agenda

• Assess the implications of emerging policy developments for Social Finance’s programs, partners, and broader fields of work

• Translate complex research, legislation, and policy developments into clear, practical insights for policymakers, practitioners, funders, and other audiences

• Research and draft policy briefs, issue papers, blog posts, presentations, memos, talking points, public comments, and other educational materials

• Work with the Head of Policy and Institute colleagues to develop evidence-informed policy recommendations and communicate them to federal and state audiences

• Collaborate with communications colleagues to disseminate Institute research and elevate Social Finance’s expertise in policy conversations

• Ensure the Institute’s written products are accessible, nonpartisan, and tailored to their intended audiences

Policymaker and Stakeholder Engagement

• Build and maintain relationships with congressional and executive branch staff, state policymakers, researchers, advocates, practitioners, funders, and other stakeholders

• Represent the Social Finance Institute in coalition meetings, policy briefings, conferences, and other external forums

• Identify and help organize opportunities to showcase Social Finance’s work with policymakers, including briefings, roundtables, convenings, testimony, and educational activities

• Convene and facilitate conversations among policymakers, researchers, practitioners, and other stakeholders to advance shared policy objectives

• Work effectively across political and ideological perspectives while maintaining Social Finance’s nonpartisan approach

Organizational Contributions

• Connect policy and research activities with Social Finance’s programmatic experience and institutional priorities

• Contribute to proposals, funder reports, work plans, and other materials supporting the Institute’s growth and sustainability

• Support additional Institute priorities and special projects as needed

Qualifications

Candidates should have:

• Experience working in or closely with the federal legislative or policymaking process. Prior congressional, committee, or federal policy service is strongly preferred.

• Familiarity with one or more domestic policy areas related to Social Finance’s work, such as finance, economic development, workforce development, government effectiveness, or philanthropy

• Experience conducting research or policy analysis and translating findings into practical recommendations

• Demonstrated experience working with policymakers, constituents, coalitions, external partners, or other diverse stakeholders

• Exceptional writing and editing skills, including the ability to communicate complex information clearly to policymaking and nontechnical audiences

• Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills, intellectual curiosity, and sound judgment

• A nuanced understanding of the political and policy environment and the ability to operate effectively in a nonpartisan organization

• Demonstrated ability to manage complex projects, competing priorities, and multiple deadlines, with a high degree of organization and attention to detail

• Ability to work independently, take initiative, set priorities, and solve problems while collaborating effectively with colleagues

• Strong interpersonal and verbal communication skills, including comfort engaging senior policymakers and organizational leaders

Preferred Qualifications

The strongest candidates may also bring:

• Experience developing policy proposals, legislative materials, regulatory comments, or other products for government audiences

• Experience managing external research partnerships or multi-organization projects

• Established relationships with federal policymakers, state policy leaders, researchers, or organizations in relevant fields

• Familiarity with outcomes-based approaches, innovative financing, evidence-based policymaking, or public-sector performance and delivery

Benefits

Salary

jobs.title: GTM Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE COMPANY

Braintrust is the agent observability platform. By actively applying intelligence to agent traces and automatically surfacing the most critical patterns, Braintrust gives teams the visibility to understand how agents behave in production and the tools to improve them.

Teams at Notion, Stripe, Box, OpenAI, and Cloudflare use Braintrust to trace their agents, find the issues in their observability data, and run evals that tell them how to improve.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a GTM engineer who loves building the systems that power the next stage of growth for Braintrust. GTM Engineering is responsible for building the agents, data infrastructure, and internal tools our Sales, Marketing, and RevOps teams use every day to operate more efficiently. The best projects are linked directly to pipeline or revenue and are delivered through interfaces that limit friction for users. This team is uniquely positioned at Braintrust to have a lot of leverage, since it uses our product and is a central part of agentic building.



In this role, you'll focus on:

 - Agents and internal tools: Build and ship agents and applications that GTM teams cannot live without.

 - Data infrastructure: Create models and pipelines connecting our warehouse, enrichment providers, CRM, and product usage data so tools run on data people trust.

 - Stakeholder management: Work closely with Sales and Marketing to understand their workflows and turn messy processes into durable systems.

 - Primitives: Architect compounding systems built on shared primitives that can be reused across projects.

 - Measurement: Measure the impact of what you ship quantitatively and qualitatively and use the feedback and metrics to shape the future roadmap.

 - Reliability: Keep production tools stable and reliable.

 - Building in public: Be on the cutting edge of what's possible with agentic building and share your learnings on X.




IDEAL CANDIDATE CREDENTIALS

 - 3+ years in software engineering, growth/GTM engineering, or data engineering.

 - Understands how B2B GTM works, including pipeline stages, forecasting, territories, and ABM.

 - Comfortable writing SQL, modeling data with dbt, and building pipelines without requiring assistance from others.

 - Has shipped agents that have had real users and knows how to iterate on them.

 - Can hold their own when talking about agentic system design.

 - Is excited to tie their work back to real business metrics and wants to move pipeline and revenue through engineering.

 - Builds systems that compound over time rather than in isolation, and thinks about how what they build today will extend to help the business grow in the future.

 - Has owned problems end-to-end in environments where things are sometimes loosely defined, and is willing to pick up whatever knowledge they’re missing to get the job done.




BENEFITS INCLUDE

 - Medical, dental, and vision insurance

 - Daily lunch, snacks, and beverages

 - Flexible time off

 - Competitive salary and equity

 - Wifi & cellphone stipend 


EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

Braintrust is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status.

jobs.title: Associate General Counsel, GTM & Commercial Legal
jobs.description:
At Qualtrics, we create software the world’s best brands use to deliver exceptional frontline experiences, build high-performing teams, and design products people love. But we are more than a platform—we are the creators and stewards of the Experience Management category serving over 18K clients globally. Building a category takes grit, determination, and a disdain for convention—but most of all it requires close-knit, high-functioning teams with an unwavering dedication to serving our customers.

When you join one of our teams, you’ll be part of a nimble group that’s empowered to set aggressive goals and move fast to achieve them. Strategic risks are encouraged and complex problems are solved together, by passing the mic and iterating until the best solution comes to light. You won’t have to look to find growth opportunities—ready or not, they’ll find you. From retail to government to healthcare, we’re on a mission to bring humanity, connection, and empathy back to business. Join over 5,000 people across the globe who think that’s work worth doing.

Associate General Counsel, GTM & Commercial Legal

Why We Have This Role

As Qualtrics scales globally, our Go-To-Market engine needs a pragmatic, deal-oriented legal leader to drive high-velocity revenue growth while safeguarding the business. Reporting directly to our General Counsel, you will lead the legal strategy for enterprise commercial contracting, partner operations, and go-to-market motions. You will partner shoulder-to-shoulder with our Chief Revenue Officer, Sales Operations, and Finance leaders to simplify deal cycles, unblock strategic enterprise negotiations, and scale our commercial legal architecture. This is a critical leadership post where you will turn legal into a true business accelerant across an 18K+ customer portfolio.

How You’ll Find Success

• Commercially Minded & Solution-Oriented: You view legal not as a blocker, but as an enabler of revenue. You solve complex contractual impasses with creative, risk-balanced compromises.

• Executive Presence & Influence: You build immediate trust with C-suite stakeholders, sales executives, and enterprise procurement leaders alike, translating intricate legal nuances into clear business decisions.

• Operational Architect: You enjoy designing systems, playbooks, and standardized terms that empower teams to move quickly without constant escalation.

• Bias for Action: You thrive in fast-paced deal environments, knowing when an 80/20 solution delivers maximum business momentum without sacrificing compliance.

• Empowering People Leader: You inspire, mentor, and elevate a high-performing team of commercial attorneys and contract managers, fostering high accountability and personal growth.

• Decisive Risk Prioritization: You possess the judgment to separate critical enterprise exposures from routine commercial risks, keeping deals moving smoothly.

How You’ll Grow

• Direct Executive Exposure: Partner closely with the General Counsel and executive leadership on boardroom-level go-to-market initiatives, strategic partnerships, and commercial governance.

• Enterprise Transformation Leadership: Lead the evolution of AI-driven legal operations and contracting workflows, setting new industry benchmarks for B2B SaaS deal velocity.

• Broadened Strategic Scope: Expand your legal and operational leadership beyond traditional commercial transactions into international expansion strategy, revenue recognition policy, and ecosystem partnerships.

Things You’ll Do

• Accelerate Sales Cycle Velocity: Modernize contract workflows, fallbacks, and self-service guidelines to shorten enterprise deal turnaround times while preserving core risk guardrails.

• Lead Complex Enterprise Deal Negotiations: Serve as the executive escalation point and lead negotiator for mission-critical, high-value customer and other revenue-generating contracts.

• Scale Global Commercial Operations: Partner with Sales Ops to integrate automated contract management tools and AI review workflows, eliminating contracting bottlenecks.

• Foster Cross-Functional Alignment: Maintain strong, regular operational cadence with Revenue Leadership, InfoSec, Product, and Finance to ensure clean revenue recognition and smooth customer onboarding.

• Develop and Inspire Talent: Lead, scale, and mentor the GTM Commercial Legal team, fostering a culture of ownership, deal-making excellence, and continuous learning.

What We’re Looking For On Your Resume

• Proven track record leading commercial legal teams or enterprise GTM deal desks within a high-growth, global enterprise SaaS or technology organization.

• Extensive experience negotiating complex, high-value agreements, governing cloud, data processing (GDPR, CCPA), cybersecurity, and IP provisions with Fortune 500 procurement teams.

• Demonstrated success modernizing commercial legal infrastructure—implementing playbooks, CLM tooling, or self-serve mechanisms that materially reduced deal cycle times.

• History of direct cross-functional partnership with sales leadership (VPs of Sales, CRO, Deal Desk) to hit quarterly revenue and margin targets.

• Experience in contracting within Public Sector is a plus.

• J.D. from an accredited law school and active bar admission in good standing in at least one U.S. jurisdiction.

• At least 15 years of experience is preferred.

What You Should Know About This Team

• Seat at the Revenue Table: We operate as integrated business partners embedded in the sales flow, not an isolated back-office function.

• High Trust, High Autonomy: We pass the mic, encourage calculated risk-taking, and support one another in solving novel problems without micromanagement.

• Impact Over Bureaucracy: We value actionable solutions, clear communication, and outcomes that directly affect company trajectory over legalese and endless memos.

• Unwavering Commitment to People: We invest heavily in professional development, ensuring our attorneys build the skills and visibility needed for future GC and C-level executive roles.

Our Team’s Favorite Perks and Benefits

• Wellness & Mental Health Support: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, alongside company-paid access to premium mental health platforms and wellness reimbursements.

• Generous Parental Leave & Family Planning: Robust paid parental leave programs and family-building assistance support you through all phases of life.

• Continuous Learning & Bar Stipend: Dedicated annual budget covering continuing legal education (CLE), and professional bar associations.

• Employee Resource Groups (QGroups): Vibrant, company-supported communities focused on fostering inclusion, belonging, and connection across the organization.

The Qualtrics Hybrid Work Model: Our hybrid work model is elegantly simple: we all gather in the office three days a week; Mondays and Thursdays, plus one day selected by your organizational leader. These purposeful in-person days in thoughtfully designed offices help us do our best work and harness the power of collaboration and innovation. For the rest of the week, work where you want, owning the integration of work and life. #remote

jobs.title: Float Phlebotomist / Administrative Assistant (Easton Office)
jobs.description:
About Us

One Medical is a primary care solution challenging the industry status quo by making quality care more affordable, accessible and enjoyable. But this isn’t your average doctor’s office. We’re on a mission to transform healthcare, which means improving the experience for everyone involved - from patients and providers to employers and health networks. Our seamless in-office and 24/7 virtual care services, on-site labs, and programs for preventive care, chronic care management, common illnesses and mental health concerns have been delighting people for the past fifteen years.

In February 2023 we marked a milestone when One Medical joined Amazon. Together, we look to deliver exceptional health care to more consumers, employers, care team members, and health networks to achieve better health outcomes. As we continue to grow and seek to impact more lives, we’re building a diverse, driven and empathetic team, while working hard to cultivate an environment where everyone can thrive.

The Opportunity

As a One Medical Phlebotomist/Administrative Assistant, internally known as Lab Services Specialist/Member Support Specialist, at one of our offices, you’ll provide an exceptional experience for our patients and help them accomplish an important part of their care journey by providing venipuncture as well as other clinical support services. You will be an ambassador for patients, with a mastery of human connection and a strong drive for service. You will remove barriers to care, resulting in a truly exceptional in-office patient experience. You are the steward of the space and ensure the look and feel of the office lobby are on brand with the One Medical experience. You will be the first point of contact for our patients, as well as provide any other support as requested by the Practice Coordinator, Operations Manager, or providers.

You are a strong team player and use your innovative problem solving skills to tackle various tasks and challenges. You combine excellent specimen collection technique with tactful interpersonal skills during every interaction with your patients, at both the front desk and in the lab. You have a strong grasp of verbal and written communication. You are able to identify opportunities and deliver on customer-centric solutions while using empathy, focus, and compassion in all interactions with patients and teammates. You bring self-awareness to your daily work to utilize your strengths and develop your areas of opportunity. You thrive in cultures that focus on feedback and growth and are nimble in their approach to respond to the needs of the patients and team. You have an unwavering drive to help and serve others and create amazing moments for our members and teammates. If this sounds like you, we would love to connect.

What you’ll likely work on:

• Use impeccable C-I-CARE (a framework containing the key elements of a great interaction and effective communication that we use with patients and each other) in all patient interactions, both clinical and administrative, and ensure a fluid and positive in-office experience through patient intake, same day schedule management, appropriate follow up scheduling, strong knowledge of billing and insurance, monitoring patient feedback and assisting with outreach as necessary

• Provide best in class venipuncture services on a population ranging from pediatrics to geriatrics, depending on the office location

• Perform and assist with extended scope duties such as, but not limited to non-blood specimen collection, EKGs/ECGs, vitals, ear lavages, vaccines, PPD tests, and swabs

• Maintain high standards of in-office care through proper specimen labeling, handling and processing, inventory upkeep, and tool sterilization

• Continue to care for our members beyond the lab room by answering patient messages, following up on lab cases and assisting our providers and virtual medical team with clerical duties such as, but not limited to biometric screening forms, medical record and consult review, billing inquiries, and DOH reporting

• All front of house duties including check in/check out, insurance verification, printing/paperwork tasks, prepping tests, tasking to service level expectations etc

• Contribute to team development through rounding, attending team huddles, participating in team problem solving, supporting in office providers with ad hoc asks, etc.

• Perform opening and closing duties/daily office upkeep as required, including maintaining the look and feel of both patient and employee facing spaces, restocking supplies, and organization

• Master our technology suite including, but not limited to Slack, G-suite, Zoom, Circulation, RingCentral, and our Electronic Medical Record System, in order to interact with team members and complete daily work

These responsibilities are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by personnel assigned to this job classification. They are not to be construed as an exhaustive list of job duties performed by personnel in this classification. Other job related duties may be assigned by management.

What you’ll need:

• At least 6 months of relevant experience as a Medical Assistant or Phlebotomist outside of a training/externship environment

• Strong customer service skills, including ability to establish and maintain effective customer relationships and deliver customer-centric solutions

• Strong written and verbal communication skills

• A High School Diploma or equivalent

• Proficiency in computer technology such as typing, navigating the internet and using multiple software systems simultaneously

• Experience working on collaborative, diverse, multi-disciplinary teams (additional experience with remote teams a plus)

• A proven ability to display confidence and instill trust during the collection process while delivering individualized, human-centered, customer-focused care

• A proven track record of persisting through change, consistently stepping up to take action on challenges, and learning quickly and effectively when faced with new situations or tasks

Competitive salary: starts at $20.25 per hour based on a full time schedule

The range for this role is $20.25 to $22.25 per hour based on a standard full-time schedule. Total compensation packages may be based on factors unique to particular candidates, such as skill sets, depth of experience, and work location. The total compensation package for this position may also include benefits. For more information, visit https://www.onemedical.com/careers/

This is a full time role (40 hours/week) with 8 hour shifts generally taking place between 7am-7pm based in office in Columbus, Ohio at our Easton office and providing as needed support to the New Albany and Dublin office locations.

1099 Clinical Opportunities

FUTURE OPPORTUNITIES ONLY: This is an interest form for potential future independent contractor opportunities at Parsley Health, not a currently available contract. There is no specific opening or hiring timeline associated with this posting.

Interested in working with Parsley Health? Let's connect.

Parsley Health is the leading functional healthcare company in the U.S., founded by Dr. Robin Berzin with a mission to transform how we treat chronic conditions through root-cause, whole-person medicine.

Our clinicians combine advanced diagnostics, personalized lifestyle interventions, and meaningful patient relationships to help members improve their health. We provide the clinical tools, resources, and collaborative support needed to deliver excellent care.

We're always interested in connecting with experienced MDs, DOs, NPs, and PAs who may be interested in providing care to Parsley members on a part-time, independent contractor basis.

Whether you have your own practice, work with other organizations, or are exploring additional clinical opportunities, we'd love to learn more about you.

Why reach out now?

One of the first things we do when we're looking for additional clinical coverage is review clinicians who have already expressed interest in working with Parsley.

Our needs are often very specific. We may need a clinician licensed in a particular state, available for a certain number of hours or on specific days, or someone with a particular area of clinical expertise or functional medicine training.

By sharing your licenses, experience, background, and ideal availability now, you're helping us understand where there might be a fit before we even have a specific opening.

By the time we publicly post an opportunity, we may already be speaking with clinicians whose qualifications and availability match what we need.

Whether you're actively looking for additional work, considering expanding your practice, or simply open to future opportunities, we'd encourage you to connect with us now.

What contracting with Parsley could look like

Depending on our future clinical needs, opportunities may include:

• Part-time independent contractor arrangements with varying weekly commitments

• Virtual patient care, with potential in-person opportunities depending on location and need

• Collaboration with our clinical team, including health coaches and RN care managers

• Access to Parsley's clinical technology platform and resources

• The ability to maintain an independent practice or other professional commitments, subject to applicable disclosure, conflict-of-interest, confidentiality, and patient protection requirements

• Parsley provides malpractice coverage for care delivered to our members. Independent contractors are responsible for maintaining their own required licenses and associated expenses.

Who we'd love to connect with

• Licensed MDs, DOs, NPs, and PAs with active state licensure and applicable board certification

• Clinicians with 3+ years of relevant clinical experience, ideally in primary care

• Clinicians with professional experience practicing functional, integrative, or longevity medicine

• Clinicians who have completed or are pursuing formal functional medicine training or certifications

• People who value personalized patient care, clinical collaboration, and flexibility

• Functional medicine experience and formal training are especially valuable to us, but we also welcome interest from clinicians who are earlier in their functional medicine journey.

Tell us what you're looking for

Our application asks about your clinical credentials, state licenses, functional medicine experience, formal training and certifications, ideal availability, hourly rate expectations, and what interests you about working with Parsley.

We'll also ask whether you're actively seeking additional clinical work or would consider an opportunity sometime in the future.

We'll review your information when relevant opportunities arise and reach out if there's a potential fit between your qualifications, interests, availability, and our clinical needs.

There is no need to wait for an active opportunity to introduce yourself!

Please note: This is an expression of interest in potential future independent contractor arrangements, not an application for a currently available contract. Submitting your information does not guarantee an interview, engagement, or a specific response timeline. Any future contractor arrangement is subject to applicable legal and clinical requirements.

Parsley Health is committed to equal opportunity and building an inclusive clinical team.

Important note: If you're selected to move forward in a future selection process, a member of our Talent Acquisition team will contact you from an @parsleyhealth.com email address. We will never conduct interviews through Microsoft Teams, request your banking information during recruitment, or send you a check to purchase equipment.

jobs.title: Production Scheduler
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE SITE

Anduril, a leader in autonomous systems and weapons manufacturing, is building Arsenal-1, its first hyperscale manufacturing facility, just south of Columbus, Ohio in Pickaway County. Arsenal-1 is redefining the scale and speed that autonomous systems and weapons can be produced for the United States and its allies and partners. This is a monumental and essential step toward rebuilding America’s defense industrial base, strengthening America’s warfighting capabilities, and enhancing deterrence amid rising international threats.

ABOUT THE PRODUCT

The future of defense is being built right now, and Anduril’s Roadrunner product is at its leading edge. Roadrunner is a cutting-edge VTOL (Vertical Take-Off and Landing) counter-UAS interceptor, designed for autonomous air defense operations. It rapidly detects, tracks, and neutralizes hostile unmanned aircraft systems to protect critical assets and personnel.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Roadrunner Team (RLT) will set the standard for building the future at Arsenal-1, our state-of-the-art manufacturing facility in Ashville, OH. This team will have the opportunity to train under our world-class manufacturing team at Anduril HQ in Costa Mesa, CA for 3 months before bringing that standard of excellence back to Ohio.

ABOUT THE JOB

This role is about much more than just processes; it's about orchestrating the industrialization of a vital product. You will own the entire manufacturing value-chain for Roadrunner, from current rate to high-volume deployment. Your responsibilities will span the spectrum: driving Design for Manufacturability (DFM) feedback into design, innovating tool design and selection, creating and optimizing high-rate production lines, fostering strategic vendor partnerships, embedding robust quality assurance throughout, and meticulously documenting build processes.

If you thrive under the pressure of scaling a critical product with immediate, real-world impact, we want you to help us build the next generation of Roadrunner products.

**This role requires candidates to relocate to Costa Mesa for a 3-month training program. Housing, transportation, etc. will be provided during your stay.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Execute the manufacturing of a certain product or set of products, from initial prototyping through large full-scale production.

• Work with design engineers during the development process to drive design for manufacturing best practices into the design effort, and help facilitate the transition from design to prototype to rate production.

• Act as a manufacturing liason for mechanical fabrication and avionics with subject matter expertise in these areas and key experience in design for manufacturability.

• Own documentation required for successfully manufacturing product group hardware at scale, such as MBOM’s, work instructions & requirements, etc.

• Advise on quality management and business application programs as they pertain to manufacturing within your area.

• Collaborate with internal customers and manufacturing planning teams to define capacity planning actions to meet customer needs and expectations.

• Analyze metrics for continuous improvement initiatives (cost reduction, QI reduction & capacity increase).

• Instill a culture of innovation, teamwork, and accountability within the manufacturing engineering product team.

• Develop production and test methodologies and implement best practices to enable scaling production capabilities for larger, more complex products.

• Travel to suppliers and partner sites to do initial sourcing work, solve ongoing production issues, and implement process procedures as required.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Degree in a technical field preferred such as engineering, math, or a hard science

• 3+ years of experience in a relevant field, preferably manufacturing or design of electromechanical hardware

• Demonstrated ability to creatively deliver electromechanical hardware in a resource-constrained environment

• An attitude of world-class mission assurance, quality, attention to detail, and dedication.

• A genuine interest in manufacturing and thirst for learning

• Candidates must demonstrate flexibility and dedication, being prepared to work extended hours and weekends when dictated by critical business priorities

• Regular travel between our various locations is an essential component of this role

• U.S. Citizen Required

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Exposure to aircraft programs or other relevant aerospace & defense technologies

• Software scripting experience in any language

• Lean Six Sigma certification (Green Belt or higher) or equivalent experience

• Familiarity with J-STD-001, IPC-A-610, and IPC/WHMA-A-620 or equivalent standards

US Salary Range

$99,000—$131,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

• No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

• Please always verify communications: Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address. Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

• Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

• What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.
