jobs.title: Regional Director of Academics
jobs.description:
ACCEL Schools is seeking a highly motivated Regional Director of Academics in Cincinnati, OH dedicated to creating a rigorous and nurturing environment that prioritizes student engagement and achievement for all students.

With a network of 100 charter schools and growing, ACCEL Schools employs a diverse staff of passionate administrators and educators who value research-based practices and a desire to grow as professionals. We work tirelessly to raise student achievement, regardless of historical barriers, while committed to participating in ongoing professional development, job embedded instructional coaching, and embracing a growth mindset.  The Regional Director of Academics is crucial to their success.

The Regional Director of Academics serves as part of the school leadership teams, providing job-embedded and ongoing professional development for Directors of Academics, teachers, staff, and administration. He/she provides support to the principal and school staffs in data analysis and professional development decision-making. He/she provides professional development and guidance for Directors of Academics to improve their content knowledge and effective delivery of coaching. Overall, the job of the Regional Director of Academics is to build the capacity of the schools and its teachers to meet the learning needs of all students. The Regional Director of Academics' goal is to ensure that school staff acquires the understanding and skills to enhance instructional practices at the classroom level and raise the level of student academic achievement.

Essential Role:

• Participation and/or delivery in all required Director of Academics professional development. The Regional Director of Academics is charged with acquiring the knowledge, skills, technology skills, and instructional strategies to effectively impact the instructional practices of the teachers that are coached. He/she must remain knowledgeable about current and past research in the specific content area and other pedagogies relevant to the coaching

• Identification of the school teaching and learning needs, barriers and weaknesses by analyzing student data, and organizing and implementing problem-solving actions.

• Monitor instructional effectiveness and student progress using tools and strategies gained through professional development.

• Work collaboratively with ACCEL Shared Services teams and the Regional Vice President to ensure alignment on goals and strategies for each school.

• Assistance in collaborative development of district-wide diagnostic and benchmark

• Provide continuous and targeted professional development for the Director of Academics that directly supports the school curriculum and instruction that ensures continuous student achievement of the school’s academic standards;

• Performance of additional tasks and responsibilities as assigned

• On-site support daily to schools on an assigned schedule

Required Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university

• Valid Ohio teaching credential authorizing services in the area of responsibility

• Experience in differentiated instruction in a standards-based curriculum

• Required training and certification for the content area(s)

• Minimum 3 or more years of successful Instructional Coaching

• Evidence of leadership roles

Required Experience:

The effectiveness of any coaching initiative hinges on the selection of a candidate that is highly qualified as a teacher, knowledgeable in content, and skilled in the sophisticated practices of coaching. The Regional Director of Academics must meet the following criteria:

• demonstrate deep knowledge of the relevant content areas and skillful application of research-based strategies to provide access to content standards for scholars of all academic levels;

• demonstrate knowledge and use of a rich array of instructional approaches, resources, and technologies in the relevant content area(s);

• demonstrate skill in analyzing and using data for instructional decision-making; especially differentiated instruction for scholars of all academic levels;

jobs.title: Cybersecurity Information System Security Manager
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Air Defense team builds robots that find other robots and knock them out of the sky. At a time when air superiority can no longer be taken for granted, the Air Defense team provides mission critical capabilities to warfighters. From detection to tracking, identification, deterrence, and defeat, our family of networked sensors and effectors enables our customers to rapidly close the kill chain against a broad range of UAS threats. Working across product, engineering, business development, logistics, operations, and mission success, the Air Defense team develops, tests, deploys, and sustains the Anduril Air Defense Family of Systems in challenging operational environments worldwide.

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril's Air Defense division is seeking a Cybersecurity Information System Security Manager (ISSM) to own the cyber compliance posture of our command and control (C2) software systems. This role sits at the intersection of mission-critical software delivery and government cybersecurity accreditation — you will be responsible for building and maintaining the full cybersecurity authorization lifecycle, from policy development through artifact delivery, ensuring our systems meet the rigorous security standards required for Department of Defense deployment.
You will serve as the primary cybersecurity authority for your program, driving the end-to-end Enterprise Mission Assurance Support Service (eMASS) accreditation process, enforcing security standard operating procedures, managing Plans of Action and Milestones (POAMs), and ensuring continuous compliance across development and operational environments. This is not a checkbox role — you will work directly with engineers, program managers, and government stakeholders to embed security into the development lifecycle while keeping pace with rapid software delivery.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Lead the development, submission, and management of all government cybersecurity authorization artifacts within eMASS, including System Security Plans (SSPs), Security Assessment Reports (SARs), and supporting documentation required for Authority to Operate (ATO)

• Serve as the program Information System Security Manager (ISSM), maintaining continuous monitoring activities and ensuring compliance with Risk Management Framework (RMF) requirements

• Develop, implement, and enforce cybersecurity standard operating procedures across the program, ensuring engineering teams adhere to security policies throughout the software development lifecycle

• Pull, tailor, and validate Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs) applicable to program systems, coordinating remediation efforts with development teams

• Manage and execute application and infrastructure code scans, triaging findings and coordinating remediation with engineering

• Create, track, and manage Plans of Action and Milestones (POAMs), including risk assessments, mitigation strategies, and closure activities

• Advise program leadership on cybersecurity risk posture, emerging threats, and compliance status

• Interface directly with government cybersecurity stakeholders, Authorizing Officials (AOs), and Security Control Assessors (SCAs) throughout the accreditation lifecycle

• Collaborate with software engineers to integrate security controls into continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• United States citizenship with an active Secret or Top Secret security clearance

• Minimum 5 years of experience serving as an Information System Security Officer (ISSO) or in an equivalent cybersecurity compliance role

• Minimum 3 years of hands-on experience with eMASS, including artifact creation, submission, and package management

• Demonstrated experience delivering complete RMF authorization packages through to ATO

• Strong working knowledge of NIST Special Publication 800-53, NIST 800-37, and DoD cybersecurity policies (DoDI 8510.01)

• Experience pulling, applying, and validating STIG checklists across operating systems, applications, and network devices

• Experience with vulnerability scanning and code analysis tools (for example, Nessus, ACAS, SonarQube, Fortify, or equivalent)

• Proficiency in POAM creation, management, and closure processes

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Information Technology, or a related technical discipline

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Experience with networking, communications systems, or command and control architectures

• DoD 8570/8140 certification (for example, Security+, CISSP, CISM, CAP, or equivalent)

• Experience supporting software-intensive programs with agile or DevSecOps development methodologies

• Familiarity with container security, cloud security architectures, or zero-trust frameworks

• Prior experience supporting air defense, missile defense, or integrated battle command systems

• Experience working with cross-functional engineering teams in a fast-paced, iterative development environment

• Experience with red team, blue team, or penetration testing methodologies

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

• No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

• Please always verify communications: Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address. Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

• Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

• What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

jobs.title: Scientific Software Engineer – Algorithms
jobs.description:
About Pendar Technologies

Pendar Technologies develops advanced optical sensing and chemical identification technologies that bring sophisticated laboratory analysis into real-world environments. Our instruments combine innovative optical hardware, spectroscopy, imaging, and computational methods to enable rapid, reliable identification of chemical substances.

Our technologies support applications in public safety, chemical threat detection, and scientific analysis. We are a multidisciplinary team of scientists and engineers working at the intersection of physics, chemistry, optics, and software.

The Opportunity

We are seeking a Scientific Software Engineer – Algorithms to develop the algorithms and software that power our next generation of analytical instruments.

This is a hands-on, software-intensive position for someone with a strong scientific background, excellent programming skills, and a passion for solving complex technical problems. You will work closely with scientists and engineers to develop new analytical approaches and turn them into robust, high-performance software integrated into our products.

The position offers substantial technical ownership, opportunities to work across different scientific disciplines, and the satisfaction of seeing your solutions deployed in real-world applications.

What You'll Do

• Develop, implement, and optimize algorithms for processing and interpreting scientific data, including images and spectroscopic measurements.

• Design approaches to feature extraction, signal processing, pattern recognition, classification, and quantitative analysis.

• Apply mathematical modeling, statistical methods, and machine learning where appropriate to solve challenging measurement and analysis problems.

• Write high-quality, maintainable Python code, taking solutions from initial concept through validation, optimization, and product integration.

• Leverage AI-assisted development tools to accelerate algorithm design, software implementation, and problem-solving, while applying sound scientific and engineering judgment to evaluate and validate results.

• Collaborate with scientists, optical engineers, and software developers to understand instrument behavior, establish performance requirements, and develop effective solutions.

• Evaluate algorithm performance using experimental data, troubleshoot failures, and improve accuracy, speed, and robustness.

What We're Looking For

Required qualifications

• Ph.D. in a scientific, mathematical, or technical discipline. Recent graduates are particularly encouraged to apply.

• Excellent Python programming skills, demonstrated through substantial hands-on software development experience.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, with a foundation in mathematics and statistics.

• Ability to develop original algorithmic solutions, rather than relying exclusively on existing software packages or established techniques.

• Experience working with complex scientific or technical datasets.

• Ability to develop structured, maintainable, well-tested software and independently troubleshoot difficult technical problems.

Particularly valuable experience

• Scientific computing, numerical methods, or computational modeling.

• Image analysis, computer vision, or processing of large image datasets.

• Signal processing, spectroscopy, or inverse problems.

• Statistical modeling, optimization, machine learning, or feature extraction.

• Software development for scientific instrumentation or other technically demanding applications.

• Experience using AI-assisted coding and analytical tools to improve productivity in scientific or software development workflows.

• Collaborative software development practices, including version control, code review, and automated testing.

Prior experience in Raman spectroscopy or any specific application area is not required.

Who Will Thrive Here

We are looking for someone who is intellectually curious, driven, autonomous, and resourceful. Someone who enjoys understanding difficult problems, finding creative solutions, and taking ownership of their implementation.

The ideal candidate combines scientific rigor with excellent software development skills and the flexibility to work across different technical domains. You should be comfortable learning new concepts, challenging assumptions, and making progress even when the path forward is not immediately obvious.

We value demonstrated ability, initiative, and the capacity to learn and grow over expertise in any particular application area.

Why Join Pendar?

• Challenging technical problems. Apply scientific reasoning, mathematics, and computation to develop solutions for sophisticated optical and chemical sensing systems.

• Ownership and impact. Work on algorithms from concept through implementation and see your contributions become part of real products.

• Multidisciplinary environment. Collaborate with scientists and engineers across optics, spectroscopy, instrumentation, and software.

• Meaningful applications. Contribute to technologies used in chemical identification, public safety, and other demanding real-world environments.

• Opportunity to grow. Take on diverse technical challenges in a collaborative environment that values curiosity, initiative, and independent thinking.

Compensation and Location

This is a full-time position based in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

The anticipated base salary range is $100,000–$130,000 annually, depending on qualifications and relevant experience.

jobs.title: Editor, Agent Experience
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

STLabs is hiring someone to own how our agent comes across to the people it helps. The agent resolves IT and HR requests in Slack and email for employees who are often stuck or irritated; whether it feels competent, calm and helpful in those moments is the job. You own the agent's voice and the standard for a good interaction. Engineers build the models, prompts and evaluation tooling; you decide what they aim at and show them, with examples, when they miss.




WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Write and maintain the agent's voice and behavioral guidelines: how it explains, asks, admits uncertainty, declines, escalates and closes a loop.

 - Read real transcripts every week and turn what you find into precise, example-backed asks for engineering.

 - Decide handoff behavior: when the agent acts, asks, or stops and routes to a human.


REQUIREMENTS

 - An ear. You notice when something is technically correct but lands badly, and you can say why.

 - Unusually good plain-English writing for readers who are busy and not in a good mood. Most of the output is written guidance and rewrites.

 - You have held other people to a standard across a high volume of real interactions: ran a desk, edited a team, trained staff, or graded conversations against a rubric.

 - You can read thousands of transcripts, keep the patterns in your head, and turn a pile of cases into a rule that is specific and hard to game.

 - Comfortable with a product that changes weekly. Your guidelines ship Friday and we find out what breaks.

We are not hiring from the usual AI/ Tech pool. We welcome candidates from hospitality, patient experience, editorial, teaching, support quality, and help-desk leadership. A degree in literature, philosophy or the humanities from a top school is required; beyond that, we care about evidence you have held others to a standard, not further credentials. jobs.description:
As Mercury prepares to become a bank, our Third Party Risk Management (TPRM) program is in active development to meet bank-level regulatory expectations. As an early member of a growing TPRM team, you’ll help run the program day-to-day and contribute how it matures, bringing your own judgment and point of view to a function that is usually more rigidly defined, with room to be creative and make your mark.

As a Third Party Risk Manager, you’ll help protect Mercury, our customers, and the broader financial ecosystem from the risks that come with relying on third parties. Reporting to the Senior Manager, Third Party Risk Management, you’ll complete third-party risk assessments, support risk reporting, and provide second-line oversight.

As a Third Party Risk Manager, you will play a key part in helping protect Mercury, our customers, and the broader financial ecosystem from the risks associated with third parties. Reporting to the Senior Manager, Third Party Risk Management, you will conduct third party risk assessments, help build out related risk reporting, and carry out second line oversight activities to help reduce the impact of third-party risks.

This position focuses on enterprise-wide TPRM, rather than in-depth expertise in a specific domain like security or privacy. You will work closely with subject-matter experts across Compliance, Information Security, Privacy, and Procurement to make sure their requirements are reflected in the program, bringing a view across the full third-party lifecycle and the regulatory expectations that come with banking.*

Key Responsibilities:

• Assess and risk rate: Complete third-party risk assessments, risk rate third parties, and open and track issues through resolution.

• Second-line oversight: Review and challenge first-line due diligence and ongoing monitoring, including reporting, approvals and oversight of those activities. First-line owners remain accountable for managing the third-party relationship, including SLAs, business reviews, exit strategies and onboarding.

• Reporting and data: Support maintenance of third party risk reporting and metrics for management and governance forums, and help keep the underlying data accurate.

• Tooling and automation: Help implement tooling and automation to make processes more efficient

• Program uplift: Support and contribute to uplift efforts across the TPRM program, including updates to policies, due diligence, risk assessment processes, and risk management across the third party lifecycle

Required Qualifications:

• 4+ years of third party risk management experience, including 2+ years in a regulated financial services environment (bank, or fintech working with bank partners)

• Working knowledge of regulatory guidance on third party risk, including the Interagency Guidance on Third Party Relationships (and related FFIEC, OCC and FDIC expectations), and TPRM industry practices across the third party lifecycle (planning, due diligence, contracting, monitoring, termination)

jobs.title: Medical TA Lead
jobs.description:
MISSION

Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear. 

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.




ROLE PURPOSE

We are looking for an exceptional US Medical TA Lead to own medical recruitment on the East Coast and to lead the recruiters who deliver it. This is a high-impact leadership role for someone who has taken a clinical hiring plan from forecast to filled seats, built the team to do it, and can show the numbers.

Our clinical teams deliver the care that defines the member experience at Neko, so every hire shapes the quality of that care. We are post-Series C and opening clinics across the US. You will set the standard process, data and ways of working for US medical recruiting, while staying close enough to the work to run the funnel yourself when it matters.


WHAT YOU’LL DELIVER IN THE FIRST 6–12 MONTHS

• Deliver the East Coast medical hiring plan against clinic opening dates, with start dates holding. Forecast demand with Medical and Clinical Operations, sequence hiring to openings, and report hires against plan, time-to-fill and offer acceptance weekly from one source of truth.

• Raise funnel conversion, offer acceptance and speed. Diagnose bottlenecks by stage, act on the cause rather than adding volume, and stop work that does not move the numbers.

• Own and iterate the hiring process to deliver the highest quality clinical hires at pace.

• Build a team measured on outcomes. Set outcome-based goals, coach through regular performance conversations, add capacity in the order the plan requires, and develop a clear bench for the next step up.

• Have every new market ready before requisitions open. Build the talent picture early (talent supply, compensation, competitor activity) and bring proactive ideas on sourcing channels, events and realistic timelines to Medical leadership.

• Keep data and compliance clean so the pipeline can be trusted. Requisitions current, tools used consistently, and screening volumes tracked alongside conversion, with dashboards used to spot thin or stalled pipelines early. Licensing, credentialing, background checks and offer workflows completed with People, Legal and Rewards so every hire starts on the agreed date.

• Keep partners ahead of the plan. Run a regular rhythm of hiring updates with Medical leadership, Clinical Operations and Clinical Enablement: where the plan stands, current blockers, and opportunities to move faster.

• Lead team adoption of AI in sourcing, outreach and admin, with clear norms for validation, bias and data privacy, and a clear view of where AI must not make the decision.

• Leave a documented process and data standard that the wider US team can adopt without rebuilding, and represent Neko to clinicians and in professional networks, conferences and events.


MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

• 8+ years of recruitment experience, including 3+ years leading recruitment for clinical or healthcare roles in the US.

• Experience line-managing recruiters, with accountability for their performance, development and retention.

• A record of delivering high-volume or hard-to-fill US clinical hiring against a plan, with numbers to back it up (hires vs plan, time-to-fill, offer acceptance).

• Working knowledge of US clinical licensing and credentialing requirements across states.

• Strong judgment on trade-offs: speed, process consistency and quality measured against defined performance indicators, including saying no or re-scoping when the numbers call for it.

• Experience partnering with senior clinical and operational leaders and influencing decisions with data.

• A calm, solutions-first approach in fast-moving, ambiguous environments, ideally a scale-up.

• Experience entering or scaling new markets, including building local talent pipelines and proposing sourcing approaches and timelines ahead of need.

• Experience using dashboards and reports (Ashby or similar) to manage pipeline performance and to hold a team to data quality standards.

• Experience building or standardising a recruiting process across sites or teams.

• Fluent use of AI tools in sourcing, outreach, analysis and workflow, and the ability to teach others and set responsible-use standards.

• Experience managing an RPO (recruitment process outsourcing) partner, including performance against agreed service levels, is a plus.

We offer a dynamic work environment with a high degree of autonomy that fosters growth and development. If you are passionate about building a better healthcare system for everyone and you thrive in a fast-paced environment, we would love to hear from you.

jobs.title: Space Electronics Systems Engineer II
jobs.description:
SEAKR is seeking a Space Electronics Systems Engineer II to support the design, development, testing, and integration of electronic subsystems for our next‑generation products. You will work closely with hardware, firmware, mechanical, power, and software teams to deliver reliable, radiation‑tolerant electronics that meet project specifications.

Core Responsibilities

• Subsystem Design & Implementation – Assist in developing detailed designs for avionics, payload electronics, power‑distribution units, and environmental control systems based on high-level architecture. Produce derived specifications, block diagrams, and support test planning.
• Component Evaluation – Research and recommend commercial or radiation‑hardened components (COTS, rad‑hard) under the guidance of senior engineers to meet mission specifications.
• Hardware Prototyping – Participate in prototype build, assembly, and preparation for production-grade manufacturing.
• Test Execution & Data Analysis – Execute system‑level test plans (electrical, functional, EMI/EMC, vibration, thermal). Collect and analyze test data to support verification efforts and report findings.
• Systems Integration Support – Help maintain electronic interface control documents (ICDs, EID). Coordinate with hardware, power, software, and mechanical teams to resolve interface issues.
• Documentation – Assist in producing design specifications, test procedures, and operational manuals. Contribute to the living knowledge base for future teams.
• Communication – Ability to understand technical requirements, translate customer needs into engineering tasks, and communicate progress within the team.
• Team Collaboration – Work effectively within cross‑functional teams, participate in design reviews, and support peer engineers.

Required Qualifications

• Education – Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related discipline.
• Experience – 2–5 years of systems engineering experience, preferably in the space or defense industry.
• Technical Expertise – Solid knowledge of digital and analog electronics design (mixed‑signal, high‑speed). Familiarity with Requirements Management Environment (RME) tools. Basic understanding of radiation effects (TID, SEE) and mitigation techniques. Experience working with embedded microcontrollers/FPGA.
• Testing & Validation – Experience executing electrical, EMI/EMC, thermal vacuum, vibration, and functional test plans. Ability to interpret test data for design feedback.
• Soft Skills – Good analytical, problem‑solving, and communication abilities. Strong teamwork and adaptability.

Preferred Skills

• Familiarity with RF processing system architecture and testing.
• Knowledge of space‑qualified microprocessors or FPGA families.
• Understanding of system power calculations throughout a design cycle.
• Awareness of space‑qualifying standards: NASA SP‑3008, ECSS‑E‑ST‑20C, MIL‑STD‑1553, SpaceWire, etc.

Compensation: Base salary range is $90,000-130,000/year, depending on qualifications. SEAKR has very rich medical, dental and vision insurance plans, along with a generous 401(k) retirement plan. In addition to base salary, employees are eligible for a year-end bonus. SEAKR offers a variety of paid leave, such as vacation, sick, bereavement, and FMLA.

jobs.title: Community Outreach Specialist Seasonal Support
jobs.description:
Position Overview:

The Community Outreach Specialist, Seasonal Support is a part-time, seasonal position supporting student recruitment and enrollment efforts across KIPP NYC schools. This role plays an important part in connecting prospective families with KIPP NYC's joyful, academically excellent schools by building relationships within local communities, sharing information about our schools, and supporting families through the application process.

Reporting to the Director, Student Recruitment & Community Engagement, and transitioning to the Field Recruitment Manager once that position is filled, the Community Outreach Specialist serves as a trusted representative of KIPP NYC, engaging prospective families through neighborhood canvassing, door-to-door outreach, tabling at community locations, and participation in recruitment events. The Specialist is responsible for generating prospective family leads, encouraging families to apply, and accurately documenting outreach activities to support student enrollment goals.

This role requires an outgoing, relationship-driven individual who enjoys connecting with people, takes initiative, and is motivated by achieving measurable results. The ideal candidate is passionate about KIPP NYC's mission, understands the importance of building trust with families, and believes every child deserves access to a joyful, academically excellent education.

This is a part-time, seasonal, field-based position requiring approximately 15–20 hours per week. The role involves regular travel within assigned neighborhoods across the Bronx, Brooklyn, and/or Manhattan to conduct community outreach and support student recruitment activities.

Candidates must have flexibility to work weekday afternoons after 3:00 PM, evenings, and weekends based on recruitment events, community engagement opportunities, and organizational needs.

This position is seasonal and is expected to conclude at the end of August 2027, with the possibility of renewal in the fall based on organizational needs.

Duties and Responsibilities:

General responsibilities include (but are not limited to):

Community Outreach & Family Engagement

• Represent KIPP NYC in the communities we serve by conducting neighborhood canvassing, door-to-door outreach, tabling at high-traffic locations, and participating in community and recruitment events.
• Clearly and confidently communicate KIPP NYC's mission, educational approach, and school offerings through engaging, personalized conversations with prospective families.
• Highlight school programs and resources that align with families' interests and priorities, including academics, enrichment, after school programming, and other school offerings.
• Build authentic, trusting relationships with prospective families by serving as a welcoming, knowledgeable, and credible representative of KIPP NYC.
• Respond thoughtfully to family questions and concerns, follow up with interested families, and demonstrate persistence and professionalism when navigating challenging outreach conversations.

Student Recruitment & Enrollment Support

• Work toward established weekly lead generation and application goals, taking ownership of outreach results and contributing to KIPP NYC's student recruitment and enrollment priorities.
• Encourage interested families to take the next step in the enrollment process and provide hands-on assistance with starting applications whenever possible.
• Accurately collect and document prospective family information, including family names, contact details, and grade eligibility, using KIPP NYC's designated recruitment systems.
• Ensure prospective family leads are properly attributed, recorded, and shared with the appropriate Student Recruitment and Enrollment team members.
• Develop a strong understanding of KIPP NYC schools within assigned neighborhoods, including grade levels served, school offerings, enrollment eligibility, and application procedures.
• Support prospective families in navigating the application process and connect them with appropriate team members when additional assistance is needed.

Team Collaboration & Outreach Coordination

• Collaborate with an assigned outreach team, including a team lead and fellow Community Outreach Specialists, to implement recruitment strategies within designated neighborhood zones.
• Maintain clear and timely communication with Student Recruitment and Enrollment team members to ensure prospective family leads and applications are appropriately transferred, followed up on, and supported throughout the enrollment process.
• Participate in regular team check-ins and recruitment meetings to review progress toward goals, share community insights, and strengthen outreach strategies.
• Share feedback and observations from community interactions to help the Student Recruitment and Enrollment team better understand family needs and identify opportunities to improve recruitment efforts.
• Support additional student recruitment initiatives, community engagement activities, and special projects as assigned.

• High school diploma or equivalent required.
• At least one year of experience in a goal-oriented, customer-facing role preferred, such as community outreach, canvassing, retail sales, hospitality, fundraising, field organizing, or customer service.
• Spanish fluency highly preferred.
• Demonstrated ability to work toward measurable goals, take initiative, and remain accountable for results.
• Outgoing, approachable, and comfortable initiating conversations with new people while demonstrating resilience, confidence, and professionalism.
• Strong interpersonal, communication, and customer service skills with the ability to build positive relationships with families from diverse backgrounds.
• Ability to navigate sensitive or challenging conversations with families while demonstrating empathy, professionalism, and discretion when handling personal information.
• Comfortable using technology, including smartphones, digital forms, and recruitment tracking systems, with the ability to quickly learn new tools and platforms.
• Strong attention to detail and commitment to maintaining accurate, complete, and timely prospective family records.
• Ability to work collaboratively within a team while independently managing assigned outreach activities and responsibilities.
• Ability to stand or walk for two to three hours at a time and carry recruitment materials weighing approximately 10–20 pounds as needed.
• Ability to work within assigned neighborhoods across the Bronx, Brooklyn, and/or Manhattan.
• Flexibility to work weekday afternoons after 3:00 PM, evenings, and weekends based on recruitment and community engagement needs.
• KIPP NYC parents, alumni, and individuals with strong connections to the communities we serve are especially encouraged to apply.
• Deep commitment to KIPP NYC's mission and belief that all students deserve access to joyful, academically excellent schools and strong partnerships between schools, families, and communities.
• Demonstrates KIPP NYC's core values of zest, grit, hope, social intelligence, gratitude, and a sense of humor.

Compensation & Benefits:

KIPP NYC offers a competitive hourly rate of $23-$25 per hour for this role. This rate is standardized based on the position's level and responsibilities to ensure equitable compensation across employees in similar roles.

This description is intended to describe the type of work being performed by a person assigned to this position. It is not an exhaustive list of all duties and responsibilities required by the employee.

This is a full-time, in-person role based in New York City and will require travel to our schools. If you are not in a school-based position, the cadence and frequency of travel to schools is determined by your leadership team. If you relocate outside of a commutable distance or out of the state of NY, your employment will be subject to review, which may include separation from KIPP NYC. It is important that you notify HR if you move or have plans to relocate.

You’ll lead a high-performing, cross-functional squad of Full Stack Application Engineers, Data Engineers, and QA Engineers to build, scale, and evolve the systems that power our customer-facing reporting and analytics features. This role bridges hands-on technical work, architectural leadership, and people development — ideal for someone who thrives at the intersection of technology, strategy, and team impact.

This role is a unique opportunity to guide the transformation of our embedded analytics into a new era of AI enabled business intelligence, providing high performing, trustworthy, and actionable reporting and analytics to our customers at a higher scale and speed than has been possible before.

What You’ll Do

• Lead, mentor, and grow a cross-functional engineering and data team, fostering a culture of technical excellence, ownership, and collaboration.

• Own end-to-end delivery of your squad's product area — from early involvement in product discovery and design validation through implementation, testing, deployment, and post-ship monitoring. You will own the stack, working collaboratively with systems architects to design the most effective data and analytics platform.

• Write code, review code, and architect solutions. You understand the codebase deeply enough to make informed tradeoffs and unblock your team.

• Partner with the Product team as a collaborative equal — validating technical feasibility early, pushing back when scope is unrealistic, and advocating for quality and stability as first-class priorities alongside new features.

• Balance feature work against bugs, tech debt, performance, and reliability. Work collaboratively with Product leadership to allocate engineering time towards the stability and high performance needs of our customers.

• Drive architectural decision-making, balancing innovation, scalability, and delivery speed.

• Promote engineering best practices, including clean architecture, testing, monitoring, and performance optimization.

• Help the team break work down, manage flow, and ensure design, engineering, and QA operate in parallel rather than in sequential phases.

• Champion high-quality code through design reviews, code reviews, and robust CI/CD pipelines (Docker, GitHub Actions, Kubernetes). Own the definition of "done" — tested, stable, monitored, and maintainable.

• Coach engineers on career growth, system design, and effective collaboration. Because you work alongside your team daily, feedback is immediate, specific, and grounded in real work.

• Drive AI and agentic coding tool adoption within your squad — leading by example, partnering with the Platform team on standards and guardrails, and helping your team understand how to use AI effectively while avoiding common pitfalls.

• Build an inclusive and motivated team culture centered on transparency, ownership, and impact.

• Collaborate with recruiting to attract and retain top engineering talent.

• Establish performance goals, track key metrics, and ensure operational excellence in delivery.

What We’re Looking For

• 5+ years of professional experience in software development and/or data engineering, with at least 2 years in a technical leadership or management capacity.

• Deep understanding of SQL, data modeling, and analytics/reporting

• Experience with cloud platforms and container orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes).

• Proven success leading technical teams and mentoring engineers of varied seniority levels.

• Experience with or strong enthusiasm for AI-assisted development tools and workflows.

• Excellent communication and collaboration skills — able to bridge the gap between technical and non-technical audiences.

• Strategic thinker who can connect engineering priorities to product and business outcomes.

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent experience

We know many women do not apply for a job if they don't perfectly fit the description. We want you to apply anyway.

Bonus Points If You Have

• Deep understanding of microservice architecture, RESTful API design, distributed systems, and modern frontend frameworks.

• Strong hands-on proficiency in one or more of our core technologies (Python, Java, Kotlin, TypeScript/React), with the ability and willingness to learn and work across the stack.

Why You Want to Work Here

🌴 Flexible Paid Time Off - you’re actually encouraged to use, plus 10 company holidays!

❤️‍🩹 Health Benefits - including Medical, Dental, and Vision and an HSA Match.

💰 401(k) - we match 100% up to 3% of your contribution. Eligibility is immediate with 100% vesting.

🧠 Mental Health -  all employees have access to Impact Suite & to our Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

👶 Paid New Parent Leave & Birthing Parent Leave - so you’re able to care for your little ones.

➕ Supplemental Benefits - including 100% company paid Basic Life & AD&D insurance and long & short-term disability coverage.

🌟 Nectar - our peer-to-peer recognition program to help our employees recognize the amazing work being done by other Canopians!

🥳 Company Events - including monthly company-wide meetings, summer parties, and more.

💡 ERG Committees - to plan initiatives around continuing education, community outreach, recruiting, onboarding, and more.

☕ Fully-stocked kitchen - Keto? Vegan? Flexitarian? Mandalorian? We’ve got you covered.

Our Values

We approach our work every day with a few things in mind:

🔑 Own - We own this place! We focus on outcomes, holding ourselves & each other accountable.

🏆 Win - We win by delighting our customers with the very best products and services.

👍 Do Good - We work hard to be good people!

💡 Embrace Curiosity & Candor - We approach everything with curiosity & we understand that candor is kindness and give the gift of feedback.

Act Startup Fast - We know the best way to become a world-class company is to always act like a tiny startup: fast, hungry, intense, and scrappy. But especially fast.

To learn more about us & our values, click here.

jobs.title: Staff Operations Engineer
jobs.description:
Stratolaunch accelerates the development of next-generation aerospace and defense technologies through reusable hypersonic flight testing. Our autonomous, air-launched Talon-A vehicles provide access to operationally realistic flight environments at speeds exceeding Mach 5, delivering critical data that helps customers validate system performance and advance technologies toward deployment. Our team brings together expertise in engineering, manufacturing, and flight operations to solve complex challenges and advance capabilities essential to national security.

As an Operations Engineer, you will accept a critical role in achieving new milestones in aviation and enable development of high-speed test vehicles to be air-launched from Stratolaunch Carrier Aircraft. You will provide effective leadership as the focal point for high-speed vehicle operations planning and execution, to include the potential to act as the liaison to the Test Director for vehicle and mission readiness. You should have experience in test vehicle configuration control, test planning and resourcing, and conducting disciplined, effective developmental flight test operations, or similar experience in a technically demanding high pace environment.

As a key member of the Stratolaunch team, you will have an essential role in meeting our ambitious company objectives. You must establish and maintain effective relationships with colleagues on a small, agile design-to-flight team. You will be challenged with bringing unique and complex aircraft from initial airworthiness to operational use at a company that believes in giving our team members the authority and responsibility to succeed.

ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Assist in the implementation of test strategy and objectives, test plans, test procedures, and mission cards for ground and flight testing for high-speed test vehicles

• Coordinate closely with vehicle engineering team to identify system safety and operational concerns

• Interface with multiple engineers, vehicle crew chiefs and ground support personnel to ensure operational priorities are understood and executed

• Provide organization and preparation in support of Test & Flight Readiness Reviews

• Identify test hazards and develop / implement real time mitigation actions

• Support Talon vehicle maintenance & test teams to fulfil operational necessities

• Control on-vehicle priorities and schedules to meet final assembly, test, and flight readiness requirements

• Work closely with the respective vehicle Crew Chiefs to ensure proper vehicle configuration and maintenance is complete to support mission priorities

• Assist with functional system test planning and execution in areas such as avionics, flight control actuation, recovery systems, propulsion integration and propulsion system demonstration activities

• Work with Carrier Aircraft operations teams to ensure successful vehicle mating and integrated systems testing is accomplished

• Respond to emergency situations to ensure the safety of personnel and equipment while assisting as point of contact for first responders; act as mission manager for operations in case of an incident

• Support execution of integrated vehicle ground test activities

• Contribute to high-speed vehicle test data gathering and ensure test results are appropriately reviewed, documented, and controlled

• Provide inputs to refine and mature the high-speed vehicle Concept of Operations including ground and flight operational procedures, timelines, checklists, and emergency response actions, starting from vehicle post manufacture initial testing through recovery of vehicles and return to flight ready state

• Participate in payload customer meetings, including meetings for payload integration/de-integration planning, integrated vehicle testing and data product delivery

• Facilitate payload hardware and software integration and integrated test on high-speed test vehicles

• Assist in evaluation of risks and risk mitigation plans to determine if the risks are appropriate and risk mitigations are adequate

• Travel, as needed, to support design, mission planning, mission execution, and other tasks

• Demonstrate integrity, accountability, and initiative to fulfill commitments

• Develop concept of operations for all launch and recovery locations. This includes coordination among many different teams and external parties

QUALIFICATIONS:

• To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions:

REQUIRED:

• Proven technical aerospace leadership experience, including supervision and training in a technical operations environment with a focus on execution readiness

• Aptitude to analyze and prioritize tasks on their own initiative, and drive projects to completion, to fit within overall business goals

• Ability to lead a large team, make decisions, communicate requirements, and quickly adapt to changing priorities/real world conditions

• Previous experience with new, experimental, or modified aircraft, launch vehicles or spacecraft, technical and safety review boards, and configuration control methods

• Experience with engineering, scheduling, and test data analysis tools

• Knowledge of risk management or safety management systems

• Have excellent written and verbal communication skills

• Be able to work irregular hours and workdays, and travel periodically

• US Citizenship / Ability to obtain and maintain a secret security clearance

• Critical thinking skills, and problem-solving attitude a must

PREFERRED:

• Bachelor’s degree in engineering, or similar technical foundation

• Professional Flight Test Course

• Knowledge of launch vehicle or aircraft requirements verification and development of requirements

• Understanding of launch vehicle, air-launch, or high-speed flight programs

• Prior involvement with government flight test organizations, ranges, and procedures

• Experience operating in a classified work environment or with classified hardware

• Previous expeditor or production superintendent familiarity

• Existing TS/SCI Clearance

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE:

• Staff Level ($130,800-$150,000): Bachelor’s degree (B.S.) from accredited institution and 8+ years of engineering experience, OR equivalent combination of education and experience

Special remarks regarding work environment:

• This position is located in Mojave, CA

• Travel, as needed, to support the department, travel estimated to be <20%

• #LI-Onsite

Base salary and leveling are established on a case-by-case basis. We consider several factors to ensure a competitive offer, including your location, educational background, and a comprehensive assessment of the skills and experience demonstrated during your interviews.

Benefits and our location(s):

• Healthcare (medical, dental, vision, prescription drugs)

• Paid Maternity and Parental Leave

• 50% company match per contributed dollar into 401(k) savings plan, up to $11,500

• Tuition reimbursement

This position may involve the operation of company vehicles as part of assigned duties.

Mojave Air & Spaceport is located just outside of Lancaster/Palmdale and is only 95 miles north of Los Angeles.  The area offers both affordability and central access to a variety of California's best attractions and landmarks.

Not much for the outdoors and prefer the city life? You’re within a half day’s drive or less of Los Angeles, San Diego, Las Vegas, and San Francisco where you can find a variety of live entertainment, museums, tours, and historical sight-seeing. Theme parks are in abundance, with Six Flags Magic Mountain, Disneyland, and Knotts Berry Farm ready to meet the needs of rollercoaster thrill seekers.

Food and drink fanatics are in a haven of delectable choices. Wine aficionados will also find easy access to some of the state’s best vino in Paso Robles, Santa Ynez, and even more locally in Tehachapi and Agua Dulce. Beer fanatics will find some of the best West Coast IPAs at Bravery and Lucky Luke’s in Lancaster. Any food option you crave is covered, and we always recommend the authentic and fresh Mexican food that you won’t find anywhere else in the United States.

• Standards: Monitors and interprets industry/regulatory trends and regulatory guidance. Sets both short and long term vision for programming standards. Ensures programming standards work seamless with related function’s standards.

jobs.title: Engineering Manager, Device Platforms
jobs.description:
ABOUT NIANTIC SPATIAL

AI has learned from almost everything online, but it still struggles with the physical world, where 99.5% of economic activity happens. It doesn’t know where things are, how spaces fit together, or what changes over time.

That’s one of the biggest unsolved problems in AI, and it’s the one we’re solving at Niantic Spatial. We build spatial AI models and services so people and machines can reason, learn and act safely in the physical world. We turn camera imagery, video, sensor data and archives into accurate, AI-readable representations of real places that robots can train in and machines can use to know exactly where they are.

In physical AI, mistakes have real consequences. That’s why we build AI grounded in measured reality, not guesswork, so the people and machines relying on it can trust it to get things right.

Our team built some of the world’s most widely used maps. Now we’re building something bigger: a living, measured record of the real world that machines can query, learn from and use to understand how places change over time. If you want to help AI understand the world we actually live in, come build with us.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a hands-on engineering leader to own our device-native technology organization. You will be responsible for leading both the Device SDK and Mobile Engineering teams, overseeing the development of our native SDKs, spatial computing runtimes, and flagship mobile applications.

This is a hybrid leadership role that combines people management, technical leadership, architecture, and hands-on engineering. You must be equally comfortable mentoring engineers, defining technical strategy, reviewing architecture, and contributing production code.  You will bring deep experience with the latest AI technologies, work streams, and best practices, and demonstrate forward thinking about integrating AI into the SDLC.

Reporting to the Head of Product and Platform Engineering, you will serve as a key technical partner in shaping the future of Niantic Spatial’s device-native ecosystem. You will play a key role in defining technical direction, execution strategy, and platform investments across mobile, XR, robotics, and emerging edge-computing environments.




TEAMS YOU’LL LEAD

Platform SDK - Builds and operates the native technology stack that brings Niantic Spatial’s capabilities to devices, including:

 - Native runtime architecture and SDK development

 - Computer vision and spatial computing integrations

 - Sensor fusion and device-side processing

 - Platform abstraction and cross-platform architecture

 - Hardware acceleration and performance optimization

 - Native platform integrations for mobile, XR, robotics, and edge devices

 - Build systems, release automation, and test infrastructure

Mobile Applications - Builds flagship iOS and Android applications that showcase the full potential of Niantic Spatial’s technology, including:

 - Customer-facing mobile products and sample applications

 - Platform capability validation and feedback

 - Best-practice SDK implementations

 - Mobile application architecture

 - User experience and performance optimization

 - Application release and lifecycle management




WHAT YOU’LL DO


TECHNICAL LEADERSHIP

 - Define and drive the technical vision for Niantic Spatial’s device-native ecosystem.

 - Define cutting edge AI-native development flows and guide the team to embrace best practices for agentic development

 - Establish architecture, engineering standards, and development practices across both teams.

 - Guide platform investments that improve developer experience, portability, performance, and scalability.

 - Partner closely with Research, Platform, and Product leadership to translate emerging capabilities into production-ready products and SDKs.

 - Participate directly in architecture reviews, technical design discussions, and critical implementation efforts.

 - Work with Platform to align architecture patterns to ensure a cohesive product ecosystem across all surface areas

 - Balance long-term platform investments with near-term product commitments.

 - Ensure predictable delivery, high quality, and operational excellence across all device-native products and platforms.


HANDS-ON ENGINEERING

 - Contribute production code on a regular basis.

 - Review code, mentor engineers, and actively participate in technical problem solving.

 - Support implementation of complex features spanning mobile applications, SDKs, native runtimes, and platform integrations.

 - Assist teams with debugging, performance analysis, and system optimization.

 - Maintain familiarity with day-to-day development workflows and remain actively engaged in execution.


PEOPLE LEADERSHIP

 - Directly manage the leads and engineers within the Device SDK and Mobile Engineering teams.

 - Recruit, mentor, and retain high-performing engineers.

 - Support career growth, performance management, and technical development across both teams.

 - Foster a culture of engineering excellence, ownership, collaboration, and continuous improvement.




WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - 10+ years of software engineering experience, including significant experience building and shipping native applications or SDKs.

 - 5+ years of engineering leadership experience managing teams and technical leads.

 - Expert-level proficiency in native software development for iOS (Swift) and Android (Kotlin).

 - Strong understanding of software architecture, performance optimization, and cross-platform development.

 - Experience leading engineers through complex technical initiatives while remaining hands-on.

 - Excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration skills.

 - Eligibility to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government security clearance; U.S. citizenship is required due to security clearance eligibility requirements.

 - Great at building and maintaining customer relationships, with occasional travel to client locations




NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience with in-app telemetry capture, analytics, and building business intelligence data streams that enable informed cross-functional decision making.

 - Experience supporting government or defense customers, including familiarity with FedRAMP, GovCloud, secure deployment environments, compliance documentation, and the operational expectations of regulated customer engagements.




COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

The expected salary range for this role is $238,500 to $310,000 per year. Compensation also includes an annual bonus, equity, and a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k), and more.




LOCATION & WORK MODEL

This role is based at our San Francisco, CA headquarters, with four days per week in office. There might be occasional travel to customer sites, partner organizations, and engineering off-sites.




INCLUSIVE APPLICATION

We know the strongest candidates don’t always tick every box. If you’re excited about this role and believe you could do it well, we encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn’t match every qualification listed — you may be exactly who we’re looking for.




EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

Individuals seeking employment at Niantic Spatial are considered without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, creed, age, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding or related medical conditions), marital status, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, military or veteran status, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, or any other protected category under applicable laws. CANDIDATE PRIVACY

jobs.title: Senior Director, Business Development
jobs.description:
The Senior Director of Business Development is a multifaceted leadership role responsible for maintaining industry awareness, generating leads, managing customer relationships, obtaining requests for proposals, and leading the Business Development team. The ideal candidate will possess a robust network of professional connections within the space industry.

This individual will collaborate with executives to develop and execute SEAKR’s business development strategy through the pursuit of high-win-probability opportunities. The Director is also responsible for identifying new business opportunities and developing capture strategies to support executive management bid/no-bid decisions. To strategically position the company for future business opportunities, the Director is expected to provide clear input regarding future product offering needs as part of the IRAD planning and budgeting process.

The ideal candidate will demonstrate expertise in sales, negotiations, finance, and growth strategies while embodying an entrepreneurial mindset. This is a full-time exempt position that will serve as a key representative and “face of the company” within the industry. The Director is expected to operate with a high degree of autonomy and sound judgment while maintaining strong alignment with executive leadership, effectively leading the Business Development team, adhering to company policies and processes, and delivering measurable business results.

Essential Duties/Responsibilities

Strategic Planning: Develop and execute business development strategies to drive growth and achieve company objectives. Collaborate with executives to develop, articulate, and execute a business development strategy with short-, mid-, and long-term goals by providing input from industry, market, and competitive analysis, customer needs assessments, customer feedback, product definition feedback, and future mission requirements.

Sales and Revenue Growth: Drive sales initiatives and achieve revenue targets through effective business development strategies. Coordinate with executives to define and execute strategies to grow product segment market share and profitability through market opportunity evaluation and segmentation, value proposition development, product positioning, pricing strategy, branding and channel strategy, and communications strategy development.

Client Relationships: Establish and maintain strong relationships with key clients, including government agencies, defense contractors, and commercial aerospace companies. Establish and nurture customer relationships to understand current and future needs and promote alignment of the company’s current and future capabilities to meet those needs.

Team Leadership: Lead, coach, and develop members of the Business Development team to build a high-performing and accountable organization. Establish clear priorities, expectations, and ownership across the team; provide regular feedback and coaching; monitor performance and workload; and ensure team members have the direction, resources, and support necessary to successfully execute their responsibilities. Maintain an appropriate level of engagement and presence with the team to support collaboration, development, and effective execution of business development priorities.

Cross-functional Collaboration: Work closely with the leadership team, engineering, business capture, and product development teams to align business development efforts with company goals. Align with the capture team to define technical, strategic, and business insight for RFI, ROM, whitepaper, and proposal responses.

Market Analysis: Identify and analyze market trends, customer needs, and the competitive landscape to uncover new business opportunities. Supervise marketing execution, including content for SEAKR’s website, product and marketing literature, trade show presence, trade journal articles, white papers, press releases, presentations, and datasheets. Represent the company at appropriate industry events, conferences, trade shows, and customer engagements to promote products and services.

Business Development Execution and Delegation: Establish clear ownership and accountability for business development activities across the team. Effectively delegate customer engagements, opportunity development, and other business development responsibilities to ensure appropriate coverage, develop team capabilities, and maximize organizational effectiveness. Maintain visibility into team activities, customer engagements, pipeline development, and key opportunities to ensure alignment with company priorities.

Policy and Expense Management: Demonstrate consistent compliance with company policies, procedures, and internal controls, including all Travel and Expense requirements. Utilize the company’s designated travel and expense management system (Concur) for business travel booking and expense reporting, as required by company policy, and ensure expenses are accurately documented and submitted in a timely manner. As a people leader, reinforce these expectations with members of the Business Development team and model appropriate stewardship of company resources.

Travel: Must be available to travel for business approximately 30%–50% of the time based on customer, program, and business needs. Travel should be purposeful and aligned with business development priorities, customer engagement requirements, and company objectives, while maintaining appropriate availability and presence to effectively lead and support the Business Development team. The Director is expected to exercise sound judgment in determining when in-person travel is necessary and when business objectives can be effectively accomplished through other means.

Supervisory Duties

• Provide direct leadership and oversight of members of the Business Development team.
• Establish individual and team priorities, goals, and performance expectations aligned with company objectives.
• Provide ongoing coaching, feedback, performance management, and professional development to team members.
• Effectively delegate responsibilities and customer engagements to develop team capabilities, ensure appropriate coverage, and maximize organizational effectiveness.
• Monitor team performance, workload, customer engagement, and execution against business development priorities.
• Assess organizational capabilities and resource needs and support the continued development and growth of the Business Development function.
• Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, communication, and compliance with company policies and processes.

Education or Formal Training

• The ideal candidate will have a technical background and a Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, with an emphasis in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, or an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience.
• A Master’s degree in Engineering Management or Program Management, or an MBA, is preferred.

Experience

• At least 15 years of technical business development experience, with demonstrated experience in the aerospace and/or space markets preferred.
• Demonstrated experience developing and executing business development and growth strategies within a technical environment.
• Proven experience developing and maintaining relationships with government, defense, aerospace, and/or commercial space customers.
• Demonstrated leadership experience, including managing, coaching, developing, and holding team members accountable for performance and results.
• Experience managing multiple business development opportunities, customer engagements, and capture activities simultaneously.

Security Clearance The candidate will either possess a TS/SCI with polygraph clearance or be capable of obtaining the required clearance.

Skills  Demonstrate strong analytical, negotiation, leadership, and communication skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively under pressure.

Compensation: Base salary range is $225,000-275,000, depending on qualifications. SEAKR has very rich medical, dental and vision insurance plans, along with a generous 401(k) retirement plan. In addition to base salary, employees are eligible for a year-end bonus. SEAKR offers a variety of paid leave, such as vacation, sick, bereavement, and FMLA.

SEAKR is an Equal Opportunity Employer - All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

US Citizenship Required

Applications will be accepted until 11/20/26.

Abnormal has constantly been named as one of the top cybersecurity startups and our behavioral AI system has helped us win various cybersecurity accolades resulting in being trusted to protect more than 15% of the Fortune 500 (and ever growing).

Other projects support model development and evaluation, mostly driven by automated agentic loops.

You will collaborate closely with ML Engineers, Data Scientists, and fellow Software Engineers to turn new approaches into reliable production systems and in turn help us catch more attacks and improve security investigations while limiting false positives and cost. Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.



We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.



We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.



If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.



About the Role:

Crusoe is on a mission to align the future of computing with the future of the climate. As our Staff Enterprise Technology Administrator, People Tech, you will be a senior technology owner for Crusoe’s People Technology platforms, spanning Workday, ADP Workforce Now, and adjacent systems. You’ll lead hands-on platform administration, integration, and delivery work, serve as the primary escalation point for platform incidents, and help shape the multi-year roadmap for the domain, partnering with the Architect track on architecture decisions that span multiple enterprise domains. With Workday going live in early 2027, you’ll join at a pivotal moment: stabilizing our Phase 1 launch, driving Phase 2, and building the operational foundation our People Technology platform will run on for years to come.



This is a full-time, in-person position based in our San Francisco or Sunnyvale, CA office. The ideal candidate brings deep, hands-on Workday configuration and administration experience, with a track record of both net-new implementations and sustained post-go-live support at scale. You are a decisive problem solver and effective communicator who excels at translating business needs into elegant system configurations, navigating ambiguity, and building trusted partnerships across People Operations, Recruiting, and Total Rewards.



What You'll Be Working On:

 - Workday Go-Live & Hypercare: Support Phase 1 go-live readiness, defect triage, and hypercare, driving stabilization and a seamless transition from legacy tools.

 - Phase 2 Delivery: Lead scoping, business process design, and hands-on configuration for Phase 2 modules, and contribute to the multi-year Workday roadmap.

 - ADP Workforce Now Integration: Support the delivery and ongoing monitoring of the Workday–ADP integration, including payroll data flows, output files, reconciliation workflows, and parallel run testing.

 - Support Model & Governance: Build Crusoe’s People Tech operational support model, including request intake workflows, tiering pathways, and configuration change control processes.

 - Security & System Configuration: Own hands-on configuration of Workday HCM and specialized modules, including domain security, business process frameworks, role-based access control, and segregation of duties (SOD).

 - People Team Partnership: Serve as the primary technical partner to People Operations, Recruiting Ops, Total Rewards, and Payroll, translating business goals into automated, maintainable system solutions.

 - Reporting, Analytics & Data Quality: Build and maintain custom reports, dashboards, calculated fields, and Prism Analytics models that deliver workforce insights, headcount tracking, and compliance reporting.

 - Incident Leadership: Serve as the primary escalation point for People Tech platform incidents, driving root-cause analysis, cross-system troubleshooting, and remediation.

 - Vendor & Ecosystem Management: Manage technical relationships with Workday and third-party providers, including support escalations, roadmap updates, and semi-annual release adoption.

 - Team Development & Mentorship: Mentor P2 and P3 administrators, model technical execution standards, and help develop the next generation of platform practitioners.



What You'll Bring to the Team:

 - Deep Workday Expertise: 8+ years of enterprise systems experience, including at least 4 years of deep, hands-on Workday configuration and implementation.

 - Implementation & Support Track Record: Experience delivering net-new Workday implementations from discovery through cutover, plus 2+ years of sustained post-launch administration.

 - Workday Configuration Proficiency: Advanced hands-on skills across Workday HCM Core, calculated fields, business process frameworks, Enterprise Interface Builder (EIB), and custom report writing.

 - Payroll & Third-Party Integration Knowledge: Working knowledge of enterprise payroll integrations (ideally ADP Workforce Now) and third-party benefits and data exchange.

 - Scale & Complexity: Experience implementing or supporting Workday at high-growth, mid-to-large-scale organizations.

 - Ownership & Autonomy: Ability to own a technology domain end to end, shaping roadmaps, driving complex projects forward, and making sound decisions without complete information.

 - Strong Communication & Stakeholder Management: Excellent verbal and written communication, with the ability to influence cross-functional and VP-level leaders and explain technical constraints in business terms.

 - Required Foundational Education: High school diploma, G.E.D., or equivalent.



Bonus Points

 - Bachelor’s or advanced degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Human Resources, or a related field.

 - Active Workday Pro certifications in one or more functional tracks (HCM, Benefits, Compensation, Reporting, or Payroll).

 - Experience with Workday Studio, PICOF, or PECI integration frameworks.

 - Prior background in enterprise systems consulting, combined with in-house administrative ownership.

 - Working familiarity with adjacent people platforms such as Greenhouse, Lattice, or similar.

 - Experience designing workflows and audit controls under SOX-compliant governance frameworks.

 - Experience mentoring or developing other Workday administrators or analysts.



Benefits:

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $160,000-$190,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.
